## Summary
- FollowModeController fuses IR fleet presence (desk/room/overhead Pi reports) with camera classification metadata (task #135) to pick a hero camera that follows the operator through the room without being mechanical
- Creative bias: ambient_priority base + operator_visible bonus + location ontology match + 30s repetition penalty + demonstrate-at-desk overhead boost ("show the work" shot)
- Publishes ``/dev/shm/hapax-compositor/follow-mode-recommendation.json`` at ~2 Hz from the state-reader loop
- Hero-override consumer in ``state.py`` falls back to the follow-mode recommendation when no manual override; manual override always wins
- ``HAPAX_FOLLOW_MODE_ACTIVE`` feature flag (OFF by default). When off, the recommendation is still computed + written but marked inactive so ``read_follow_mode_recommendation`` returns None and the hero-override consumer does not fall back to it
- ``hapax_follow_mode_cuts_total{from_role,to_role}`` Counter bumped whenever follow-mode drives a hero cut

author: okabe-junya
body:
## What

Print an info message to stderr when `gcloudctx auto` finds no `.gcloudctx` file.

## Why

Previously, running `gcloudctx auto` in a directory without a `.gcloudctx` file silently succeeded, which could mask user errors (e.g., forgetting to run `gcloudctx use`). The message is printed to stderr so that shell cd hooks using `2>/dev/null` remain silent, while manual invocations provide feedback.

Implemented Vercel Web Analytics for the MiniMax API Proxy project

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Web Analytics for this static HTML website following the latest official Vercel documentation.

## Changes Made

### 1. Package Installation
- Installed `@vercel/analytics` version 2.0.1 via npm
- Added to package.json dependencies
- Generated package-lock.json for dependency consistency

### 2. Analytics Script Integration
Added the Vercel Analytics script tag to all three HTML pages in the public directory:

- **public/index.html** - Main landing page
- **public/chat.html** - MiniMax chat interface
- **public/config-guide.html** - AI tools configuration guide

Each file now includes:
```html
<script defer src="https://cdn.vercel-insights.com/v1/script.js"></script>
```

The script tag was added in the `<head>` section, right after the title tag and before the styles, following best practices.

## Implementation Details

### Why This Approach?
This project is a Vercel-hosted static site with HTML files (not a Next.js React application), so I used the script injection method recommended in the official Vercel documentation for vanilla HTML projects.

### Script Placement
The analytics script uses the `defer` attribute, which means:
- The script downloads in parallel with HTML parsing
- Executes after the document has been parsed
- Doesn't block page rendering
- Optimal for performance

### What Gets Tracked?
Vercel Web Analytics will now automatically track:
- Page views across all three HTML pages
- Visitor metrics (unique visitors, page views)
- Geographic data
- Browser and device information
- Performance metrics (Web Vitals)

## Files Modified
1. `package.json` - Added @vercel/analytics dependency
2. `package-lock.json` - Created with dependency lock information
3. `public/index.html` - Added analytics script
4. `public/chat.html` - Added analytics script
5. `public/config-guide.html` - Added analytics script

## Next Steps
After deployment to Vercel:
1. Analytics will be automatically enabled
2. Visit your Vercel project dashboard → Analytics tab to view insights
3. Data will start appearing within a few hours of deployment

## Documentation Reference
Implementation based on official Vercel documentation:
- https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/quickstart
- https://vercel.com/docs/analytics/package

The script-based approach is specifically designed for static HTML sites and requires no build process or additional configuration.

body:
The `/api/chat` endpoint was missing validation for individual elements within the `conversation` history array. This could allow an attacker to send malformed or unexpected data structures in the conversation history, potentially causing issues when the data is processed or forwarded to the external AI API.

This fix adds `express-validator` rules to:
1. Ensure `conversation.*.role` is a string and one of the allowed roles: 'system', 'user', 'assistant'.
2. Ensure `conversation.*.content` is a non-empty string.

These changes ensure the integrity of the conversation history before it is used to build the final AI request payload.

author: aetherlogosprime-architect
body:
## Summary

Followup to #141. After actually reading the Routines docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/routines), the morning's scaffolding was built on a wrong mental model — fixed here.

**What Routines actually is:** a saved Claude Code session that runs in Anthropic's cloud against a fresh clone of the repo. Not scheduled invocation of the local CLI. The cloud session has **no access to the local ledger**; findings propagate back only via git (PRs) or connectors.

**What kept:** the scaffolding's core (whitelist, corrigibility pass-through, subprocess wrap, findings capture) is still the right shape — both for cloud Routines invoking `divineos scheduled run <cmd>`, and for local cron on a hypothetical persistent host. Event persistence and briefing-surface mechanisms only fire usefully in the local-cron case; docstrings now say so honestly.

**What added:** `docs/routines/` with:
- `README.md` — how Routines works, how DivineOS fits, registration via `/schedule` or web UI
- `daily-anti-slop.md` — daily enforcer-verification, opens a PR on failure
- `weekly-progress-digest.md` — weekly git-level digest (flagged that the ledger-aware version waits on persistence)
- `on-pr-integrity-check.md` — GitHub-triggered anti-slop + verify + tests, PR comment only

**What changed:** docstrings in `scheduled_run.py` and `scheduled_commands.py` rewritten to state the persistence caveat explicitly. README architecture-tree line updated.

## Why

Better to correct the story than to ship code that claims things that aren't true. The scaffolding still pays for itself, but the docstring framing was based on guessing how Routines worked instead of reading the docs. This PR is the honest version.

## Test plan

- [x] 16 scheduled-run tests still pass
- [x] Precommit green (format, lint, mypy, doc drift, broad exceptions, vulture)
- [x] No code changes in this PR — only docstrings + new markdown

#### correctness

**File:** `OpenTelemetryInstrumentationHelper.java:108`  
**Change:** Guarded completion-time GraphQL error event extraction behind `result != null` before iterating `result.getErrors()`.

**Change:** Annotated nullable state fields and the `setOperationName()` parameter with `@Nullable`.  
**Reason:** The nullability rule requires `@Nullable` only where `null` actually flows: these state fields are unset after construction, and `operationName` is populated from `OperationDefinition.getName()`, which may be absent.

**Change:** Added the missing `otel.instrumentation.graphql.capture-query` configuration entry.  
**Reason:** `metadata.yaml` review is mandatory for instrumentation modules, and configs read by the module must be documented there; GraphQL reads `capture_query` with default `true`, but this setting was missing from metadata.

author: bmf-san
body:
## Why

`pkg/strategy/scalping` is intentionally a **5-field EMA-only reference implementation** (`ema_fast_period`, `ema_slow_period`, `take_profit_pct`, `stop_loss_pct`, `order_notional`). But its own README, the top-level READMEs, and `docs/STRATEGY.{md,ja.md}` all advertised it as "EMA crossover **+ RSI filter**" with RSI / cooldown / `max_daily_trades` / `trend_ema_period` / `auto_scale_*` / `symbol_params` / `fee_rate`. None of those fields exist in `params.go` or `strategy.go` — they live only in `example/strategy/scalping`.

Anyone copy-pasting the config snippets from that README into a project using the bundled strategy would have fields silently ignored.

author: jonathanpeppers
body:
When the blend mask is all-zeros (all lanes take min) or all-ones (all lanes take max), the generator now emits a direct Min/Max assignment instead of computing both Min and Max plus a Blend/ConditionalSelect.

This optimization is applied to all SIMD generator methods that operate on per-vector blend masks:
- `WriteSimdSortMethod32_Avx2` (int/uint AVX2)
- `WriteSimdSortMethod64` (long/ulong/double AVX-512)
- `WriteSimdSortMethodFloat` (float AVX2)
- `WriteSimdSortMethodDouble` (double AVX2)
- `WriteSimdSortMethod32_Avx512` (int/uint/float AVX-512)
- `WriteArmSimdSortMethod` (byte/sbyte ARM NEON)
- `WriteArmSimdSortMethod16` (short/ushort/char ARM NEON)

`WriteArmSimdSortMethod32` already had this optimization. `WriteSimdSortMethod` (byte/sbyte) and `WriteSimdSortMethod16` (short/ushort/char) were not modified because their full-vector blend masks always contain a mix of values.

### Benchmark impact (x86 AVX2, i9-9900K)

The biggest gains are on `float` and `double`, where the AVX2 paths had the most trivial blends to eliminate:

| Type | Before | After | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| float (27) | 107 ns | 76 ns | **29% faster** |
| float (28) | 109 ns | 73 ns | **33% faster** |
| double (27) | 110 ns | 94 ns | **15% faster** |
| double (28) | 111 ns | 100 ns | **10% faster** |

All tests pass.

body:
Two compounding bugs were making KY stuck at 40% coverage:

1. **KY retired their old URL scheme.** \`/recorddocuments/bill/{code}/{type}{num}/orig_bill.pdf\` now returns 404 for every bill including ones that worked this morning. New scheme is \`apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/{yy}{rs|ss}/{type|lower}{num}.html\` (HTML, not PDF — extractTextFromHtml handles it).

2. **Session regex only matched OS compact format.** The original regex \`^(\d{4})(RS|SS|\d*SS)\`  rejected LegiScan's \`"2026 Regular Session"\` format, so every LegiScan-sourced KY bill got synth=[] and fell to a dead OS fallback. That's 1,035 of 1,737 total KY bills (~60% of the state).

Now handles both shapes. Direct test extracts HB742 cleanly (1,079 chars, 99 words).

author: prantogg
body:
## Summary

Fixes a latent bug from the Phase 1 name-resolution work. `wkls.india.maharashtra.counties()` returned 0 rows because region-level methods built their region filter as `country_iso + \"-\" + chain[1].upper()`, producing `IN-MAHARASHTRA` instead of `IN-MH`. The dataset holds region ISOs like `IN-MH`, so the filter matched nothing.

## Root cause

Three call sites concatenated the country ISO with the uppercased chain element to form a region filter:
- `Wkl.resolve()` at chain depth 3
- `Wkl._get_suggestions()` city branch
- `Wkl._get_subdivisions()` depth-2 branch

All three assumed `chain[1]` was the region ISO suffix. After Phase 1, `chain[1]` can be a name (\"maharashtra\"), which breaks the concatenation.

## Fix

- New `REGION_LOOKUP` query (ISO-or-name match, same pattern as `COUNTRY_LOOKUP`).
- New module-level `_region_info` cache keyed by `(country_iso, raw_identifier_lower)` → canonical region ISO.
- Lazy `Wkl._region_iso` property that populates the cache on first access.
- Three call sites route through `self._region_iso` instead of inline concatenation.
- `Wkl.configure()` clears `_region_info` alongside `_country_info`.

## Test plan

- [x] 58 tests pass + 2 xfails (unchanged)
- [x] Two regression tests added: `test_counties_via_name_chain`, `test_cities_via_name_chain`, both assert the name-chain count equals the ISO-chain count
- [x] ruff format + check pass

## Follow-ups (separate PRs, stacked on this one)

- PR adding `.search()`, `__dir__` overrides, `__getitem__` deprecation
- PR broadening `.search()` and listing methods to subtree scope

`let x: T = perform e(...)` is now rejected when the annotated `T` does not match the effect's declared return type. Unknown effects are silently skipped (they're already reported separately by the undeclared-effect check).

### Item 3 — if/else branch termination consistency
Warns when one branch of an `if/else` terminates (goto/return/exhaustive match) but the other falls through. Catches the "forgot to goto in one branch" bug that the existing whole-handler fall-through warning glosses over.

Reuses the `block_always_terminates` + `enum_variants` machinery from #43 so an exhaustive enum match counts as termination.

### Item 4 — binary operator operand compatibility
Walks every expression and reports binary operators whose two operands resolve to incompatible concrete types (e.g. `1 + "two"`, `1 == "one"`). Conservative — if either operand's type can't be inferred, the check is skipped rather than emitting a false positive.

## Design notes

- All three checks live in `validate_expression_types` (items 2 + 4) and `check_if_branch_consistency` (item 3), both wired into the existing per-handler loop.
- Both use the `TypeContext` scaffolding introduced by #44, so no new inference infrastructure was needed.
- Scope reset at if/else and match-arm boundaries matches the existing goto-type-validation behavior — branches don't leak bindings to siblings or parents.

## Known limitation

`Statement::If` and `Expr::BinOp` do not carry spans in the current AST, so diagnostics from items 3 and 4 report at line 0, col 0. Adding spans to these nodes is a separate follow-up (apply the #13 pattern to expression and nested-statement nodes).

## Test Plan

- [x] `cargo test -p gust-lang --test diagnostics_validation` — 56 tests pass (46 existing, 10 new)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` — no regressions
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

## Test coverage added

Item 2:
- match: annotated type compatible with effect return → no error
- mismatch: annotation vs effect return → error
- unknown effect: annotation check is skipped

Item 3:
- one branch terminates, other falls through → warning
- both branches terminate → no warning
- neither branch terminates → no warning (other checks cover this)

Item 4:
- matching operand types → no error
- `i64 + String` → error
- `1 == "one"` (comparison) → error
- unknown operand type → no error (conservative)

Closes #30.

body:
## Summary

Ports the RSS app's Dart `UrlValidator` into the core SDK so Music, RSS, Podcasts, Scratchpad, and Blackout stop writing the same URL-validation logic independently. Every SDK consumer that performs a network fetch on a caller-supplied URL should now run the input through `privacysuite_core_sdk::privacy_utils::url::validate_url` first.

- Promotes `privacy_utils` from a single file to a module directory; the new `url` submodule lives alongside the existing tracking-parameter stripper. Existing `strip_tracking_params` callers are unaffected.
- Returns an opaque `ValidatedUrl` that strips fragment + credentials, lowercases host, and deliberately omits `Deref<Target = ::url::Url>` so string-level manipulation can't reintroduce a bad byte.
- Adds a thin UniFFI wrapper (`validate_url(String) -> Result<String, PrivacySuiteError>`) with seven distinct error variants for Kotlin/Swift callers.

## Rejection classes covered (one `#[test]` per class)

| Class | Test(s) | Error variant |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| Non-http(s) scheme | `file`, `javascript`, `data`, `mailto` | `InvalidScheme` / `MissingHost` |
| RFC 1918 IPv4 | 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 | `PrivateAddress` |
| Loopback IPv4 | 127.0.0.1 | `PrivateAddress` |
| Cloud metadata v4 | 169.254.169.254 | `PrivateAddress` |
| Loopback IPv6 | `[::1]` | `PrivateAddress` |
| Link-local IPv6 | `[fe80::1]` | `PrivateAddress` |
| IPv4-mapped IPv6 | `[::ffff:127.0.0.1]` | `PrivateAddress` |
| ULA IPv6 (incl. AWS fd00:ec2::254) | `[fd00:ec2::254]` | `PrivateAddress` |
| IPv6 zone-id | `[fe80::1%eth0]` | `InvalidHostCharacters` |
| Hex-encoded IPv4 | `0x7f.0.0.1` | `ObfuscatedIpEncoding` / `PrivateAddress` |
| Octal-encoded IPv4 | `0177.0.0.1` | `ObfuscatedIpEncoding` / `PrivateAddress` |
| Decimal-wrapped IPv4 | `2130706433` | `ObfuscatedIpEncoding` / `PrivateAddress` |
| Percent-encoded CRLF in host | `%0d%0aHost: evil.com` | `InvalidHostCharacters` / `Parse` |
| Raw NUL | `http://example.com/\0` | `InvalidHostCharacters` |
| Raw CRLF | `http://example.com/\r\n` | `InvalidHostCharacters` |
| Credentials | `user:pass@`, `user@` | `EmbeddedCredentials` |
| Bidi homograph | `\u202Eexample.com` | `InvalidHostCharacters` / `Parse` |
| Empty / garbage | `""`, `"not a url"` | `Parse` |

Positive controls: `https://example.com/feed`, `https://example.com:8443/path?q=1#frag` (fragment stripped), `https://sub.domain.example/path`, `http://example.com/feed`, `https://8.8.8.8/`.

## Integration notes

- **G1 `PrivacyClient` (in parallel):** call `validate_url` on the input URL and on every redirect hop (mirror of the pentest H10 fix already shipped in `boomleft-rss/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/privacy.rs::is_private_url`). API is stable.
- **No dep bump.** Re-uses the already-pinned `url = "=2"`. No `thiserror` added to the core SDK — `UrlError` is hand-rolled in the same style as `CryptoError` to keep the proc-macro-audited surface minimal.

## Design decisions / ambiguities

- **Trailing-dot hostnames (`http://example.com./`)**: accepted. The WHATWG parser treats trailing-dot as valid DNS (absolute root) and no SSRF class requires it — stripping the dot is a caller policy, not a validator concern.
- **Aggressive hostname rejection** (`localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`): NOT done in this pass. The Rust desktop helper blocks these, but the SDK-level validator deliberately sticks to literal-IP classification + obfuscation-detection. DNS-name SSRF is a resolver-time concern (the DoH resolver already refuses to resolve private addresses). Adding name-based SSRF here would duplicate that and false-positive on legitimate `*.local` zeroconf setups that callers may want.
- **Cloud metadata**: 169.254.169.254 and `fd00::/8` are covered; Alibaba Cloud `100.100.100.200` is NOT — it falls outside the RFC ranges and would need an explicit literal. Handoff said "just block the IPv4 literal + the fd00::/8 range and call it done for this pass," so deferred.
- **Obfuscated IP detection is conservative**: we only flag a dotted host as obfuscated when every label looks numeric/hex, so legitimate hostnames with numeric subdomains (`0a1b2c.example.com`) aren't false-positives.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p privacysuite-core-sdk` (default features)
- [x] `cargo check -p privacysuite-core-sdk --all-features`
- [x] `cargo check -p privacysuite-core-sdk --tests --all-features`
- [x] `cargo check -p privacysuite-ffi`
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` (tauri-plugin-privacysuite still compiles)
- [ ] `cargo test -p privacysuite-core-sdk --lib privacy_utils::url` — **NOT RUN**: the test runner is denied by this sandbox. Tests compile cleanly (`cargo check --tests`), but actual execution needs a reviewer in a sandbox without that restriction, or a CI run.

body:
## Summary

Adds a new `src/exporters/` package mirroring the existing `src/importers/` architecture so the project can write conversations out (universal JSON or ChatGPT format) the same way it can read them in. Closes todos 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.3.3, 2.3.4 (Stream D3).

### What's new

- **BaseExporter** (`src/exporters/base_exporter.py`) — abstract class with shared `load_conversations`, `apply_filters`, and `write_json` helpers. Loads from both the new `data/conversations/` layout and the legacy `conversations/` layout. Upgrades legacy on-disk records to universal shape on load so downstream exporters see a uniform input.
- **Filters** dataclass — `date_from`, `date_to`, `platforms` (case-insensitive list, `unknown` matches legacy entries), `limit`.
- **ExportResult** dataclass — success flag, exported/failed counts, errors, output path, metadata, plus `success_rate` / `total_processed` properties.
- **JsonExporter** — writes a versioned envelope `{format, format_version, exported_at, source_storage_path, conversation_count, filters_applied, conversations: [...]}`. `validate()` re-parses and checks each conversation has the universal required fields.
- **ChatgptExporter** — converts universal `messages` lists back into ChatGPT's `mapping` parent->child node structure (with a synthetic root) and emits epoch timestamps. `validate()` runs the output through the existing `schemas/chatgpt_schema.validate_chatgpt_export`.

### Tests

77 new tests in `tests/test_exporters/`, with **100% line coverage on `src/exporters/`**.

### Round-trip preservation

ChatGPTImporter -> JsonExporter preserves: id, platform, platform_id, model, title, messages, topics, date, created_at, import_metadata.

ChatGPTImporter -> ChatgptExporter passes the ChatGPT schema validator but is lossy on tree branching (collapsed to linear), per-message model_slug/request_id/tool-call metadata, and exact current_node selection.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- CLI command for invoking exporters.
- MCP tool wiring.
- Cursor and Claude exporters.

author: beltoforion
body:
## Summary
Enforce "each input port has at most one upstream output" at the port level. Fan-out is unchanged — one output can still feed any number of inputs — but a second output can no longer attach to an input that already has an upstream.

### `InputPort`
- New `_upstream: OutputPort | None` field.
- Read-only `upstream` property.
- Managed by the output side so callers never have to set it manually.

### `OutputPort`
- `can_connect(input)` additionally returns `False` when the input already has a different upstream.
- `connect(input)` raises a clear `TypeError` in that case: *"Input '…' is already connected to '…'. Disconnect it first."*
- `disconnect(input)` and `disconnect_all()` clear the input's upstream when it points to this output.

### UI / loader
No changes needed:
- Interactive drag: `FlowScene.mouseReleaseEvent` already catches the `TypeError` from `connect_ports` and surfaces it via the error-banner through `connection_error`.
- Flow loader: `flow_io.load_flow_into` catches incompatible edges and logs; remaining edges still load.

## New tests (`tests/test_port_connections.py`)
- Fan-out to multiple inputs works.
- Second-upstream attempt raises and is not recorded.
- Idempotent reconnect of the same pair is a no-op.
- `disconnect` / `disconnect_all` clear the upstream.
- An input is reusable after disconnect.

body:
## 문제
탈퇴 후 다시 소셜 로그인한 회원의 \`mb_leave_date\` 가 클리어되지 않아 프로필에는 '탈퇴'로 표시되지만 실제로는 정상 활동 중 (#9395).

예: \`kakao_86650815\` (\"돌아온조앙\") — \`mb_leave_date=20260312\`, \`mb_today_login=2026-04-05\`, \`mb_point=5630\`

## 영향 범위
\`\`\`sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM g5_member
WHERE mb_leave_date != '' AND mb_leave_date != '0000-00-00'
  AND mb_today_login IS NOT NULL
  AND mb_today_login > STR_TO_DATE(mb_leave_date, '%Y%m%d');
-- 결과: 1,973
\`\`\`

## 변경
### 1. \`updateLoginTimestamp\` (oauth/member.ts)
UPDATE 에 \`mb_leave_date = ''\` 추가 — 로그인 성공 시마다 탈퇴 플래그 함께 클리어해 '복귀' 상태로 복원.
- \`mb_leave_date\` 는 **본인 탈퇴 플로우(member-leave.ts)에서만** 설정되므로 로그인 시 클리어가 안전.
- 어드민 정지는 별도 필드 \`mb_intercept_date\` 로 분리되어 있어 영향 없음.
- social-login-postprocess.ts 에서 호출되는 경로로 모든 OAuth 로그인에 자동 적용.

### 2. \`migrations/002_clear_stale_mb_leave_date.sql\`
기존 1,973개 stale 계정 복구용 **수동 실행** 마이그레이션.
- \`mb_today_login > mb_leave_date\` 조건으로 실제 재로그인 발생 계정만 대상
- 백업 쿼리 + DRY RUN 쿼리 주석 포함
- 운영자가 수동으로 타이밍 선택하여 실행

## Test plan

- [ ] 정상 회원은 로그인 시 \`mb_leave_date\` 값 변함 없음
- [ ] 어드민이 \`mb_intercept_date\` 로 정지시킨 계정은 로그인 차단 플로우 여전히 작동
- [ ] 마이그레이션 DRY RUN 쿼리 결과 = 1,973
- [ ] 마이그레이션 실행 후 \`kakao_86650815\` 프로필에서 탈퇴 표시 사라짐

body:
## Summary

Renames the Reactor DSL text factory and its element record for consistency with WinUI's own naming:

- `Factories.Text` → `TextBlock` (the DSL factory method)
- `TextElement` → `TextBlockElement` (the element record)
- All `Factories.Text(...)` call sites collapse to bare `TextBlock(...)` via `using static`

## Scope

**353 files changed** (~3,178 / ~3,169 insertions/deletions):
- `src/Reactor/Core/Element.cs` — renamed the `TextElement` record
- `src/Reactor/Elements/Dsl.cs` — renamed the `Text` factory method and its return type across `Heading` / `SubHeading` / `Caption`
- `src/Reactor/Core/Reconciler.cs` — updated the two pattern matches in `ExtractElementCaption` / `ResolveCaptionForElement` that resolve caption-derived automation names
- `src/Reactor.Cli/Loc/LocalizableStringScanner.cs` — DSL method table updated (`"Text"` → `"TextBlock"`)
- `src/Reactor/Controls/Validation/FormField.cs` + 8 tests — added `using static Microsoft.UI.Reactor.Factories;` where call sites previously used the `Factories.` qualifier
- 25 sample / test / docs-pipeline files — bare `Text(...)` DSL calls renamed to `TextBlock(...)`
- Docs (`SKILL.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `skills/*.md`, `skills/design-docs/*.md`) and regenerated `docs/guide/*.md` updated for naming consistency
- `tests/Reactor.AppTests.Host/SelfTest/Fixtures/DevtoolsFixtures.cs` — carried over during rebase onto the new devtools phase 1 merge

## Naming-conflict analysis (pre-change)

Verified before starting:
- No existing `TextBlock` factory method on `Factories`
- No existing `TextBlockElement` type anywhere in the codebase
- Coexistence with WinUI's `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls.TextBlock` type is fine — a method and a type can share a name in C# because invocation context disambiguates (`TextBlock(...)` binds to the method, `new TextBlock()` / `typeof(TextBlock)` / type-position references bind to the WinUI type)
- Did not rename the unrelated `Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Documents.TextElement` WinUI type

## Test plan

All three test suites per `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

- [x] **Unit tests** (`dotnet test tests/Reactor.Tests`) — 3,859 passed, 0 failed, 46 skipped
- [x] **Selfhost tests** (`dotnet run --project tests/Reactor.AppTests.Host -- --self-test`) — 423 fixtures, 1,612 TAP asserts, 0 failures
- [x] **E2E tests** (`dotnet test tests/Reactor.AppTests`) — 105 passed, 1 failed. The single failure is `Interactive_DataGrid_ClickEditTabCommit`, which **reproduces identically on `main`** with no rename changes. Tracked as #34.

## Notes for reviewers

- The rebase onto `main` picked up the 024 devtools phase 1 merge; two fresh `TextElement` references in `Reconciler.cs` and nine `Factories.Text` references in the new `DevtoolsFixtures.cs` were renamed in place.
- Docs were recompiled with `mur docs compile --no-screenshots` to keep `docs/guide/*.md` in sync with the renamed DSL. No screenshot regeneration.

PR #53 added the automated pentest credential bootstrap — each run creates, TOTP-enrolls, signs-in as, and deletes an ephemeral Firebase user. That needs `roles/firebaseauth.admin`. Ran the equivalent standalone script against `pablohealth-oss`, `pablohealth-dev`, `pablohealth-prod`. `firebaseauth.admin` binding confirmed in all three. The pablohealth-oss pentest Job was migrated from `349958062694-compute@...` to `pentest-identity@pablohealth-oss.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

author: cardz3n
body:
## Release 1.0.6 (critical)

Fixes the **HTTP 400 Bad Request** reported on the admin *Test Credentials* button and during live checkout attempts on the testing site.

### Root cause
CARDZ3N is a **white-labeled NMI instance**. The plugin had hardcoded `secure.nmi.com` (the generic NMI host) in two places \u2014 the Transaction API endpoint and the Collect.js script URL. CARDZ3N merchant credentials do not exist on `secure.nmi.com`, so every authenticated call returned 400. Any diagnostic flow that hit `/merchants/login.php` (NMI's **human** login page, not an API endpoint) would also always return 400 / HTML.

### Fix \u2014 hostname swap (exactly as requested)

| URL | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Transaction API | `https://secure.nmi.com/api/transact.php` | `https://z3n.transactiongateway.com/api/transact.php` |
| Query API | *(not previously used)* | `https://z3n.transactiongateway.com/api/query.php` |
| 3-Step Redirect | *(not previously used)* | `https://z3n.transactiongateway.com/api/v2/three-step` |
| Collect.js | `https://secure.nmi.com/token/Collect.js` | `https://z3n.transactiongateway.com/token/Collect.js` |
| `/merchants/login.php` | not hit in code, but verified absent | n/a \u2014 never called |

### New plumbing
- `Api_Client` gains `COLLECTJS_URL`, `QUERY_URL`, `THREE_STEP_URL` constants plus `collectjs_url()`, `query_url()`, `three_step_url()` static helpers \u2014 a single source of truth for every external gateway URL.
- **4 new runtime filters** for merchants on a different white-label NMI host:
  - `cardz3n_gw_api_endpoint`
  - `cardz3n_gw_collectjs_url`
  - `cardz3n_gw_query_url`
  - `cardz3n_gw_three_step_url`
- Classic checkout and Blocks checkout both now enqueue Collect.js via `Api_Client::collectjs_url()` instead of a hardcoded literal.

### Docs
- `readme.txt` External Services section, `docs/INSTALL.md` troubleshooting table, and `LICENSE` attribution note all updated.

### How to verify on the testing site
1. Install `cardz3n-gateway-1.0.6.zip` (replaces 1.0.5).
2. WP Admin \u2192 WooCommerce \u2192 Settings \u2192 Payments \u2192 CARDZ3N Gateway \u2192 click **Test Credentials**. The request should now return **200** with a parsed NMI response instead of 400.
3. Reload the Blocks checkout. Collect.js should load from `z3n.transactiongateway.com` (check the Network tab). Run a sandbox transaction \u2014 the tokenized `payment_token` should flow through `process_payment()` and land in NMI.

### Version bumps
- Plugin header `Version:` \u2192 1.0.6
- `CARDZ3N_GW_VERSION` constant \u2192 1.0.6
- `readme.txt` `Stable tag:` \u2192 1.0.6

### Not affected
- No changes to Blocks Checkout integration, HPOS handling, uninstall cleanup, or GPL/licensing.
- No new merchant-facing settings (the new host is the default; filters are opt-in for edge cases).
- WP.org directory assets from 1.0.2 are still current.

### Description
- Added a new `uiPreset` state in the main React App and a `UI_OPTIONS` configuration object to hold three layout presets inside `carioca-game.html`.

body:
## Summary

Closes #44. `server_lifespan` awaited `validate_connection()` but ignored its `bool` return, so a client whose health-check returned `False` (rather than raising) was still registered as healthy. Tools would then hit a broken client and surface opaque downstream errors.

Extracted a `_register_client(context, name, client)` helper that:
1. Calls `await client.validate_connection()`.
2. On `True`: registers the client.
3. On `False`: logs a warning and closes the client.
4. On exception: logs and closes the client (previously the client was leaked — the exception branch created an `httpx.AsyncClient` but never awaited `close`).

The helper also collapses three near-identical blocks and fixes the `PLR0912` over-branching that the fix would otherwise trip.

author: copilot
body:
Implements the withdraw command for the wallet microservice — an HTTP `POST /withdrawals` endpoint that reduces fixed-income position lots by a desired monetary value using FIFO (oldest-first) consumption with all-or-nothing semantics and idempotent retry.

### Application layer (`WithdrawService`)
- Two-pass lot selection: pass 1 is a read-only sufficiency check, pass 2 mutates eligible lots in FIFO order
- `units_sold = (valueFromLot / lot.UnitPrice()).Round(6)` with half-up rounding
- `if_match` optimistic concurrency validation between passes
- Idempotency via `ProcessedCommand` with race-safe `ErrDuplicate` → re-read fallback
- Typed errors (`InsufficientPositionError`, `ConcurrencyConflictError`) for structured 409 responses
- 34 tests, 100% statement coverage

### HTTP handler adapter (`WithdrawHandler`)
- Thin API Gateway v2 event mapper following the existing `DepositHandler` pattern
- `codedErrorResponse` helper produces `{"error": "...", "error_code": "..."}` for `INSUFFICIENT_POSITION` and `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT`
- Reuses `jsonResponse`, `errorResponse`, `jsonMarshal` from the deposit handler (same package)
- 13 tests, 100% statement coverage

### Lambda bootstrap routing
- Replaces single-handler `lambda.Start` with a path-based router:

```go
route := func(ctx context.Context, req events.APIGatewayV2HTTPRequest) (events.APIGatewayV2HTTPResponse, error) {
    switch req.RequestContext.HTTP.Path {
    case "/deposits":
        return depositHandler.Handle(ctx, req)
    case "/withdrawals":
        return withdrawHandler.Handle(ctx, req)
    default:
        // 404
    }
}
```

- `WithdrawService` takes no `AssetRepository` — `product_asset_id` is passed directly as the `instrumentID` parameter to `FindByClientAndInstrument`

body:
## Summary

Wave 26 Task 2 of 3 — the read + write UX for threaded task comments. Builds on Task 1's schema ([#154](https://github.com/JoelA510/PlanterPlan-Alpha/pull/154)).

Adds a `planter.entities.TaskComment` client, a `useTaskComments` hook family with optimistic mutations, a mention parser, four new UI components under `src/features/tasks/components/TaskComments/`, and mounts `<TaskComments>` inside `TaskDetailsView`. No route changes, no new npm deps.

Task 3 will wire realtime invalidation on top of this.

## What shipped

**Data layer**
- `planter.entities.TaskComment` — 4 methods:
  - `listByTask(taskId, { includeDeleted? })` — author-hydrated via `select('*, author:users(id, email, user_metadata)')`; filters `deleted_at IS NULL` by default.
  - `create({ task_id, author_id, parent_comment_id?, body, mentions? })` — inserts + re-selects with author join.
  - `updateBody(commentId, { body, mentions? })` — stamps `edited_at` via `nowUtcIso()`; DB trigger owns `updated_at`.
  - `softDelete(commentId)` — `deleted_at = now()` + blanks `body` per the Wave 26 SSoT contract.

> **Cross-schema join note**: `auth.users` isn't in `Database['public']['Tables']`, so the typed client surfaces a `SelectQueryError` for the `author:users(...)` select. author: rgbkrk
body:
## Summary

Widget writes were arriving anonymous. The IOPub echo writer on the daemon side was writing to the CRDT under the default `runtimed:state` actor, so peers receiving a sync couldn't tell a kernel-authored echo apart from a frontend write. The runtime agent forwarded the echo back to the kernel, and the loop started. During rapid slider drags, the pipeline stalled.

The fix is attribution. Every echo now carries an `rt:kernel:*` actor ID. The runtime agent reads who wrote each comm field and forwards only what a foreign actor wrote.

Supersedes #1896.

## The fix

Three changes.

**1. Writes carry the kernel's actor ID.** The IOPub-driven comm-state writer was grabbing the state_doc lock and writing under the default `runtimed:state` actor. It now does `fork_and_merge` with the kernel's own `rt:kernel:*` actor. Every echo is attributable.

**2. Per-field foreign view in `receive_sync_and_foreign_comms`.** The runtime agent's filter was per-frame. If the coordinator coalesced a kernel echo with an unrelated status or queue update, the frame had a foreign change and the echo slipped through. The new view walks each `comm.state` and keeps only fields whose current LWW winner was a foreign actor. Kernel-authored values get stripped before the diff runs.

**3. Value-aware `optimisticKeys` on the frontend.** The optimistic cache now stores the last-written value per key, not just a key set. Echoes that match what the frontend wrote get suppressed. Kernel corrections (think ipywidgets clamping `5.1` back to `5.0` on a max-`5.0` slider) pass through and replace local state.

## E2E reproducer

Cherry-picked from #1896:

- `e2e/specs/widget-slider-stall.spec.js`
- `crates/notebook/fixtures/audit-test/16-widget-slider.ipynb`
- xtask fixture registration and `e2e/wdio.conf.js` entry

Drives alternating slider values through the real widget pipeline, then runs a second cell to confirm the kernel's still responsive. Also switched the `__nteractWidgetUpdate` / `__nteractWidgetStore` bridge from `DEV`-gated to `VITE_E2E`-gated so the bundled E2E build actually exposes it.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p notebook-doc --lib`: 332 pass, 4 new foreign-sync tests
- [x] `cargo test -p runtimed --lib`: 325 pass
- [x] `pnpm vp test run widget-update-manager`: 19 pass

- [ ] `cargo xtask e2e test-fixture 16-widget-slider`: repro on main, pass on this branch
- [ ] Manual: open a FloatSlider, drag fast, kernel stays responsive

author: keanji-x
body:
## Summary

PR #13 added `NEIGE_PASSWORD` to `neige-server`, but the env var was never reaching the server process — SSH doesn't transport env vars by default (`SendEnv` needs matching `AcceptEnv` in the remote `sshd_config`, and root access to reload sshd). Verified: `/proc/<server-pid>/environ` on the remote never contained `NEIGE_PASSWORD`, even with it exported locally.

`neige-connect` now reads `NEIGE_PASSWORD` from the local env and inlines the value into the remote start-up script as a nohup env prefix (single-quote escaped). Usage stays the same — `export NEIGE_PASSWORD=...` locally, run `neige-connect`.

## Exposure

The value sits in the remote `bash -c` argv for the few seconds the start-up script runs, then only lives in the spawned server's environ (same-uid readable). The server's argv stays clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p neige-connect`

author: ntner
body:
### What is the feature/update/fix?

**Feature: Target a dedicated health port in `health.port` and `liveness.port`**

Services on a rack often expose an application port via a load balancer and want readiness and liveness probes to target a different endpoint, such as an internal-only diagnostics or `/healthz` port that is never exposed outside the cluster. Before 3.24.5, the Convox manifest forced both the traffic port and the probe port to be the same.

3.24.5 adds a `port` field to both `health:` and `liveness:` in `convox.yml`. When set, the probe targets the override port instead of the main service port. When unset (the default), both probes continue to target `service.port`, matching prior behavior exactly.

| Field              | Type              | Scope                 | Default                     | Notes                                                                               |
|--------------------|-------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `health.port`      | scalar or map     | Readiness probe only  | `service.port`              | Accepts `port: 8080` or `port: { port: 8080, scheme: https }`                       |
| `liveness.port`    | scalar or map     | Liveness probe only   | `service.port`              | Same form as `health.port`                                                          |
| `scheme` (health)  | `http` / `https`  | Override only         | Inherits `service.port.scheme` | Coalesces from the service port when omitted                                     |
| `scheme` (liveness)| `http` / `https`  | Override only         | None (plain HTTP)           | Liveness does not auto-inherit; set explicitly if you need HTTPS on the probe       |

The startup probe is unaffected and continues to target the main service port regardless of `health.port` and `liveness.port`.

---

### Why is this important?

Splitting health endpoints from the load-balanced traffic port is a common hardening practice: the `/healthz` endpoint is meant for the kubelet, not the public internet, and keeping it off the public port avoids exposing internal status to anyone who can reach the load balancer.

Before this change, users either had to fold health into the same listener as the main service (exposing it publicly) or disable Convox probes entirely and roll custom ones. Both paths are worse than just pointing the probe at a different port.

**Benefits:**

| Benefit | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Keep health endpoints off the public listener. | Diagnostics, metrics, and liveness endpoints can live on an internal port that the load balancer never sees. |
| Independent scheme override. | `health.port.scheme` lets a plain-HTTP health endpoint sit behind an HTTPS-terminating service port. |
| Independent readiness vs liveness ports. | Services with separate readiness and liveness endpoints (different ports, different paths) can now express that in Convox manifest directly. |
| Drop-in compatible. | Manifests that do not set the new field produce identical pod specs to prior releases. Downgrades are safe. |

---

### How to use it?

Point the readiness probe at a separate internal diagnostics port:

```yaml
services:
  web:
    build: .
    port: 8080
    health:
      path: /healthz
      port: 9090
    liveness:
      path: /live
      port: 9090
```

Traffic routes to port 8080 via the load balancer, while the readiness and liveness probes query `http://<pod>:9090/...`.

Override the scheme explicitly on the readiness probe (for example, plain HTTP health behind an HTTPS service port):

```yaml
services:
  api:
    build: .
    port: https:8443
    health:
      path: /healthz
      port:
        port: 9090
        scheme: http
```

Here `port: 8443` remains HTTPS for public traffic, while the readiness probe queries `http://<pod>:9090/healthz` inside the cluster without the TLS handshake.

Use the map form on `liveness.port` when you need HTTPS on the liveness probe:

```yaml
services:
  secure-worker:
    port: https:8443
    liveness:
      path: /live
      port:
        port: 9090
        scheme: https
```

#### When to use this

| Pattern | Configuration |
|---------|---------------|
| Public HTTP service, internal plain-HTTP health endpoint | `port: 8080` + `health.port: 9090` (scheme inherits) |
| Public HTTPS service, internal plain-HTTP health endpoint | `port: https:8443` + `health.port: { port: 9090, scheme: http }` |
| Distinct readiness and liveness ports | Set both `health.port` and `liveness.port` (they can be the same or different) |
| gRPC service with gRPC health on a separate port | `port: grpc:50051` + `grpcHealthEnabled: true` + `health.port: 50052` |

---

### Does it have a breaking change?

**No breaking changes** are introduced with this feature.

- Manifests without `health.port` or `liveness.port` produce byte-identical pod specs to 3.24.4.
- No changes to CLI flags, API routes, struct field order, or rack parameters.
- `ServiceHealth` and `ServiceLiveness` gain a new field (`Port`) with zero-value defaults, so older SDK consumers deserialize correctly.
- Downgrade-safe: older racks silently ignore the unknown `port` field in the manifest and fall back to probing the main service port.
- No new Terraform variables, so no TF state fingertrap risk.

---

### Requirements

This feature requires version `3.24.5` or later for the rack.

**Update the Rack:** Run `convox rack update 3.24.5 -r rackName` to update to this version.

_Note that your rack must already be on at least version `3.23.0` before performing this update._

_If you're unfamiliar with v3 rack versioning, we recommend reviewing the documentation on [Updating a Rack](https://docs.convox.com/management/cli-rack-management/) before applying any updates._

author: dfederspiel
body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code

## Description

Adds a reliability harness that quantifies how often an Ollama model emits schema-valid tool_calls. This is the instrument we needed before declaring any model \"shippable\" or any fix \"helpful\" — it produces a number, not a vibe.

**Why** — Previous debates about Ollama tool support (#73, #74) mixed three different axes: *capability* (does the model advertise tools?), *plumbing* (does our runtime pass them through?), and *reliability* (does the model use them right?). PR #80 cleaned up capability. This PR makes reliability measurable.

**What** — [scripts/benchmark-tool-reliability.ts](scripts/benchmark-tool-reliability.ts). Raw \`fetch\` to \`/api/chat\` with no runtime wrapper, so the numbers reflect the model, not our code. Suite:

- **single-arg-explicit** — one tool, one required param, \"use the tool\" in the prompt
- **multi-arg** — three required params, tests multi-arg compliance
- **tool-choice** — two tools, must pick the right one
- **no-tool-needed** — conversational question with a tool available, model should abstain

Scored as success iff: a \`tool_calls\` array is emitted, the call's name matches a provided tool, and args validate against the schema (required fields present, types correct, enums respected). For \`no-tool-needed\`, success is the opposite — no \`tool_calls\`.

**Baseline** (5 iterations/case, macOS CPU, Ollama local):

| Model         | Overall | single | multi | choice | restraint | avg latency |
|---------------|---------|--------|-------|--------|-----------|-------------|
| llama3.2:1b   | **35%** (7/20)  | 60%    | 80%   | 0%     | 0%        | ~2s         |
| qwen3.5:4b    | **100%** (20/20) | 100%   | 100%  | 100%   | 100%      | ~29s        |

**What this changes:**

- qwen3.5:4b is **shippable on this suite today**. No retry loop needed to hit \"single tool, called reliably.\"
- llama3.2:1b's failures aren't what I was about to fix (schema drift). In tool-choice it emits raw JSON as message content (not structured \`tool_calls\`); in restraint it always calls a tool. A schema-validating retry loop wouldn't have touched either — neither produces a malformed tool_call to retry.
- The harness has now prevented one misdirected fix. That's its job.

**Usage:**

\`\`\`bash
npx tsx scripts/benchmark-tool-reliability.ts llama3.2:1b 5
npx tsx scripts/benchmark-tool-reliability.ts qwen3.5:4b 10
npx tsx scripts/benchmark-tool-reliability.ts all 5 --json
\`\`\`

**How it was tested** — Ran both models end-to-end; results above. Harness is pure fetch, no existing behaviour touched — no test suite impact.

**Follow-ups** (not in this PR):
- Extend suite to cover multi-turn flows once we have a fixture for that
- Widen metrics beyond binary success (e.g., failure-mode histogram)
- Integrate into CI as a nightly signal

author: quangvdao
body:
## Summary

**F2 Slice 2.** Stacked on [#297](https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/VCV-io/pull/297) (F1 Slice 2 + F2 Slice 1).

Introduces:
1. The **generic env-channel wrapper** `EnvOpenProcess Party Δ Event State` — the structural pairing of an `OpenProcess` with an `EnvAction`.
2. A **clean framework / model split** for corruption: `CorruptionModel` (the 3-field bundle) and `SnapshotLeakable` (the snapshot leakage observer) live in their own files; the CJSV22-flavoured machinery is renamed under `MomentaryCorruption.*`.

Three commits, additive throughout, **zero new axioms** (only one structural lemma uses `propext`).

The original F2 design memo proposed threading a fourth universe parameter `Σ` through `OpenNodeSemantics` (with `Σ := Empty` default) so corruption events would live alongside `BoundaryAction` on every node. That direction is invasive (touches every `OpenProcess` constructor and the 14 `_iso` lemmas in `OpenProcessModel.lean`). This PR ships the same expressive power **additively** by introducing a wrapper layer above `OpenProcess` instead. Existing `OpenProcess` consumers are unchanged; corruption-aware constructions opt in via the new wrapper.

## Generic env-channel wrapper

### `EnvOpenProcess Party Δ Event State` (`VCVio/Interaction/UC/EnvOpenProcess.lean`, new file)

Two-field structure:
* `process : OpenProcess Party Δ` — the standard open-process boundary surface;
* `envAction : EnvAction Event State` — an independent env-driven channel.

Generic in `(Event, State)`. The two channels are kept structurally orthogonal, matching CJSV22 §3.2 where corruption events flow from the environment rather than from the adversary's port boundary.

### Wrapper API (~15 declarations)

| Declaration | Role |
| ----------- | ---- |
| `toOpenProcess` | Forget env channel, recover plain `OpenProcess`. |
| `react` | React to a single env event on env-side state (delegates to `envAction.react`). |
| `ofOpenProcess P S` | Trivial wrap with `Event := Empty`. |
| `passive P Event S` | Wrap with passive alphabet (every event no-ops). |
| `comapEvent g E` | Adapt alphabet contravariantly along `g : Event → Event'`. |
| `withEnvAction E ea` | Replace env action wholesale (re-target to a new `(Event', State')`). |
| `mapBoundary φ E` | Adapt boundary along `PortBoundary.Hom`, env channel intact. |

Plus rfl-grade simp lemmas for every projection and the `comapEvent_id` / `comapEvent_comapEvent` functoriality lemmas.

## Framework / model split

The Slice 1 vocabulary lumped the *framework* (alphabet-agnostic abstractions) and the *Signal model* (CJSV22-flavoured AMC machinery) into a single `Corruption.lean` file with names like `CorruptionAlphabet`, `CorruptionState`, `LeakableState`. Slice 2 separates them:

### Framework

* **`CorruptionModel`** (`VCVio/Interaction/UC/CorruptionModel.lean`, new file). A 3-field bundle:
  ```lean
  structure CorruptionModel where
    Event : Type
    State : Type
    envAction : EnvAction Event State
  ```
  This is the API for "I want to write a process / proof / lemma generic over the corruption model" — declare `(M : CorruptionModel)` and use `M.Event`, `M.State`, `M.envAction`, `M.Process Party Δ`. The `M.Process` abbreviation specializes `EnvOpenProcess` to the model's `(Event, State)`.

* **`SnapshotLeakable`** (`VCVio/Interaction/UC/Leakage.lean`, new file). The static per-party state-projection observer (the typed form of CJSV22's equivocability obligation). Generic in the party identity, not bundled into `CorruptionModel` because the same model appears with several leakage observers across different proofs (a snapshot leak in the IND-CCA proof, a structured leak in the side-channel reduction). Future leakage observers (interactive, erasure-aware, structured/partial) become separate typeclasses without disturbing existing code.

### Signal model

* **`MomentaryCorruption.*`** (`VCVio/Interaction/UC/MomentaryCorruption.lean`, renamed from `Corruption.lean`). Everything CJSV22-specific lives under this namespace, making it explicit *which* corruption model is in scope:

  | Slice 1 name (deprecated)         | Slice 2 name                                           |
  | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `CorruptionAlphabet Sid Pid`      | `MomentaryCorruption.Alphabet Sid Pid`                 |
  | `CorruptionState Sid Pid`         | `MomentaryCorruption.State Sid Pid`                    |
  | `CorruptionState.applyCompromise` | `MomentaryCorruption.State.applyCompromise`            |
  | `CorruptionState.applyRefresh`    | `MomentaryCorruption.State.applyRefresh`               |
  | `CorruptionState.reactBase`       | `MomentaryCorruption.react`                            |
  | `CorruptionState.envActionBase`   | `MomentaryCorruption.envAction`                        |
  | `CorruptionProcess Sid Pid Δ`     | `MomentaryCorruption.Process Sid Pid Δ`                |
  | `MachineProcess.withCorruption`   | `MachineProcess.withMomentaryCorruption`               |
  | `LeakableState`                   | `SnapshotLeakable` (in `Leakage.lean`, party-generic)  |
  | `Epoch`                           | `MomentaryCorruption.Epoch`                            |
  | `CorruptionPolicy`                | (deleted; use `ProcessOver.StepPolicy` directly)       |

  The bundled value `MomentaryCorruption.model Sid Pid : CorruptionModel` ties the model into the framework API.

### Why this rename now

Per discussion in this PR cycle, the user observed that the Slice 1 names were "overly broad" and Signal-specific despite their generic-sounding names. The framework / model split addresses this:

* **`CorruptionModel`** as the framework type makes the *named-choice* nature explicit. New corruption models (static, persistent-adaptive, threshold, mobile, leakage-resilient) become their own values of `CorruptionModel`; nothing in the framework forces commitment to AMC.
* **`MomentaryCorruption.*`** makes it grep-discoverable that *this is the AMC model*. Other models will live under their own namespace (`StaticCorruption.*`, etc.).
* **`SnapshotLeakable`** makes the *snapshot* observation model explicit (rather than the misleadingly generic `LeakableState`). Other observers (interactive, erasure-aware) ship as their own typeclasses when needed.
* **`CorruptionPolicy` deleted** — it was a no-op alias over `ProcessOver.StepPolicy`. A richer policy DSL (with corruption-aware combinators like `static`, `momentary`, `bounded n`) is its own follow-up slice; the alias added no expressive power.

## Deferred (F2 Slice 3+)

* **Composition operators** `EnvOpenProcess.par` / `wire` / `plug` lifted from `OpenTheory`. Deferred so the env-channel combination strategy can be an explicit parameter rather than a baked-in default. Three natural strategies surface in CJSV22-style protocols: broadcast (every event hits both sub-wrappers), targeted (only the wrapper holding the addressed `MachineId` reacts; needs `HasAccessControl` integration), and Kleisli-sequential (left then right).
* **Four `*.envReact` (generic) and `*.corrupt` (model-canonical) forwarding lemmas.** Together they show how env reactions on a composite decompose into reactions on the components. They are the conceptual heart of CJSV22 §4.2 and slot in once the composition operators ship.
* **Runtime integration.** A small extension to `processSemanticsOracle` in `Runtime.lean` so env events are scheduled alongside boundary ticks.
* **Event-policy DSL.** Generic policy combinators on env-event traces (`static`, `momentary`, `bounded n`, `byEpoch`, etc.). Replaces the deleted `CorruptionPolicy` alias with something that actually adds value.
* **Pilot protocols** (`F_AKE`, `F_E2E` with the healing theorem `heals_after_refresh`).

See `Notes/vcvio-uc-f2-corruption-design.md` for the updated slicing plan and §0.1 for the rename inventory.

## Test plan

- [x] `lake build` (full repo, 3574/3575)
- [x] `#print axioms` audit on a

author: nathanjohnpayne
body:
Authoring-Agent: claude

Closes the preflight-detector half of #137 (failure mode B). The firebase-CLI-side fix (detect stale `firebase-tools` configstore inside `op-firebase-deploy`) remains open.

## Summary

Adds `adc_is_usable()` to `scripts/op-preflight.sh`, mirroring `source_cred_is_usable` in `scripts/firebase/op-firebase-deploy`. Called after materializing a fresh ADC and on cached-hit fast-path reuse. If the credential fails the OAuth2 `/token` round-trip, preflight prints an actionable multi-line warning with the exact `gcloud auth application-default login` + `op document edit 'GCP ADC' --vault=Private ...` commands to refresh the 1Password item, and skips the `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` export so downstream callers (`op-firebase-deploy`, `gcloud` wrappers) transparently fall back to the local firebase-login / ADC path — the exact workaround the issue reporter identified.

## Why

#137 failure mode B: a 1Password ADC item whose authorized_user `refresh_token` has been revoked/expired by Google is still `op read`-able, so preflight used to materialize a file and export `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` happily — only for the next `op-firebase-deploy` invocation to refuse the credential with:

```
Error: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS points to an unusable credential file: /var/folders/.../op-preflight-adc-*
```

The reporter's workaround was `env -u GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS -u OP_PREFLIGHT_DONE op-firebase-deploy --only hosting`, which forced the script to fall through to the local firebase-login ADC that had just been refreshed by `firebase login --reauth`. Automating that fallback in preflight removes the manual step.

## Implementation

- **New helper `adc_is_usable`** wraps a Python3 snippet that unwraps `impersonated_service_account` → `authorized_user`, passes through on `service_account` keys, and for `authorized_user` hits `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` with the embedded refresh token. Returns 0 on mint success, 1 otherwise (including python3 unavailable, malformed JSON, missing fields, network failure — erring toward "treat as stale" so downstream callers aren't stuck holding a dead credential).
- **New helper `log_stale_adc_guidance`** emits a multi-line warning with the exact refresh commands. Called from both the full-fetch and cached-hit paths.
- **Full-fetch path.** After `op read > $ADC_TMPFILE` succeeds and the file is non-empty, run `adc_is_usable`. On pass: export normally. On fail: delete the tempfile, log guidance, record `STALE` in the summary, proceed with preflight-done + PATs intact so review commands keep working.
- **Cached-hit fast path.** In `emit_from_session_file`, extend the ADC validation from file-exists-and-non-empty to also require `adc_is_usable`. On fail: log guidance, return non-zero to trigger a full refresh (the refresh re-detects stale on the fresh materialization and takes the same skip path — one biometric re-prompt, accepted as the cost of catching the stale-cache case; the alternative is emitting a dead `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` export for up to `TTL_SECONDS`).

## Self-Review

- **Correctness.** End-to-end test: seeded a deliberately-broken ADC at `$HOME/.cache/mergepath/op-preflight-claude-adc.json` with `{"type": "authorized_user", "refresh_token": "INVALID_FAKE", ...}`, ran preflight. Output: fast-path detected stale → full refresh → full fetch also stale → multi-line warning → no `export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` line emitted. `OP_PREFLIGHT_DONE=1` still set, PATs still exported (when mode is `review` or `all`). Edge cases: non-existent file, empty file, malformed JSON, missing fields, `service_account` passthrough — all verified via inline arithmetic.
- **Regression risk.** Additive — a `--mode review` invocation is unaffected (adc_is_usable is never called). A `--mode deploy`/`all` invocation against a healthy ADC sees a small additional cost (one HTTPS round-trip to `oauth2.googleapis.com`, ~50-200ms). When python3 is unavailable, adc_is_usable returns 1 — I chose stale-by-default over skip-validation because a deploy with a bad credential fails fast downstream with a clearer message than a silently-skipped check.
- **Style.** Matches the existing helper style in the file. All Python lives in `<<'PY'` heredocs identical to the sibling check in `op-firebase-deploy`.
- **Test coverage.** End-to-end manually verified on the happy path (no ADC item available → clean "not available" path) and the stale-refresh-token path (warning + skip). A bash unit-test harness for preflight helpers is out of scope here.
- **Security / dependency hygiene.** No new dependencies — `python3` + `urllib` are already required by `op-firebase-deploy`'s sibling check. No secrets logged. `$ADC_TMPFILE` deleted on stale detection. The OAuth2 round-trip transmits the refresh token over HTTPS to Google's canonical endpoint only.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI lint passes.
- [ ] First preflight run on a healthy 1Password ADC item: normal happy-path output, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` exported.
- [ ] Preflight run after the 1Password ADC has been rotated/revoked: multi-line warning, no export, `OP_PREFLIGHT_DONE=1` still set, downstream `op-firebase-deploy` falls through to local auth.

Closes SEE-217. Five deferred reviewer findings against the alert pipeline (carried over from the S-194 / SEE-204 five-reviewer review):

- **AC-1 — selector cache scoping (R1-M-1, R3-M-1, R5-LOW).** `selectVisibleAndCounts` cache moved from module-level `let` bindings to a `WeakMap<AlertsState, CacheEntry>`. No more cross-instance leak in tests, GC reclaims old entries when stores die. Public API unchanged.
- **AC-2 — walker recursion depth cap (R5-LOW).** `reviveBigintTimestamps` capped at `REVIVE_MAX_DEPTH = 32` (≈6× headroom over the deepest legitimate Seerflow payload). Past the cap, value returns unchanged and `logger.warn("revive depth cap")` fires once per top-level call (closure-scoped flag).
- **AC-3 — walker scope tightening (R1-I-2, R3-M-4).** `request()` now invokes `reviveBigintTimestamps` only when a small allocation-free `hasBigintMarker` pre-check finds a bigint marker. Bigint-free responses (`/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/status`, etc.) skip the walker entirely.
- **AC-4 — alert_batch length cap (R5-LOW).** WS `alert_batch` arm wrapped in `v.pipe(v.array(AlertDataSchema), v.maxLength(100))`. Backend caps at `batch_max_events = 10` server-side; the frontend cap defends against a misbehaving / compromised peer with 10× headroom over the backend default.
- **AC-5 — deprecate dual selectors (R3-L-2).** `selectVisible` and `selectCounts` deleted. The two test-only consumers were rewritten to call `selectVisibleAndCounts(...).visible` / `.counts`. `AlertFeed.tsx:137` already used the combined selector; no widget consumers existed.

R3-M-5 (`makeLogger` JSDoc) was already addressed in S-194 and is explicitly out of scope. Documented in story.

## Diff

Frontend-only TypeScript: `frontend/src/stores/alerts.ts`, `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts` and their `*.test.ts` peers. No backend code touched. No new runtime deps.

body:
PowerShell 5.1 misparsed backtick-continued `git -c` flags, causing `(local run)` in the commit message to be evaluated as a subexpression — `local` was invoked as a command and the script aborted.

## Changes

- **`scripts/run_scraper.ps1`**
  - Replace `git -c user.name=… -c user.email=…` backtick continuation with `GIT_AUTHOR_*` / `GIT_COMMITTER_*` env vars — no line continuation needed
  - Change commit message from `(local run)` → `[local run]` to eliminate the subexpression ambiguity entirely
  - Wrap commit/push in `try/finally` to null out the env vars afterward, preventing session pollution

**Before:**
```powershell
git -c user.name="local-scraper" `
    -c user.email="local-scraper@$env:COMPUTERNAME" `
    commit -m "chore: update CRA feed (local run) [skip ci]"
```

**After:**
```powershell
$env:GIT_AUTHOR_NAME    = 'local-scraper'
$env:GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL   = "local-scraper@$env:COMPUTERNAME"
$env:GIT_COMMITTER_NAME  = 'local-scraper'
$env:GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL = "local-scraper@$env:COMPUTERNAME"
try {
    git commit -m 'chore: update CRA feed [local run] [skip ci]'
    git push origin main
} finally {
    $env:GIT_AUTHOR_NAME = $env:GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL = $null
    $env:GIT_COMMITTER_NAME = $env:GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL = $null
}
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Bug

`scripts/run_scraper.ps1` fails to execute on Windows PowerShell 5.1 because the commit message contains parentheses:

```powershell
commit -m "chore: update CRA feed (local run) [skip ci]"
```

PowerShell's parser interprets `(local run)` as a sub-expression and tries to invoke `local` as a command, producing:

```
local : The term 'local' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program.
```

even though the parentheses are inside a double-quoted string. This appears to be related to how the multi-line `git -c … `` continuation interacts with the parser on PS 5.1.

## Fix

In `scripts/run_scraper.ps1`, replace the entire commit-and-push block (currently around lines 76–85) with a version that:

1. **Uses square brackets instead of parentheses** in the commit message: `chore: update CRA feed [local run] [skip ci]`
2. **Sets git author/committer via environment variables** instead of `git -c …` continuation lines (cleaner, avoids backtick line-continuation issues entirely):

```powershell
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Commit + push if anything changed
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    git add cra_feed/output/
    git diff --cached --quiet
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        $env:GIT_AUTHOR_NAME     = "local-scraper"
        $env:GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL    = "local-scraper@$env:COMPUTERNAME"
        $env:GIT_COMMITTER_NAME  = "local-scraper"
        $env:GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL = "local-scraper@$env:COMPUTERNAME"
        git commit -m "chore: update CRA feed [local run] [skip ci]"
        git push origin main
    } else {
        Write-Host "No changes to commit."
    }
```

## File encoding

The file MUST be saved as **UTF-8 with BOM** (or ASCII) so Windows PowerShell 5.1 parses it correctly. Do NOT save as UTF-16. The existing file is already correctly encoded — preserve that encoding.

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/run_scraper.ps1` parses and executes cleanly under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
- The commit message contains `[local run]` (square brackets) instead of `(local run)`.
- No other behavioral changes — same git fetch/pull/venv/pytest/scrape/validate/push flow.
- File encoding preserved (UTF-8 with BOM or ASCII, NOT UTF-16).

body:
## Summary

Integration-tier resilience scenarios from #253 (umbrella #247). Five of six scenarios implemented against `AppIntegrationTestHarness`; the stream-failure-containment one is deferred to #266 because it needs a new fixture hook (relay-side mux ERROR injection).

- **HalfOpenReconnectTest** — #243 regression guard: relay-side WS drop without a close frame drives the tunnel to DISCONNECTED via mux keepalive.
- **IdleTimeoutWakeTest** — idle-equivalent drop plus synthetic FCM wake recovers to CONNECTED through `WakeReconnectDecider`.
- **CertRotationMidSessionTest** — #237-class guard: `renewWithMtls` while the tunnel is live doesn't knock it off; client cert rolls; `/renew` carries the mTLS client cert.
- **RelayRestartTest** — killing + restarting the relay subprocess lets the client detect via keepalive and reconnect on wake.
- **RapidFcmWakesTest** — 5 FCM wakes + decider calls in <2s keep the tunnel stable. (Service-level `reconnectJob` dedup is covered at `:work`'s unit-test tier.)

`TunnelTestSupport` wires a test-friendly `WebSocketFactory` (OkHttp + DNS loopback override, fixture-CA trust, on-disk cert) so scenarios drive a real `TunnelClientImpl` with accelerated keepalive instead of mutating the production factory in Koin. #262's Conscrypt SNI issue is not in play because these scenarios only exercise the device-side TLS egress, not the relay's SNI passthrough for synthetic AI clients.

author: seedofevil
body:
## Summary

Implements a bounded browser-microphone dictation feature for canonical Vera that routes through the shared voice-session pipeline. Operators can now capture audio directly from the Vera web interface using a mic button, which is transcribed and processed identically to the panel Voice Workbench's voice lanes.

## Key Changes

- **New voice-session pipeline module** (`voice_session_pipeline.py`): A shared, bounded STT → (lifecycle | Vera + optional preview) → optional TTS pipeline consumed by both the panel Voice Workbench and canonical Vera dictation. Implements fail-closed semantics at every step (empty transcript, STT error, Vera error, TTS error, etc.) without fabricating previews or bypassing canonical state seams.

- **Vera dictation endpoint** (`POST /chat/voice`): Accepts raw audio blobs with strict validation (audio/* content-type required, max 25 MB, non-empty body). Writes turns to the canonical Vera session with `voice_transcript` input origin, identical to typed chat. Returns a compact JSON payload for inline thread updates without full-page reload.

- **TTS audio serving** (`GET /vera/voice/audio/<token>`): Short-lived tokenized endpoint that serves synthesized audio without exposing temp-file paths. Tokens expire within 10 minutes; registry is pruned on each request.

- **Browser dictation enhancer** (`vera_dictation.js`): Progressive enhancement script that:
  - Reveals mic button and voice bar only when voice foundation is enabled AND browser supports MediaRecorder + getUserMedia
  - Operator-initiated recording only (no always-on listening)
  - Renders turns inline via the shared pipeline result
  - Handles lifecycle actions, action-oriented preview drafting, and TTS playback
  - Gracefully degrades when JS or mic unavailable; typed chat always works

- **UI components** (index.html, vera.css): Mic button with recording pulse animation, voice state bar showing transcription/processing status, error display, and optional TTS audio player. All hidden by default for progressive enhancement.

- **Index page updates**: Advertises mic button, voice bar, and dictation script when voice foundation is enabled.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Trust model**: Turns persist as `voice_transcript`-origin entries on the canonical Vera session store, enabling seamless continuation in the canonical UI. Preview drafting reuses the canonical deterministic path; lifecycle phrases dispatch through the bounded canonical-state-only seam (no fake submit).

- **Fail-closed design**: Empty/non-audio/oversized bodies return 400/415/413 without touching STT or Vera. STT errors, Vera errors, and TTS failures each surface as typed negative results; text remains authoritative even when TTS fails.

- **Shared pipeline**: Both the panel Voice Workbench (file-path and browser-mic lanes) and canonical Vera dictation call the same `run_voice_session_turn()` function, ensuring identical STT path, lifecycle dispatch, preview drafting, and trust framing regardless of audio source.

- **Temp file lifecycle**: Audio blobs are written to short-lived temp files with appropriate suffixes based on content-type. TTS output paths are registered with expiring tokens so the browser never learns real filesystem paths.

body: ## Summary Third attempt at the lineup-caption-edit bug. Every edit-in-place approach (PR #7, #8, #9) broke the embed→attachment link on Discord's side in a different way (image vanishes, renders above the embed, or duplicates). Root cause: once an embed-with-attachment message exists, Discord does not let you reliably re-link a fresh embed's image to either the original attachment or a re-uploaded copy via `msg.edit`. It seems to work only for the initial `channel.send`. **Fix:** on caption edit, delete the old lineup message and send a fresh one with the same image and the new caption — using the same code path as the original `/lineup` post, which we know renders correctly. Update the lineup cache to track the new message ID so subsequent `/panel` Edit Caption targets the right message. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Post a new lineup with `/lineup image:` — image inside embed, normal render. - [ ] Click **✏ Edit Caption**, change the text, submit. - [ ] Old lineup message is gone. A new lineup message appears at the bottom of the channel with the updated caption and image **inside** the embed (single image, no standalone preview). - [ ] Run `/panel` → **✏ Edit Lineup Caption** — confirm it targets the latest (newly posted) message, not the deleted one. - [ ] Edit the caption a second time — works the same way, no orphans. - [ ] (Visible side effect) The lineup message's position in the channel changes on each edit (moves to bottom) and notifications may fire again. This is the trade-off for guaranteed correct rendering. ### Notes - If the old message has no attachment, falls back to regular edit-in-place (no disruption). - No env/config changes. - Old lineup messages still around from PR #7/#8/#9 attempts may have lost their original attachment — those are unrecoverable; post a new one. ## Summary
The "Allow Microphone" button shipped in #157 didn't work from the user's perspective — it called `getUserMedia()` to trigger Chrome's URL-bar reminder, but that reminder is subtle, browser-dependent, and invisible to many users. The click looked like a no-op.

The button promised an action it can't deliver: **no JavaScript API exists to programmatically reset a denied permission**, full stop.

This PR reframes the modal as an honest visual guide pointing the user at where the fix actually lives — browser chrome, not the page.

## Changes
- **Pulsing arrow at the top of the viewport** pointing up toward the URL bar, with a "LOOK UP HERE" label. Animates 1.6s ease-in-out infinite so the user's eye follows it to the address bar.
- **Three numbered steps** with circular badges:
  1. Click the lock icon in the address bar
  2. Set Microphone to Allow
  3. Call opens automatically (or click Try Again)
- **Button renamed Allow Microphone → Try Again** — honest about what it does (retry `getUserMedia` in case the user has flipped the setting).
- **On still-denied retry, inline red status panel**: "Still blocked. Use the lock icon in the address bar above — NICE can't override your browser's mic setting." Confirms the click was registered AND that the fix lives outside the page.
- **`permissions.onchange` watcher unchanged** — still auto-resumes the call the moment the user flips the setting.

## Files
- [app/js/lib/call-mode.js](app/js/lib/call-mode.js) — new arrow markup, step-list markup, status element, retry-feedback in `_attemptMicGrant`.
- [app/css/app.css](app/css/app.css) — `.nice-ai-mic-help-arrow` (pulse animation), `.nice-ai-mic-help-steps` (numbered list with badges), `.nice-ai-mic-help-status` (checking + blocked variants).

## Verification

- Modal renders with arrow, 3 steps, Try Again button (verified)
- Try Again on still-denied state shows red "Still blocked" status panel (verified)
- Cancel + backdrop click both close cleanly

Pod 4 v1.7.2 install completes but \`User=dac\` modules (env-monitor, calibrator) crash-loop with systemd 203/EXEC. Root cause: uv installs managed Python under \`/home/root/.local/share/uv/\` (mode 0700); \`dac\` user can't traverse → permission denied on execve.

author: o0charlie0o
body:
## Summary

Fixes the macOS House Preview video export path to actually use VideoToolbox end-to-end. On a 3840×2052 @ 40 fps sequence exported as H.264 this takes encode time from **~166 ms/frame to ~3.5 ms/frame** — total wall time from ~170 ms/frame (5.8 fps) to **~9.3 ms/frame (~107 fps)** on an M1 Max. Roughly **17–18× faster at 4K**.

> ⚠️ **Tested on macOS only** (M1 Max, Metal canvas, VideoToolbox encoder). The hardware-acceleration path is guarded by `#if defined(__APPLE__)` so Windows and Linux builds should be unaffected, but they haven't been exercised. The Node bounds-check and parallel-branch null-check are platform-agnostic but likewise only tested on macOS.

## Root cause

`VideoExporter.cpp` had a `#ifdef XL_DRAWING_WITH_METAL` block intended to switch the encoder to `AV_PIX_FMT_VIDEOTOOLBOX` so a GPU-backed CVPixelBuffer could be fed straight to the hardware encoder. But `XL_DRAWING_WITH_METAL` is only defined in `src-ui-wx/ui/graphics/xlGraphicsBase.h`, a UI header that `VideoExporter.cpp` doesn't include — so the preprocessor always stripped the block. Every macOS export has silently fallen back to `AV_PIX_FMT_YUV420P`, which means an `sws_scale` RGB→YUV conversion runs on the CPU for every frame. At 4K that conversion alone is ~150 ms per frame.

On top of that, the generic `avcodec_find_encoder(AV_CODEC_ID_H264)` lookup returns `libx264` before `h264_videotoolbox` on FFmpeg builds that include libx264 — so even when someone picked H.264 they were getting software encode.

## Changes

**`src-ui-wx/ui/media/VideoExporter.{cpp,h}`**
- Wire up a real VideoToolbox hardware context: `av_hwdevice_ctx_create(AV_HWDEVICE_TYPE_VIDEOTOOLBOX)` + `av_hwframe_ctx_alloc`/`av_hwframe_ctx_init` with `format=AV_PIX_FMT_VIDEOTOOLBOX`, `sw_format=AV_PIX_FMT_NV12`, pool size 40; attach via `av_buffer_ref` to `_videoCodecContext->hw_frames_ctx` before `avcodec_open2`.
- Frames are now allocated with `av_hwframe_get_buffer` (pool-backed CVPixelBufferRef in `data[3]`) instead of `av_frame_get_buffer`. `av_frame_make_writable` is called before re-filling a ring slot to avoid racing the encoder's retained buffer.
- Explicitly prefer `h264_videotoolbox` / `hevc_videotoolbox` by name on Apple before falling back to the generic lookup.
- Drop the stale "force HEVC above 1080p" rule — H.264 High profile supports 4K up through Level 5.2; honor the user's codec choice.
- Pass VideoToolbox performance hints for offline encoding: `realtime=0`, `prio_speed=1`, `frames_before=0`.
- Replace the dead `#ifdef XL_DRAWING_WITH_METAL` guard with `#if defined(__APPLE__)` so the fast path actually compiles in.

**`src-ui-wx/ui/graphics/metal/xlMetalCanvas.mm`**
- `getFrameForExport` software-encoder fallback now uses `vImageConvert_BGRA8888toRGB888` (Accelerate / SIMD) instead of a per-pixel CPU loop.

**`src-ui-wx/ui/graphics/opengl/xlGLCanvas.{cpp,h}`**
- `getFrameForExport` uses a persistent readback buffer (no `new uint8_t[w*4*h]` / `delete` per frame), reads as `GL_RGB` directly (skipping the per-pixel RGBA→RGB loop), and flips via `memcpy` per row.

**`src-core/models/Node.h` + `src-core/render/PixelBuffer.cpp`** (small unrelated hardening that surfaced during testing)
- `NodeBaseClass::GetForChannels` / `SetFromChannels` now guard `offsets[x] < chanCnt` in addition to the existing `!= 255` sentinel check. The constructor that initializes `offsets` from an `rgbOrder` string silently truncates `std::string::npos` to 255 (so a missing channel letter is handled), but a pathological rgbOrder whose letter positions exceed the node's `chanCnt` would write past the caller's buffer. This is a cheap belt-and-suspenders check.
- Null-check `n` in the `PixelBufferClass::GetColors` parallel branch to match what the serial branch already does.

## Test plan

**macOS (done locally):**
- [x] macOS + Metal + H.264 4K (3840×2052 @ 40 fps): `h264_videotoolbox` selected, exports ~21s vs >5min previously, .mp4 plays in QuickTime and VLC.
- [x] End-to-end batch render + video export run completes without the `NodeBaseClass::GetForChannels` crash that showed up during earlier testing.
- [x] macOS + H.265 preference — `hevc_videotoolbox` picked, output plays.
- [x] macOS + explicit "MPEG-4" codec preference — falls back to `mpeg4` encoder without errors (considerably slower than H.264/H.265 as expected; it's the software encoder).
- [x] macOS + 1080p sequence — no regression; per-frame time is lower than the 4K run (encoder work scales ~linearly with pixel count).

**Needs verification by reviewers:**
- [ ] **Windows build still compiles and exports** (hardware path guarded by `__APPLE__`, but I haven't built on Windows).
- [ ] **Linux build still compiles and exports** (same).
- [ ] No warnings from `av_hwdevice_ctx_create` / `av_hwframe_ctx_init` in the log on init.
