author: vineetsridhar1
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes for coding channel creation when repos are cloned on a desktop bridge:

- **Server `listBranches`**: previously matched *any* cloud runtime before checking if it had the repo, so if a cloud container and a desktop bridge were both connected, cloud won — but cloud had not cloned the repo yet and returned `"Repo not cloned"`. Now requires the chosen runtime to actually have the repo in `registeredRepoIds` (`apps/server/src/services/session.ts`).
- **Container-bridge**: scans `/repos` on connect and sends `repo_linked` after `ensureRepo` succeeds, so cloud runtimes correctly advertise which repos they have on disk (`apps/container-bridge/src/{bridge,workspace}.ts`).
- **CreateChannelDialog**: filters the repo picker to repos registered on at least one connected runtime, with an inline empty state when none are cloned (`apps/web/src/components/sidebar/CreateChannelDialog.tsx`). When there is no accessible local runtime at all, falls back to showing all repos to preserve cloud-only flows.

## Test plan

- [ ] Desktop bridge connected with repo A cloned; Create Channel dialog only shows repo A (not other org repos).
- [ ] Base-branch combobox lists branches for repo A (no more `"Repo not cloned"` error).
- [ ] Desktop bridge disconnected + cloud runtime only: repo picker still shows all repos (cloud clones on demand).
- [ ] No connected runtimes at all: picker shows repos but operations will fail later (no regression).
- [ ] `pnpm -r lint` and `pnpm --filter @trace/server test:unit` pass.

### Description

- Updated the shared header rules in `styles.css` to use a translucent white background, subtle shadow, and `backdrop-filter` blur for light depth while retaining sticky positioning. 
- Strengthened the brand typography with a responsive `clamp()` size, heavier weight, tighter tracking, and improved line-height to increase visual hierarchy. 
- Restyled navigation links to use pill-style padding, rounded radii, slightly increased font-size, and smooth hover/focus backgrounds and outlines for better affordance.

author: slabgorb
body:
## Summary
Replaces \`just server\`'s \`just api-run\` delegation with a direct prebuild-then-exec recipe. Eliminates \`cargo run\`'s rebuild-check overhead on warm restarts — useful during playtest debugging where you restart the API repeatedly to verify each fix.

## Behavior change

**Before:**
\`\`\`makefile
server *flags:
    just api-run {{flags}}
\`\`\`
Calls \`api-run\` which does \`cargo build -p sidequest-namegen ...; cargo run -p sidequest-server -- ...\` — two cargo invocations, plus \`cargo run\` rechecks the server every time.

**After:**
\`\`\`makefile
server *flags:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cd sidequest-api
    cargo build \
        -p sidequest-server \
        -p sidequest-namegen \
        -p sidequest-encountergen \
        -p sidequest-loadoutgen
    exec target/debug/sidequest-server \
        --genre-packs-path {{content}} \
        {{flags}}
\`\`\`
One cargo build for all four binaries, then \`exec\` the server directly. Warm restart = nearly instant.

## Wrapper integration
\`just server\` is in the cargo-guard GUARDED set (not in BYPASS_JUST_RE), so the build still runs under the cargo-guard wrapper with:
- \`RUSTC_WRAPPER=\"\"\` (bypasses sccache contention)
- \`CARGO_HOME=<oq-2-root>/.cargo\` (clone-local registry)
- mkdir-based flock (serializes concurrent cargo invocations)
- 30s heartbeat to stderr (defeats 2-min stream watchdog)

Verified with hook test harness: \`just server\` and \`just server --headless\` both produce the wrapped command with correct env injection.

## What's NOT changed
\`just api-run\` is unchanged — still the canonical defensive path for ad-hoc invocations and is referenced by \`playtest-server\`. Only the \`server\` alias body is replaced.

## Test plan
- [x] Recipe parses (\`just --show server\`)
- [x] Hook still guards \`just server\` (test cases verified)
- [ ] Post-merge: \`just server\` cold-start (first run, full build)
- [ ] Post-merge: \`just server\` warm-restart (no source changes — confirm near-instant startup)

author: bluesentinelsec
body:
## Summary

Implements all 6 slices of the render profile system from #20.

### Slice 1: Shading modes (UNLIT/FLAT/GOURAUD/PHONG)
- sdl3d_shading_mode enum replaces the binary lighting_enabled flag
- FLAT: one PBR eval per triangle at centroid -> flat-color rasterizer
- GOURAUD: PBR eval at each vertex -> colored rasterizer with interpolation
- PHONG: existing per-fragment lit path
- set_lighting_enabled preserved as convenience wrapper

### Slice 2: Affine UV mode
- SDL3D_UV_AFFINE skips perspective correction in the lit fill loop
- Produces PS1/DOS/SNES-style texture warping on tilted surfaces

### Slice 3: Vertex snap
- Quantizes projected screen coordinates to a configurable grid
- Produces PS1-style vertex wobble/jitter

### Slice 4: Vertex fog
- SDL3D_FOG_EVAL_VERTEX computes fog per-vertex, interpolates across triangle
- Fog factor carried through Sutherland-Hodgman clipping
- Produces banded fog characteristic of PS1/N64

### Slice 5: Color quantization + Bayer dithering
- Post-shading palette reduction with 4x4 ordered Bayer dithering
- Configurable palette size (e.g. 256 for DOS aesthetic)

### Slice 6: Render profile struct + presets + runtime switching
- sdl3d_render_profile struct with all flags
- sdl3d_set_render_profile / sdl3d_get_render_profile (zero-cost struct copy)
- Named presets: sdl3d_profile_modern/ps1/n64/dos/snes
- Callers can start from a preset and override individual flags
- Runtime switching works mid-frame between draw calls

### Preset table
| Flag | Modern | PS1 | N64 | DOS | SNES |
|------|--------|-----|-----|-----|------|
| Shading | Phong | Gouraud | Gouraud | Gouraud | Flat |
| Texture | Bilinear | Nearest | Bilinear | Nearest | Nearest |
| UV mode | Perspective | Affine | Perspective | Affine | Affine |
| Fog eval | Fragment | Vertex | Vertex | Fragment | Fragment |
| Tonemap | ACES | None | None | None | None |
| Vertex snap | No | Yes (1) | No | No | No |
| Color quantize | No | No | No | Yes (256) | No |

### Testing
43 new tests total: shading mode API (12), preset validation (5 table-driven), render profile API (4), custom profiles (1), fog eval mode (2), UV mode (2), vertex snap (2), color quantization (1), runtime switching (1), PBR shading correctness (2), plus existing fog/tonemap/shadow tests.

167 existing unit tests + 60 non-fixture lighting tests all passing. clang-format clean. No new dependencies.

Closes #20

body:
### Motivation
- Improve training throughput by batching matrix operations and fusing Q/K/V projections to enable full-batch/full-sequence matmul and better use of BLAS/AVX/OpenMP optimizations.
- Make training configuration flexible via environment variables and reduce unstable training by switching to an adaptive optimizer and lower default learning rate.

### Description
- Added batched matrix routines `matmul_batch_rm` and `matmul_batch_qkv_fused` with `cblas` and OpenMP fallbacks and used them to compute Q/K/V, attention outputs, FFN and output logits in batch form.
- Converted many per-sample `matvec_rm` calls into flattened batched matmuls and reorganized intermediate tensors into flat buffers to enable vectorized and parallel computation.
- Replaced plain SGD updates with an Adam implementation (per-parameter `m`/`v`, bias correction, `adam_update` helper) and introduced optimizer state vectors for all trainable parameters.
- Exposed runtime training parameters via environment variables `JARVIS_SAMPLE_STRIDE`, `JARVIS_EPOCHS`, `JARVIS_BATCH_SIZE`, and `JARVIS_MAX_TOKENS`, adjusted defaults (`learning_rate` 0.001, `sample_stride` 2, reduced default epochs), and updated `README.md` with training notes.

### Testing
- Compiled the project with OpenMP and BLAS enabled (e.g. `g++ -O2 -fopenmp`) as a basic automated build verification and the binary built successfully.
- Ran a short smoke training run on a small dataset using the updated binary to confirm forward/backward and parameter update paths execute without crashing.  No unit test suite was added or run beyond this smoke test.

## Description

This PR tightens Clojure hybrid WAM backtracking semantics by preserving and restoring runtime construction state across choice points.

## Changes

- Save heap length, unify queue, and build stack shape when pushing Clojure WAM choice points.
- Restore those structures during backtracking, trimming heap state back to the saved choice-point boundary.
- Add a Clojure WAM smoke regression for a branch that partially constructs `f(a)`, fails, and then succeeds with `f(b)`.

## Why

The previous Clojure WAM trail work restored variable bindings on backtrack, but compound/list construction state also needs an explicit restoration boundary. This keeps the Clojure target moving toward the same WAM-quality invariants as the more mature hybrid targets, especially for clauses that build terms before failing into an alternate branch.

author: robennals
body:
## Background and Motivation

The AI tutor complained to a student that they had used the word \"burs\" in their essay — but that word never appeared in the essay. The hallucination was consistent across turns and sessions.

## Root Cause

The review-step system prompt (`src/lib/prompts.ts:48`) used the literal word `\"burs\"` as the illustrative example for \"ask about unclear words\":

> If any word … is unclear to you (e.g., \"burs\" — is that a typo? a brand? a word you don't know?), ASK…

That concrete example sits in the system prompt on every turn, and the model pattern-matched it into the student's essay as if they had written it. Classic example-contamination.

## Proposed Changes

Replace the concrete `\"burs\"` example with abstract phrasing that describes the category instead of naming a specific fake word:

> If any word, phrase, abbreviation, or reference in the draft is unclear to you — a possible typo, an unknown brand, a word you don't recognize — ASK the student…

One-line change. No behavior change to the rule itself; just removes the leaky example.

## Testing

- `pnpm lint` — passes
- `pnpm test` — 238/238 pass, coverage unchanged
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — passes

author: owezzy
body:
## Summary

- Fixes the persistent `CORS_ORIGINS must be valid JSON` deployment failure
- The "Create Hetzner environment file" step wrapped the SSH command in double quotes, causing the local shell to strip inner double quotes from JSON values before sending to the remote host
- Changed to a local heredoc piped via stdin to SSH, which preserves all quoting intact

## Root Cause

The outer double quotes in `ssh host "..."` caused bash to process inner double quotes in CORS_ORIGINS JSON, stripping them. The remote server received unquoted JSON array values.

**Fix:** Use `ssh host 'cat > file' <<'ENVEOF'` pattern — local heredoc content is never processed by a double-quoting shell layer.

## Testing

This fix can only be verified by a deployment run. Merging to main triggers the Hetzner deploy workflow.

body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>🐛 Null pointer risk in nw_server_status forcemonitor command</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Description
> 
> In `nw_server_status/server_status.py`, the `forcemonitor` command does not check if the monitor channel exists before attempting to access its permissions, leading to a potential null pointer exception.
> 
> ## Location
> 
> **File:** `nw_server_status/server_status.py`  
> **Lines:** 209-210
> 
> ## Current Code
> 
> ```python
> async def forcemonitor(self, ctx):
>     voice_channel = await self.get_guild_monitor_channel(ctx.guild)
>     bot_perms = voice_channel.permissions_for(ctx.me)  # ❌ Null pointer if voice_channel is None
> ```
> 
> ## Root Cause
> 
> The method `get_guild_monitor_channel()` can return `None` (see line 112):
> 
> ```python
> async def get_guild_monitor_channel(self, guild):
>     channel_id = await self.config.guild(guild).monitor_channel()
>     if not channel_id:
>         return None  # ← Returns None if not configured
>     
>     channel = guild.get_channel(channel_id)
>     if not channel:
>         return None  # ← Returns None if channel deleted
>     
>     return channel
> ```
> 
> However, the caller at line 209 does not check for `None` before accessing `voice_channel.permissions_for()`.
> 
> ## Impact
> 
> - **Bot crash** when `/forcemonitor` is used before a monitor channel is configured
> - `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'permissions_for'`
> - Command fails ungracefully without user-friendly error message
> 
> ## Fix Required
> 
> Add a null check before accessing the channel:
> 
> ```python
> async def forcemonitor(self, ctx):
>     voice_channel = await self.get_guild_monitor_channel(ctx.guild)
>     
>     if not voice_channel:
>         await ctx.send("❌ No monitor channel is configured. Use `[p]monitor <channel>` first.")
>         return
>     
>     bot_perms = voice_channel.permissions_for(ctx.me)
>     # ... rest of the code
> ```
> 
> ## Priority
> 
> **HIGH** - Causes bot crash and poor user experience.
> 
> ## Testing
> 
> After fixing:
> 1. Run `[p]forcemonitor` without setting up a monitor channel first
> 2. Verify you get a helpful error message instead of a crash
> 3. Set up a monitor channel, then run `[p]forcemonitor` again
> 4. Verify it works correctly

body:
## Summary

iOS 写真アプリの「非表示」機能をモデルにした、マンガの非表示機能。Face ID / パスコードで認証後に閲覧可能。

## 機能

- コンテキストメニューから「非表示にする」で一覧から非表示
- ライブラリに「非表示」セクション追加（件数表示付き）
- Face ID / Touch ID / パスコードで認証後にリスト表示
- スワイプまたはコンテキストメニューで「非表示を解除」
- 設定で「ライブラリに非表示を表示」トグル

## フィルタリング

非表示マンガは以下すべてから除外:
- ホーム画面（曜日タブ）
- ライブラリ（セクション・出版社一覧）
- 検索・キャッチアップ・ウィジェット・通知・バッジ・登録数

## 実装

- `MangaEntry.isHidden: Bool` (SwiftData lightweight migration)
- `hiddenIDs: Set<UUID>` でインメモリ管理（即時反映）
- `setHidden()` で `entry.modelContext` を使用して保存（refresh() による ModelContext 差し替え時にも正しいコンテキストで永続化）
- `BiometricAuthService` で LocalAuthentication を async/await で利用
- BackupData v11

## 根本原因と解決

`refresh()` が `self.modelContext` を新しいインスタンスに差し替えるが、HiddenEntriesView の `@State entries` に保持されたエントリオブジェクトは古い ModelContext に属したまま。`self.modelContext.save()` では変更が永続化されなかった。`entry.modelContext` で保存することで解決。

Closes #181

## Test plan

- [x] 非表示にする → 一覧から消える + 件数更新
- [x] 非表示セクション → 認証 → リスト表示
- [x] スワイプで解除 → リストから即座に消える
- [x] 戻る → ライブラリに即座に反映
- [x] 設定トグルで非表示セクションを隠せる
- [ ] テーマ切替で表示が破綻しないこと
- [ ] バックアップ・インポートで isHidden が保持されること

body:
## Summary

Full MVP for BMRS canvassing admissions across three packages plus CI.

### Backend (`/backend`)

- **Node.js + Express + TypeScript**, Prisma ORM, PostgreSQL
- **JWT auth** (HS256) with `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`, `GET /auth/me`
- **Leads**: `GET /leads` (filters: teacher, class, status, location, date range, free-text `q`), `GET/PATCH/DELETE /leads/:id`, `POST /leads`, and `POST /leads/sync` for bulk offline-queue drain with **last-write-wins** conflict resolution
- **Reminders**: full CRUD at `/reminders` plus `GET /reminders/upcoming`
- **Highlights**: `GET /school-highlights` (any authenticated user), admin-only `POST/PATCH/DELETE`
- **Admin analytics**: `GET /admin/teachers`, `GET /admin/analytics/leads-per-teacher`, `GET /admin/analytics/overview` (by-class + 30-day timeseries)
- Zod validation, central error middleware, role-based (`TEACHER` / `ADMIN`) middleware
- Seed script with deterministic admin + teacher accounts and a few demo leads/highlights
- Jest + Supertest test suite; ESLint (flat config) + `tsc --noEmit` clean

### Mobile (`/mobile`) — offline-first Flutter

- **Riverpod** DI + **Dio** API client with Bearer-token interceptor
- **SQLite** (`sqflite`) local store for leads and reminders, each row carrying `sync_status` (pending / synced / failed) + `last_sync_error`
- **Sync engine** runs every 2 min and on reconnect (`connectivity_plus`), drains pending leads via `POST /leads/sync` and reminders via `POST /reminders`; marks rows synced / failed and exposes an outcome stream the UI subscribes to
- **Screens**: Login, Home (bottom nav), Leads list with Synced / Pending / Failed badges + retry, Lead form, Reminders, School Highlights
- **Reminders** scheduled locally via `flutter_local_notifications` (fires even offline); logs also sync to backend for cross-device visibility. FCM is intentionally stubbed.
- Strict analyzer settings; `dart format` clean; unit tests for model ↔ DB row round-trips

### Web (`/web`) — React dashboard

- **Vite + React 18 + TypeScript**, React Router, TanStack Query, Recharts, axios, date-fns
- **Login** → JWT stored in `localStorage`; restored sessions are validated against `/auth/me` on load
- **Leads page** with filter bar (teacher, class, status, location, date range, search) and one-click **CSV export** (UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it cleanly)
- **Analytics page** (admin): leads-per-teacher bar chart + conversion-rate table, by-class distribution, 30-day capture timeseries
- **Highlights page**: viewer for teachers, add / remove for admins
- ESLint (flat config) + `tsc --noEmit` + `vite build` all green

### Infra

- `docker-compose.yml` for local Postgres 16
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs backend (lint / typecheck / test), web (lint / typecheck / build), and mobile (`dart format --set-exit-if-changed`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`) on every PR

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Bring up the stack locally: `docker compose up -d` → `cd backend && npm install && npx prisma migrate dev && npx prisma db seed && npm run dev` → `cd web && npm install && npm run dev` → sign in as `admin@bmrs.local` / `admin12345` and as `teacher@bmrs.local` / `teacher12345` and confirm role-gating (analytics tab + teacher filter only for admin, highlight add/delete only for admin).
- [ ] Verify offline-first on the mobile app: `cd mobile && flutter pub get && flutter run`, kill the network, create a couple of leads + a reminder (rows should badge Pending), reconnect, and watch the sync engine flip them to Synced within ~2 min (or on the pull-to-refresh).
- [ ] Sanity-check filters + CSV export on the web Leads page against what's in the DB, and confirm the analytics charts reflect the seed data.
- [ ] Decide whether to flip the default branch to `main` in repo settings (bot does not have permission) and whether to make the repo private.

### Notes

- Auth is JWT-only per your instruction; AWS Cognito / SNS / Amplify are deferred for a future session.
- Local push notifications only for MVP; FCM is wired as a stub (the reminder log still syncs to the server for a future server-side push).
- Mobile default API base URL: `http://10.0.2.2:4000` for Android emulator, `http://localhost:4000` elsewhere — override via `--dart-define=API_BASE_URL=…` if needed.
- Web base URL is `http://localhost:4000`; override with `VITE_API_BASE_URL` in `web/.env`.

author: nicksgan-belcort
body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/doctor.sh` + `/harness:doctor` command. Auto-runs at the start of `/harness:sprint`, `/harness:quick`, and after `/harness:setup`. **Blocks the pipeline on CRITICAL failures** (missing Playwright MCP, missing Context7 MCP, Node < 20, plugin not installed, writable-dir issues) and prints copy-paste fix commands so the user never has to google.

This is purely additive — no existing file behaviour changes except that sprint/quick/setup now run doctor as step 0.

## 摘要

新增 `scripts/doctor.sh` 脚本与 `/harness:doctor` 命令。会在 `/harness:sprint`(完整流水线)、`/harness:quick`(快速模式)、以及 `/harness:setup`(初始安装)启动时自动运行。**当发现 CRITICAL(致命)问题时会阻止流水线继续执行**(例如 Playwright MCP 未安装、Context7 MCP 未注册、Node 版本低于 20、插件未安装、目录不可写等),并直接输出可复制粘贴的修复命令 —— 使用者不需要再去 Google 查找解决办法。

本 PR 是纯增量更新,不改变任何既有文件的行为,只是在 sprint/quick/setup 流程最前面加入一个 doctor(诊断)关卡。

---

## The problem this solves

A real user report: a sprint failed in a confusing way because the Playwright MCP wasn't installed. The harness happily dispatched the Planner and Generator (which don't need Playwright), then crashed when the Evaluator tried to open a browser. The user only learned about the missing MCP *after* burning tokens on a planning pass that became useless.

The root cause is that the pipeline assumed its environment was ready. It checked nothing. The harness docs listed the MCPs under "Required" but there was no runtime guard — the first agent that needed a missing dependency would fail partway through a task.

## 本 PR 解决的问题

真实用户反馈:有一次 sprint(完整流水线)运行失败,原因是 Playwright MCP 没装。但 harness 本身没意识到这个问题,照样派出 Planner(规划代理)和 Generator(生成代理)执行 —— 这两个代理不需要 Playwright。等流水线跑到 Evaluator(评估代理)尝试打开浏览器时才崩溃。使用者直到白白花掉规划阶段的 token 之后,才发现原来是缺了 MCP。

根本原因是:流水线假设环境已经就绪,什么检查都没做。文档虽然在 "Required(必需)" 一节列出了所有 MCP,但运行时没有任何守卫。第一个用到缺失依赖的代理会在任务进行到一半时突然失败。

---

## What this PR does

### New files

- **`plugins/harness/scripts/doctor.sh`** (executable) — the actual preflight logic. Verifies:
  - **CRITICAL** (blocks pipeline on failure): `claude` CLI, `git`, Node ≥ 20, `npx`, Context7 MCP registered, Playwright MCP registered, harness plugin present, global rules in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, project directory writable.
  - **RECOMMENDED** (warns only): git working tree clean, inside a git repo, `frontend-design` / `security-guidance` / `agentlint` optional plugins.
  - Every failure prints the exact install command. Supports `--strict`, `--json`, `--quiet` flags.
  - Exit codes: `0` = pass, `1` = critical failure (block), `2` = script error.
- **`plugins/harness/commands/doctor.md`** — the `/harness:doctor` command wrapper. Explains when to run it manually vs. when it runs automatically.

### Modified files

- **`plugins/harness/commands/sprint.md`** — adds **Step 0: DOCTOR** before Planner dispatch. Exit code != 0 → stop, show report, do NOT dispatch any subagent.
- **`plugins/harness/commands/quick.md`** — same Step 0 gate.
- **`plugins/harness/commands/setup.md`** — after `install-rules.sh`, runs doctor so users see their environment status immediately, not at 3am mid-build.
- **`plugins/harness/skills/harness/SKILL.md`** — adds `/harness:doctor` row to the commands table.

## 本 PR 具体改动

### 新增文件

- **`plugins/harness/scripts/doctor.sh`**(可执行) —— 真正的环境检查逻辑。检查项:
  - **CRITICAL(致命,失败即阻断)**:`claude` CLI、`git`、Node ≥ 20、`npx`、Context7 MCP 已注册、Playwright MCP 已注册、harness 插件存在、`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` 已安装全局规则、项目目录可写。
  - **RECOMMENDED(建议,仅警告)**:git 工作区干净、处于 git 仓库中、`frontend-design` / `security-guidance` / `agentlint` 可选插件。
  - 每一项失败都会直接输出可复制粘贴的安装命令。支持 `--strict`、`--json`、`--quiet` 参数。
  - 退出码:`0` = 全部通过,`1` = 有致命失败(阻断),`2` = 脚本本身出错。
- **`plugins/harness/commands/doctor.md`** —— 对应的 `/harness:doctor` 命令文档。说明何时手动运行、何时自动触发。

### 修改文件

- **`plugins/harness/commands/sprint.md`** —— 在 Planner(规划代理)派发之前加入 **Step 0: DOCTOR(诊断)**。退出码 != 0 → 立即停止,输出报告,不派发任何子代理(subagent)。
- **`plugins/harness/commands/quick.md`** —— 同样加入 Step 0 的诊断关卡。
- **`plugins/harness/commands/setup.md`** —— 在 `install-rules.sh` 之后立刻运行 doctor,用户第一时间就能看到环境状态,而不是凌晨 3 点 build 到一半才发现。
- **`plugins/harness/skills/harness/SKILL.md`** —— 命令表格新增 `/harness:doctor` 一行。

---

## Test plan

- [x] Run `bash plugins/harness/scripts/doctor.sh` on a fresh macOS/Linux shell — verify CRITICAL items detect correctly
- [x] Verify plugin-path detection works for: `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, `~/.claude/skills/harness/`, `~/.claude/plugins/*/skills/harness/`, and dev-checkout script-relative path
- [x] Verify `--quiet` suppresses output on success and prints on failure
- [x] Verify `--json` output is valid JSON
- [x] Manually uninstall Playwright MCP (`claude mcp remove playwright`), rerun doctor, confirm exit 1 + correct fix command printed
- [ ] Reviewer: run inside your own harness environment and check the report matches reality

## 测试计划

- [x] 在全新的 macOS/Linux shell 下运行 `bash plugins/harness/scripts/doctor.sh`,验证各 CRITICAL 项检查正确
- [x] 验证插件路径检测覆盖所有场景:`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`、`~/.claude/skills/harness/`、`~/.claude/plugins/*/skills/harness/`、以及 dev checkout(开发仓库检出)时以脚本相对路径定位
- [x] 验证 `--quiet` 在成功时静默、失败时输出报告
- [x] 验证 `--json` 输出为合法 JSON 格式
- [x] 手动卸载 Playwright MCP(`claude mcp remove playwright`),重新运行 doctor,确认退出码 1 且输出正确的修复命令
- [ ] 审阅者(reviewer): 在你自己的 harness 环境中运行,检查报告是否与实际情况一致

---

## References

The design of this check is grounded in two Anthropic publications plus prior-art patterns from the community:

- **[Harness design for long-running application development](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)** (Rajasekaran, 2026) — emphasises that harness reliability depends on the surrounding tooling being predictable. When the Evaluator's Playwright MCP isn't responding, the whole Generator-Evaluator loop degrades to a self-review, which the same article calls out as a known failure mode ("models praise own work").
- **[Trustworthy agents in practice](https://www.anthropic.com/research/trustworthy-agents)** (Anthropic, 2026) — recommends catching misconfiguration with explicit up-front checks rather than silent runtime failure, consistent with Anthropic's broader principle of surfacing uncertainty early.
- **[GitHub Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)** — its `/speckit.constitution` and preflight steps demonstrate that a hard gate at workflow entry prevents a large class of confusing mid-flow failures.
- **[Superpowers plugin](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)** — uses an explicit "orient" phase at the start of each subagent cycle. Our doctor extends this from per-agent orientation to per-pipeline orientation.
- **[BMAD Method](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD)** — its getting-started flow insists on environment verification before any agent work, which matches this PR's design.

## 参考文献

本 PR 的设计基于两篇 Anthropic 官方论文与社区已有实践:

- **[Harness design for long-running application development(长运行应用的 harness 设计)](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps)**(Rajasekaran, 2026) —— 明确指出 harness(harness 引擎)的可靠性依赖于周边工具链的稳定性。当 Evaluator(评估代理)的 Playwright MCP 无响应时,整个 Generator(生成代理)↔ Evaluator 循环会退化成"自我评审",而同一篇文章把这一点列为已知失败模式("models praise own work",模型倾向给自己的产出打高分)。
- **[Trustworthy agents in practice(可信代理实践)](https://www.anthropic.com/research/trustworthy-agents)**(Anthropic, 2026) —— 建议通过显式的前置检查捕获配置问题,而不是依赖运行时的沉默失败。这与 Anthropic 一贯倡导的"尽早暴露不确定性"原则一致。
- **[GitHub Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)** —— 其 `/speckit.constitution` 以及工作流启动前的检查步骤表明,在工作流入口设置硬性关卡(hard gate)能避免大量流程中段的诡异失败。
- **[Superpowers 插件(Superpowers plugin)](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)** —— 每个 subagent(子代理)循环开头都会有一个显式的 "orient(定位)" 阶段。本 PR 的 doctor 把这种单个代理级别的定位,扩展到整个 pipeline(流水线)级别。
- **[BMAD Method](https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD)** —— 其 getting-started(入门)流程坚持在任何代理工作之前先做环境验证,这与本 PR 的理念一致。

---

This is PR 1 of 10 in the v1.3 series. Subsequent PRs will address:
subagent hook isolation, CLAUDE.md context bloat, structured amendment flow (`/harness:clarify`, `/harness:amend`), mid-build steering (`/harness:steer`), phase rewind, eva

This PR adds support for device haptics as force feedback (rumble) and also sends controller gyro from device gyro and accelerometer.

- Added `deviceHaptics` and `deviceGyroMode` to `TemporarySettings`
- Persisted both settings through `NSUserDefaults` / `DataManager`
- Added settings UI for haptics and gyro in `SettingsViewController`
- Updated `HapticContext` so it can handle device haptics in addition to controller haptics

author: dpanman
body:
## Summary

- `selectRange` walked from anchor to target through the flat `photos[]` array. Because `photos[]` is sorted globally by shot time, two cameras that shot at overlapping times end up **interleaved** in that array even though each belongs to its own group — so a shift-click within camera A picked up every interleaved camera B photo sitting between anchor and target.
- The fix walks the **active group's own `indices`** instead. If the prior anchor doesn't live in the active group, the click falls back to a plain toggle and the new cell becomes the next anchor.
- New flow test: click in group 0, jump to a different camera's group, shift-click — expect 2 selected (not hundreds).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 15 parser + 46 grouping + 7 exif + 35 flow, all green
- [x] New regression case: "shift-click does not leak across groups" passes
- [x] Existing within-group shift-click ("shift-click range selects 10") still passes

body:
## Summary

Second follow-up from the review in #11 — addresses §3 (agents) P0/P1 findings.

**What changed**

- Every one of the 20 agents in `bettercallclaude/agents/` now declares a `model:` field in its frontmatter. Previously none did, so cost/latency inherited whatever the caller's current model happened to be — not reproducible for users, and unaligned with Anthropic's subagent guidance.
- `orchestrator.md` and `briefing.md` gained the `Task` tool. Both of them describe multi-agent workflows in their prompts (spawning `swiss-legal-advocate`, `swiss-legal-adversary`, `swiss-judicial-analyst`, etc.) but without `Task` they literally cannot spawn subagents — the prompt described behaviour the agent could not execute.

**Model assignments**

| Tier   | Agents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| opus   | `orchestrator`, `judicial`                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| haiku  | `citation`, `summarizer`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| sonnet | `adversary`, `advocate`, `briefing`, `cantonal`, `compliance`, `corporate`, `data-protection`, `drafter`, `fiscal`, `procedure`, `prompt-engineer`, `realestate`, `researcher`, `risk`, `strategist`, `translator` (16 default agents)                   |

Rationale:
- `opus` for the two agents doing high-stakes coordination/synthesis (orchestrator plans multi-agent pipelines; judicial delivers calibrated probabilistic synthesis where miscalibration has real cost).
- `haiku` for mechanical consolidation (citation formatter, summarizer/length-budgeter) — cheap and fast, no reasoning required.
- `sonnet` for everything else — the doctrinal research/drafting/strategy default.

Pick a different tier later by editing the single `model:` line in a given agent file.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

Risk: **green** — frontmatter-only change, no code paths modified.

- [ ] Spot-check `bettercallclaude/agents/orchestrator.md` and `bettercallclaude/agents/briefing.md` — the `tools:` list now includes `Task` at the top.
- [ ] Decide whether the `opus`/`haiku`/`sonnet` split above matches your cost/quality preference. Easy to retune: each agent has a single `model:` line.
- [ ] In Claude Code, delegate to `swiss-legal-workflow-orchestrator` with a pipeline that requires spawning subagents (e.g. advocate+adversary+judicial) and confirm it can now actually dispatch them via the Task tool.

### Notes

- No changes to `description:` wording or other fields — those fall under §3 P1 and can ship later if desired.
- Validate Plugin Structure CI step does not enforce a `model:` field, so no CI update needed.
- Next up: `fix/repository-naming-collision` (§7, PR C).

body:
Добавлен отдельный admin-only интерфейс для управления пользователями: просмотр списка, создание, редактирование и удаление операторов/администраторов. Решение закрывает сценарии из задачи, включая запрет на удаление собственного аккаунта и отображение даты создания пользователей. - **Маршруты и серверная логика (`app.py`)** - Добавлены маршруты: - `GET /admin/users` — список пользователей - `GET/POST /admin/users/add` — создание пользователя - `GET/POST /admin/users//edit` — редактирование пользователя - `POST /admin/users//delete` — удаление пользователя - Валидации: - обязательность полей при создании - уникальность `username` (с исключением текущего пользователя при edit) - защита от удаления собственного аккаунта - ограничение роли значениями `admin|operator` - Пароль при создании/обновлении сохраняется в хеше через `generate_password_hash`. - **UI: админ-шаблоны** - Добавлены: - `templates/admin/users.html` — таблица пользователей, роли, дата создания, действия - `templates/admin/add_user.html` — форма создания - `templates/admin/edit_user.html` — форма редактирования (пароль опционален) - Добавлены flash-уведомления для успешных и ошибочных сценариев. - **Навигация (`templates/base.html`)** - Для администратора добавлен пункт бокового меню: - `👥 Управление пользователями` → `url_for('admin_users')` - Подсветка active-состояния для всех `/admin/users*` страниц. - **Пример серверной части** ```python @app.route("/admin/users//delete", methods=["POST"]) @admin_required def admin_delete_user(user_id): user = User.query.get_or_404(user_id) if user.id == session.get("user_id"): flash("Нельзя удалить свой аккаунт!", "danger") return redirect(url_for("admin_users")) username = user.username db.session.delete(user) db.session.commit() flash(f"Пользователь {username} удален!", "success") return redirect(url_for("admin_users")) ``` ### Screenshot ![Admin users panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/643c42a9-80c6-4a21-b4db-e6cc61b58223)
Original prompt ## Добавить админ-панель для управления пользователями **Требуется создать интерфейс для администратора по управлению операторами:** ### 1. **Маршруты (app.py):** ```python # Список пользователей @app.route("/admin/users") @admin_required def admin_users(): users = User.query.all() return render_template("admin/users.html", users=users) # Добавление нового пользователя @app.route("/admin/users/add", methods=["GET", "POST"]) @admin_required def admin_add_user(): if request.method == "POST": username = request.form.get("username", "").strip() password = request.form.get("password", "").strip() role = request.form.get("role", "operator") if not username or not password: flash("Заполните все поля!", "danger") return redirect(url_for("admin_add_user")) if User.query.filter_by(username=username).first(): flash("Пользователь уже существует!", "danger") return redirect(url_for("admin_add_user")) user = User(username=username, password=password, role=role) db.session.add(user) db.session.commit() flash(f"Пользователь {username} создан!", "success") return redirect(url_for("admin_users")) return render_template("admin/add_user.html") # Редактирование пользователя @app.route("/admin/users//edit", methods=["GET", "POST"]) @admin_required def admin_edit_user(user_id): user = User.query.get_or_404(user_id) if request.method == "POST": username = request.form.get("username", "").strip() password = request.form.get("password", "").strip() role = request.form.get("role", "operator") if not username: flash("Заполните имя пользователя!", "danger") return redirect(url_for("admin_edit_user", user_id=user_id)) # Проверить уникальность username (кроме текущего) if username != user.username and User.query.filter_by(username=username).first(): flash("Имя пользователя уже используется!", "danger") return redirect(url_for("admin_edit_user", user_id=user_id)) user.username = username if password: # Только если введен новый пароль user.password = password user.role = role db.session.commit() flash("Пользователь обновлен!", "success") return redirect(url_for("admin_users")) return render_template("admin/edit_user.html", user=user) # Удаление пользователя @app.route("/admin/users//delete", methods=["POST"]) @admin_required def admin_delete_user(user_id): user = User.query.get_or_404(user_id) # Нельзя удалить себя if user.id == session.get("user_id"): flash("Нельзя удалить свой аккаунт!", "danger") return redirect(url_for("admin_users")) username = user.username db.session.delete(user) db.session.commit() flash(f"Пользователь {username} удален!", "success") return redirect(url_for("admin_users")) ``` ### 2. **Шаблон: templates/admin/users.html** ```html {% extends "base.html" %} {% block content %}

author: workshop-maybe
body:
Closes #43.

## Summary

The public XP activity dashboard. Two user-facing surfaces (a landing strip on `/` and a dedicated `/xp/activity` page) surface current contribution activity and tell the multi-project trajectory story. A shared email-capture form collects interest in the future "post your own project" feature.

v1's job is **trajectory declaration**, not social-proof of current momentum. The stats are a supporting signal; the declared future ("contribute now → earn XP → post your own project") is the load-bearing claim.

## What's in this PR

**New code (7 files):**

- `src/lib/xp-activity.ts` — server-only aggregation. Mirrors `xp-leaderboard.ts`: gateway fetch with 10s timeout, commitments-first + submissions-join fallback, accepted-decision filter. Returns contributors / tasksCompleted / xpReleased / xpTotalSupply / pendingReviews / up to 10 recentAccepted entries.
- `src/types/xp-activity.ts` — shared types.
- `src/app/api/xp-activity/route.ts` — thin GET wrapper, matches `/api/xp-leaderboard`.
- `src/app/api/project-posting-waitlist/route.ts` — email-only POST: zod validation, Resend-key guard, bot honeypot, in-memory per-IP rate limit (5/min, best-effort per-instance), dual Resend send (internal + confirmation).
- `src/components/xp/project-posting-waitlist-form.tsx` — shared form with `variant: "inline" | "expanded"`, full state machine (idle/submitting/success/error), sessionStorage-backed already-submitted suppression, mobile stack.
- `src/app/(app)/xp/activity/page.tsx` + `activity-content.tsx` — the dedicated public page.
- `src/app/page-content.tsx` (new) — holds the existing landing client logic plus the new activity strip.

**Modified (4 files):**

- `src/app/page.tsx` — restructured from `"use client"` to an async server component. Prefetches activity stats into React Query via `HydrateClient`. Existing client logic (`LandingHero` / `FirstLoginCard` conditional, mint-redirect state) moved verbatim to `page-content.tsx`.
- `src/config/routes.ts` — adds `PUBLIC_ROUTES.activity`.
- `src/app/(app)/xp/xp-content.tsx` — adds Activity CTA alongside the existing Leaderboard CTA (now a 2-column grid on `/xp`).

## How it maps to the requirements

| Req | Satisfied by |
|---|---|
| R1 (3 landing metrics + near-zero graceful rendering) | `page-content.tsx` strip |
| R2 (tagline, no numbers) | `page-content.tsx` copy block |
| R3 (Notify me + See all activity links) | inline form variant + `Link` to `/xp/activity` |
| R4 (new public route sibling to leaderboard) | `src/app/(app)/xp/activity/` |
| R5 (hero + metrics + pending + recent list + "What's next" + form + untrusted-string handling) | `activity-content.tsx` |
| R6 (endpoint with zod + honeypot + rate limit + Resend key guard + disclosure) | `project-posting-waitlist/route.ts` + form privacy note |
| R7 (shared component, states, mobile) | `project-posting-waitlist-form.tsx` |
| R8 (server prefetch + HydrateClient + page.tsx split) | Both server pages + the two content files |
| R9 (branch + PR + no CC attribution, dcm check) | This PR + post-merge DM to dcm |

## Not in v1 (per plan)

- Time-series charts, per-task drill-down, per-contributor history pages.
- Assignment 2 content, project-token mint flow, specific XP threshold, specific ADA cost — this PR only tells the story.
- Database persistence of waitlist emails — inbox-based via Resend.
- Automated bulk announcement when the feature ships.
- Verified Resend sender domain (flagged for pre-volume follow-up).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes (modulo the two pre-existing unrelated errors: stale `.next` types for `/transparency` → `/project-wallet` rename, `resend` module not installed locally).
- [x] Verified the landing `page.tsx` restructure preserves the existing mint-redirect flow by moving the body verbatim into `page-content.tsx`.
- [ ] Vercel preview: `/` loads, hero fills viewport, scroll reveals activity strip with 3 stat numbers and the inline form. Form reveals on "Notify me" click; submitting a real email triggers both Resend emails (internal + confirmation); error path works with invalid email.
- [ ] Vercel preview: `/xp/activity` loads with server-prefetched data (no client loading spinner), all four stat cards render, recent-accepted table renders (or the empty-state placeholder if zero activity), "Where XP is going" block shows the three-step trajectory, expanded form works.
- [ ] Vercel preview: navigate `/xp` → click Activity CTA → lands on `/xp/activity`. Back → returns to `/xp`.
- [ ] Vercel preview: mobile viewport (375px) — landing strip stacks, recent table is scrollable, form stacks vertically.
- [ ] Confirm dcm is OK with the single-project-for-now framing before merge (R9 acceptance step).

## Release tie-in

This is the v0.0.2 capstone feature. Release notes + tag flow from `docs/plans/2026-04-18-005-release-v0-0-2-plan.md` pick up after this merges.

## Plan

Full plan at `docs/plans/2026-04-18-006-feat-xp-activity-dashboard-plan.md`. Origin requirements at `docs/brainstorms/2026-04-18-xp-activity-dashboard-requirements.md`.

author: elares
body:
Closes #82 (Option C — estimated multiplier; Option A deferred to follow-up)

## Summary
Adds a treatment-specific LP overshoot multiplier to the immune coupling model so that SDT/PDT dead cells release ~2× more DAMPs per cell than RSL3, reflecting the biological reality that the autocatalytic LP cascade continues post-threshold for high-ROS treatments.

## Why Option C instead of Option A
The issue recommended Option A (modify ferroptosis-core to let LP accumulate post-death). I chose Option C (estimated multiplier in sim-tme only) because:
- **Zero ferroptosis-core changes** — no ground truth regeneration, no calibration update, no test changes
- **1 file changed, 20 lines** — vs Option A's 3+ files and hours of verification
- **Same class of parameter** as immune_kill_rate (0.02), damp_clearance_rate (0.03), and every other immune parameter — all are documented estimates
- Option A remains a valid follow-up when emergent LP dynamics are needed

## Biology (cross-referenced against books/)
- Autocatalytic LP cascade continues post-threshold (Biology2e Ch.7-8: chain reaction propagation)
- SDT: high exogenous ROS → fast LP accumulation → cascade continues ~3 steps → LP reaches ~20 (2× threshold)
- RSL3: slow GPX4-dependent LP accumulation → minimal momentum → LP reaches ~10.5 (1.05× threshold)

## Results (O2 gradient λ=120μm)

| Metric | Before overshoot | After (2× SDT) | Change |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|--------|
| SDT immune kills (no anti-PD1) | 297 | 539 | +81% |
| SDT immune kills (anti-PD1) | 781 | 1,520 | +95% |
| RSL3 immune kills | 2 | 2 | unchanged |
| SDT overall | 88.0% | 88.1% | +0.1% |
| SDT + anti-PD1 | 88.3% | 88.7% | +0.4% |

## Verification
```bash
cargo test -p ferroptosis-core --lib   # 19/19 unchanged
cargo run --release --bin sim-tme      # immune kills increased for SDT
cargo run --release --bin sim-original  # bitwise identical (zero core changes)
```

body:
## Summary

Add `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` to the base `claude` command in `call_claude.py`. Drops the harness-injected dynamic system prompt content (cwd context, harness metadata, periodic operational reminders) from forked subagents.

Direct token reduction per call is small (~500-2000 tokens). The bigger win is **prompt cache reuse**: with the dynamic block removed, the stable prefix below it (agent prompts, MCP tool schemas, plugin config — plausibly 20-40k tokens) can be matched as a cache prefix across the many subagent dispatches in a designer run, billing as cache reads (~10× cheaper) instead of full write rate every time.

Cache benefit only materializes if the rest of the prefix is also stable. PR #234 (drop `additionalContext` injection) is a precondition for this flag's cache savings to fully land. Worth merging this after #234.

## Test plan

author: syndicalt
body:
## Summary

Ships the public read-only demo tenant (#229). Anonymous visitors click `/demo` → get a short-lived read-only session on pre-seeded `t_demo` → land on `/dashboard` with a non-dismissible "demo mode" banner. Unblocks the landing-page "See it live →" CTA that shipped in PR #231 as a 404.

## How it works

1. `GET /demo` creates a 1-hour read-only session bound to `u_demo_visitor`, sets the cookie, redirects to `DASHBOARD_URL/dashboard?demo=1`.
2. Tenant middleware flags the session as read-only via a new WeakMap on the request.
3. `createReadOnlyMiddleware()` (mounted on `/v1/*` and `/v1/chat/completions`) refuses `POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE` with `403 demo_read_only`. Reads / exports / chart renders all pass through untouched.
4. `DemoBanner` (client component wired into the dashboard layout) reads `isDemo` from `AuthContext` and renders a sticky strip.
5. Scheduler job `demo-reseed` wipes and reseeds `t_demo` nightly; gated by `PROVARA_DEMO_ENABLED=true`.

## Seed narrative

The seed data is crafted to showcase every feature on first visit:

- 200 requests + cost logs across 30 days, 5 cells, 3 providers, 3 users, 2 API tokens
- ~67 judge feedback rows — weighted toward 3–5, with one cell (`coding+complex`) systematically low to drive the regression narrative
- 1 unresolved regression event on that cell with a -1.4 delta
- 2 active cost migrations with real reported savings (`$28.50` and `$14.70`/mo)
- Budget at 75% of a $500 cap with `[50, 75]` thresholds already fired
- Weight snapshots with a `balanced → cost` profile change mid-window so `/v1/spend/drift` returns a real event

Enterprise subscription so every tier-gated view unlocks.

## Ops action alongside merge

On Railway → `provara-gateway` → Variables:
- Add `PROVARA_DEMO_ENABLED=true`

Redeploy. The `demo-reseed` job fires after 30s on first start and populates `t_demo`. After that, `/demo` works.

## Tests

- 6 new tests (3 for seed idempotency + shape, 3 for middleware behavior)
- Full suite 517/517

- `packages/db/src/schema.ts` + migration `0035_luxuriant_texas_twister.sql` — `sessions.read_only`

author: jiu-xiao
body:
This change adds project-level constexpr generation to `xrobot_gen_main` and tightens the generator's configuration parsing so invalid YAML and malformed config structures fail with clear errors instead of leaking Python tracebacks or silently degrading into incomplete output.

Before this change, project code could only pass literal values or ad-hoc string expressions through `User/xrobot.yaml`. That made it awkward to express strongly typed compile-time configuration shared across modules, especially for template arguments and aggregate constructor arguments. In the same area, the generator's parser had several edge cases that were unsafe in practice: nested manifest YAML could be flattened by indentation loss, top-level non-mapping YAML could reach deep code paths and crash with `AttributeError`, and malformed `global_settings` / `modules` entries could be silently ignored or fail unclearly.

The root cause was that `GenerateMain.py` only handled simple value formatting and assumed a mostly well-formed config tree. It had no project-level constexpr emission path, no dedicated config loader with structural validation, and manifest parsing stripped indentation from lines before handing them to YAML parsing.

The fix adds a project-level `constexprs` / `constexpr_includes` surface to `User/xrobot.yaml`. When present, `xrobot_gen_main` now emits `xrobot_constexpr.hpp`, and both `constructor_args` and `template_args` can reference generated symbols using `{constexpr: Name}`. The generator remains in a single `GenerateMain.py` file, keeps the existing CLI entrypoint, and the package version is bumped to `0.2.9`. README usage was updated to match the real current behavior, including the single-file generator, the `User/xrobot.yaml` layout, and the `xrobot_setup` flow.

This PR also hardens config parsing behavior. Manifest parsing now preserves indentation so nested YAML structures survive round-tripping. Config loading validates that the top-level YAML is a mapping, and generation now validates `global_settings`, each `modules[*]` entry, and per-module `constructor_args` / `template_args` mappings explicitly. On CLI failure paths, these validation errors are surfaced as readable command-line errors instead of raw stack traces.

Validation was done in three layers. First, `python3 -m compileall src/xrobot/GenerateMain.py` was run on the final branch state. Second, an ad-hoc parsing regression and boundary verification matrix was executed with 22 passing checks, covering valid generation, malformed YAML, top-level type errors, malformed module entries, invalid constexpr references, and CLI error surfaces. Third, a local multi-module smoke run exercised real generator flows with mock `BlinkLED`, `WebotsCamera`, `ArmorDetector`, and `PoseFilter` modules, covering manifest-driven default config generation, nested manifest args, config-driven module discovery, `@instance` references, and the new `constexprs` / `constexpr_includes` emission path. Together these checks verify both the new feature and the generator's failure behavior on malformed input.

## Summary by Sourcery

Add project-level constexpr header generation to xrobot_gen_main and harden configuration parsing and CLI error handling.

New Features:
- Introduce project-level constexpr and constexpr_includes configuration in User/xrobot.yaml to generate an xrobot_constexpr.hpp header and support {constexpr: Name} references in constructor and template arguments.

Bug Fixes:
- Tighten YAML and config loading so non-mapping top-level configs, invalid modules lists, or malformed entries raise clear errors instead of silently degrading or crashing with tracebacks.
- Make modules extraction and main generation robust to invalid module declarations by enforcing proper types and required fields and surfacing errors via CLI exit codes.

Enhancements:
- Preserve manifest YAML indentation during parsing to support nested structures.
- Validate overall config structure, global_settings, modules entries, and per-module constructor_args/template_args as mappings with clearer requirements for names and ids.
- Ensure template arguments preserve raw type-expression strings while still supporting constexpr references.
- Improve xrobot_gen_main and xrobot_setup documentation to reflect the single-file generator, updated config layout, and constexpr workflow.
- Update xrobot_setup behavior and README examples to describe the current workspace bootstrap flow and CLI output.

Build:
- Bump package version to 0.2.9 in pyproject.toml to publish the new generator behavior.

Documentation:
- Document the User/xrobot.yaml configuration schema including global_settings, modules, and project-level constexprs, plus updated usage examples for xrobot_gen_main and xrobot_setup.

author: osamu620
body:
## Summary
Root causes #1 + #2 from the JPIP-viewer slowness investigation (follow-up to #284).

**Before:**
- `jpip_begin_frame()` zeroed the entire accumulated `DataBinSet` on every fetch — every pan was a cold start, and the server had to resend precincts the client already held.
- A fresh `openhtj2k_decoder` was constructed per frame, re-doing SIZ/COD/QCD marker parsing, tile-tree allocation, codeblock tagtree init, and line-decode ring-buffer setup on every viewport change.

**After:**
- `jpip_begin_frame()` is a no-op (ABI-compat stub). `DataBinSet` accumulates across frames; `jpip_reset_cache()` added for explicit disconnect.
- `JpipContext` holds a persistent `openhtj2k_decoder` with `enable_single_tile_reuse(true)`. Sparse codestreams reassembled from the same `CodestreamIndex` have byte-identical main headers → the reuse cache hits from frame #2 onward.
- `invoke_line_based_stream_reuse()` actually exercises the cached tile tree.
- `dirty` flag lets both `end_frame` paths skip reassembly when no new data-bins arrived since the last decode.

Native-side code is unchanged (whole file is under `#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__`). Both WASM JPIP targets (`libopen_htj2k_jpip` and `libopen_htj2k_jpip_mt_simd`) build clean locally.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open `/jpip_viewer?debug=1`, connect, pan around a gigapixel source. Second and later pans to newly-visited viewports should log substantially lower `decode=` ms than the first frame (reuse cache hitting).
- [ ] Pan back to a previously-visited viewport with no new data-bins arriving → `lastFetchKey` short-circuits the request entirely (already covered by PR #284).
- [ ] Verify against a Part 1 source (not only HT) that single-tile reuse doesn't corrupt output — e.g. via `ctest -R "^dec_p1_"` on a local native build for regressions in the shared decoder.
- [ ] Reconnect flow: disconnect + connect → server serves a fresh codestream; confirm no stale cache artifacts (add `jpip_reset_cache` wire-up to viewer if needed — not in this PR yet; currently create_context produces a fresh handle on reconnect).

author: unclesaurus
body:
Closes part of #628. Lands the routing pipeline and recall tools; LLM-powered extractors and typed concepts from the linker are documented follow-ups.

## Scoping decision

The ticket mentioned three "new tables" — \`interactions\`, \`decisions\`, \`action_items\`. After discussion we scoped honestly against what the graph already holds:

| Ticket "new table" | Actual home in this PR |
|---|---|
| \`interactions\` | **No new table.** Enriches existing \`mentions\` edge properties with sentiment + topics. |
| \`decisions\` | **Graph node type \`decision\`.** Mirrors the skill pattern from #643. |
| \`action_items\` | **SQL table** with indexes for status/date/assignee query shapes. |

## 3-pass person resolver

Exact → fuzzy first-name → collision detection. Ambiguous matches are flagged \`status=pending\` rather than silently merging. Covered by the critical \`test_does_not_auto_merge_on_collision\` test.

## New tools on MemoryFeature

- \`recall_action_items(status, days, assignee_concept_id, limit)\`
- \`update_action_item(item_id, status, due_date, assignee_concept_id)\`
- \`recall_decisions(limit)\`
- \`recall_interactions(person_concept_id, limit)\`
- \`confirm_person_match(message_id, mentioned_label, concept_id)\`

All validate inputs and return structured errors for bad types/ranges.

## Pipeline

\`SchemaRouter\` runs after \`AssociativeLinker\` in \`process_message\`. Best-effort — a failure in one lane (e.g. action_items DB write) doesn't block the others. Privacy gated: skipped when \`skip_schema_routing=True\` in metadata; EPHEMERAL/ISOLATED agents never reach this code path.

## Tests

- **26** schema router tests (extractors, 3-pass resolver, orchestration, best-effort lane isolation, pending match surfacing)
- **17** recall tool tests (CRUD, input validation, cross-agent isolation)
- Full unit suite: **3832 passed**, 25 skipped (+68)

## Doc updates

[MEMORY_SYSTEM.md](../blob/main/docs/architecture/MEMORY_SYSTEM.md) decision matrix extended with 3 new rows + a section on the routing boundaries and 3-pass resolver.

### Motivation
- Replace the previous schema-heavy bounded generator with a GPT-4.1-first coding-agent proposer that can select evidence and perform bounded, verifiable code edits in a sandboxed workspace.  
- Give the proposer controlled tool access to archive / traces / code so it can choose which evidence to inspect rather than relying on a single prebuilt summary.  
- Make candidate generation diff-safe, branch-safe and test-safe: one candidate per invocation, traceable diffs, smoke-tests and strict consistency checks; fail-fast and avoid polluting the archive.  

### Description
- Added a controlled tooling layer `proposer/agent_tools.py` implementing `ProposerToolbox` with APIs: `list_harnesses`, `read_harness_spec`, `read_harness_code`, `diff_harnesses`, `list_runs`, `read_run_metadata`, `search_traces`, `read_trace_snippet`, `validate_candidate`, and `smoke_check_candidate`.  
- Switched proposer to a GPT-4.1-first agent: `TYPEFLY_PROPOSER_MODEL` defaults to `gpt-4.1` and proposer will fail-fast if a GPT model is requested but `OPENAI_API_KEY` is missing (unless `allow_fallback_heuristic` is explicitly enabled). (`proposer/propose_candidate.py`).  
- Made proposer a coding-agent workflow that: reads archive/index, exposes tool-discovery context to the LLM, chooses 1–3 harnesses to inspect, generates edits by file (starting from a parent snapshot), runs smoke checks (`py_compile`), validates consistency, writes `parent_diff.patch` and `runtime_metadata` (`parent_commit`, `changed_files`, `candidate_branch_hint`, `diff_path`) and only accepts the candidate if all guards pass. No auto-push/merge. (`proposer/propose_candidate.py`, `proposer/evaluate_candidate.py`).  
- Strengthened consistency and sandbox wiring: introduced `TRACKED_CONTRACT_FILES` and required `changed_files` in the proposal contract; runtime-effect detection can be extended via `validator_rules.runtime_effect_modules()`; candidate must modify at least one runtime-effect sandbox module (e.g. `state_features.py`, `trigger_logic.py`, `prompt_composer.py`). (`proposer/consistency.py`, `proposer/registry.py`).  
- Persisted and documented diff/manifest metadata: candidate `spec.json` includes `manifest` and `runtime_metadata` (lineage, active sandbox modules, evidence pointers, parent commit, changed files, diff path), and each candidate writes `parent_diff.patch` for review/rollback without automatic git operations. (`proposer/propose_candidate.py`, `proposer/README.md`).  
- Output contract / prompts updated to be code-editing friendly and require `changed_files` in addition to the previous contract fields. (`proposer/prompts.py`).  
- Tests and docs: added `proposer/agent_tools.py` tests (`test/test_proposer_agent_tools.py`), updated consistency tests, and updated `proposer/README.md` to document kept/deprecated/re-wired editable options and the new safety metadata.

## Summary

Downgrades the \`TypeDoc Verification\` CI check from blocking failure to a warning annotation. Closes #2027.

## Why

TypeDoc HTML output is non-deterministic in small ways — hierarchy/navigation metadata re-orders when unrelated enum shapes change. Three recent PRs (#2021, #2024, #2026) all hit this gate with trivial drift, each requiring a round-trip regen commit. This is operational noise, not a quality signal.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Drop the gate entirely** — too aggressive; we still want the signal.
2. **Make it non-blocking (this PR)** — warning annotation preserves visibility.
3. **Auto-commit regen from CI** — rejected for now: adds \`contents: write\` permission to the docs-check workflow, which is a larger security/complexity tradeoff for a low-severity issue. Revisit if noise accumulates.

author: alpibrupa
body:
## Summary

End-to-end smoke test that validates the six pieces shipped through v0.4.x → v0.5.0 actually compose as a system. Found **two real bugs** in the process, both fixed here with regression tests.

## `demo/pitch-smoke.sh`

Drives the full pipeline:

1. Generate Ed25519 keypair
2. Start local registry with `AGENTSPEC_API_KEYS="alice:...,bob:..."`
3. Author agent manifest (permissive trust, `runtime: test-echo`)
4. Push as alice
5. Pull anonymously (public-read aggregated across tenants)
6. Lock with `--sign-key-env`
7. Run with `--via=bwrap --require-signed --pubkey <hex> --lock <path>`
8. Inspect records + verify lock + negative test (tamper lock, confirm run refuses)

Uses the new `test-echo` pseudo-runtime so no real LLM CLI is required. Prereqs: bwrap, curl, python3.

```
[1/8] ok signing keypair generated (pub=fb3ad098dfb3ae3e…)
[2/8] ok registry running at http://127.0.0.1:53015 (tenants: alice, bob)
[3/8] ok agent manifest written (runtime=test-echo, trust=full)
[4/8] ok pushed as alice → ag1:7301475beadd
[5/8] ok pulled anonymously (no API key) → .../pull-workdir/pitch-smoke.agent
[6/8] ok locked + signed (128-char Ed25519 signature)
[7/8] ok ran via bwrap with signature-verified lock
       runtime output: [test-echo] Pitch-smoke demo agent …
[8/8] ok record captured + lock verified
       run_id=01KPKG1YD5ZMZSK0P1BCG7DCTW, records=1
       tamper check: run refused tampered lock ✓

Pitch-smoke: all 8 steps passed.
```

## Bug 1 — `pull_agent` didn't parse the native server response

`client.pull_agent` expected either a Noether envelope (`{"ok", "data": {"result": {...}}}`) or a flat manifest dict. The agentspec-native server returns `{"hash": "...", "manifest": {...}}` — neither shape was recognised. Pull silently fell through to the `/stages/{id}` Noether fallback, which agentspec-native doesn't serve, and returned `None` → CLI printed `NOT_FOUND`. Anonymous pulls were broken against our own server.

**Fix:** extract the nested `"manifest"` key explicitly, keeping `"result"` and flat-dict fallbacks for Noether compat. Three regression tests in `test_registry_pull_roundtrip.py`: authenticated round-trip, anonymous public-read round-trip, still-missing-hash still returns None.

## Bug 2 — `runner` didn't flush stdout before spawning

When `agentspec run` was piped (`agentspec run | tee`), Python's block-buffered stdout held the "Launching..." line while the subprocess's line-buffered output went out immediately, making the log appear as `runtime-output → resolver-info → launch-msg` instead of the intended order at process exit. Purely cosmetic but visible in the demo.

**Fix:** `sys.stdout.flush()` + `sys.stderr.flush()` before `subprocess.run` in `runner.execute`.

## New: `test-echo` runtime

Zero-dependency pseudo-runtime that maps to POSIX `echo`. Added to `RUNTIME_BINARIES`, `PROVIDER_MAP` (no auth), and the runner's builder dispatch. Used by integration tests and the smoke. Five tests pin it.

## New: `python -m agentspec`

Added `src/agentspec/__main__.py`. The installed `agentspec` console script has a hardcoded shebang that breaks across venv relocations; `python -m agentspec` is portable. Demo script prefers it.

## Test delta

- **+8 tests**: 5 in `test_test_echo_runtime.py`, 3 in `test_registry_pull_roundtrip.py`.
- **428 passed, 0 regressions** (was 420 on main).
- Ruff clean on all new files.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — 428 pass
- [x] `demo/pitch-smoke.sh` — 8/8 steps pass locally on Linux with bwrap installed
- [ ] Reviewer: run the smoke on a different Linux host to confirm portability
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm `python -m agentspec` is the right canonical entry-point addition (alternative: fix the console-script shebang in `pyproject.toml`)

author: lucabattistini
body:
## Summary

Lands Phase 2 of the [cycle-performance rearchitecture plan](../blob/main/docs/plans/2026-04-19-001-refactor-maestro-cycle-performance-plan.md). Bottega surface changes that back fan-out (Phase 5) and graph-aware scope propagation (Phase 4).

**New Bottega data relation:** `component_usage.json` per project. Tracks (component → screens) edges for graph-aware scope expansion. Migration-safe: pre-existing projects without a usage file return `null` on read; `usage_index_initialized` flag on each entry distinguishes "never tracked" from "truly zero dependents" (per plan R33 + SpecFlow §4 resolution).

**New plural MCP tools** (collision-tolerant, no `batch_` prefix per plan R32):
- `add_components(projectId, components[], screenSlug?)` → per-item ResultMap
- `update_components(projectId, updates[], screenSlug?)` → per-item ResultMap
- `track_component_usage(projectId, componentId, screenSlug)` → `{tracked}`
- `get_component_usage(projectId, componentId?)` → usage entry / array / null

**ResultMap shape** — array + discriminated union on `status`:
```json
{
  "results": [
    { "id": "button", "status": "added" },
    { "id": "input",  "status": "collision", "code": "COMPONENT_EXISTS", "message": "…" },
    { "id": "card",   "status": "rejected",  "code": "TOKEN_VALIDATION_FAILED", "message": "…" }
  ],
  "counts": { "added": 1, "updated": 0, "collision": 1, "rejected": 1 }
}
```

Preserves input order; enables exhaustive TypeScript checks on `status`. New `DUPLICATE_IN_BATCH` code catches same-id-twice caller bugs.

**Singular tools**: `add_component` and `update_component` gain an optional `screenSlug` parameter — backwards-compatible; omission = no usage tracking. Existing callers (biopsy, anything not on the new flow) unaffected.

**Version coupling**: Bottega `1.0.0 → 1.1.0` (additive minor per semver). Maestro's `plugin.json` adds `min_bottega_version: "1.1.0"`. New `check-bottega-version` skill GETs `/health`, compares, returns a structured `{compatible, bottega_version, required_version, halt_reason?}` so orchestrators can halt hard on mismatch (R34).

**Surface-area contract** (AGENTS.md amended): specialist building-blocks 70 → 71, total skills/ files 81 → 82.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` green (bottega + maestro workspaces)
- [x] `pnpm test` — 351 tests passing (334 prior + 17 new) in ~400ms
- [x] New test file `tests/projects/component-usage.test.ts` covers read/write/track/get + concurrency + pre-existing-project migration
- [x] No regressions in existing component / token / design-system tests

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

`No additional operational monitoring required: this PR adds Bottega MCP tools + a plugin skill + a new JSON file on disk under ~/.bottega/projects/<slug>/. No production service is deployed; Bottega runs locally per-user. The new data relation is additive and migration-safe for pre-existing projects. Failure modes already covered by existing Bottega error taxonomy (PROJECT_CORRUPTED on malformed JSON, STORAGE_ERROR on fs failure).`

## Not in this PR

- Maestro orchestrator changes to CALL the new plural tools — those land in Phase 5 (fan-out architecture)
- Maestro scope resolver that consults `get_component_usage` — Phase 4 (scope model)
- CI Test step remains commented (vitest hang issue #10162 upstream, unrelated to this work)

## Origin

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-04-19-001-refactor-maestro-cycle-performance-plan.md` Phase 2 (4-5 days focused work). Completed in this session.

body:
Lands the next milestone of the collab v1 build-out — the §4.6 scope resolution algorithm, the single primitive that gates every `path` argument across the forthcoming `collab_*` tools (W2 Day 4 onwards).

### Changes

- **`src/collab/scope.ts` (new)** — `validateScopedPathSyntax` (pure, zero Graph calls) covers steps 1–5: pre-normalisation refusals, single URL-decode + post-decode re-check, NFC/NFKC equality, segment validation, and layout enforcement (flat `proposals/`/`drafts/` vs recursive `attachments/`). `resolveScopedPath` adds steps 6–7: byId path resolution at `/me/drive/items/{folderId}:/{joined}:`, ancestry walk capped at N=8 hops, and the `shortcut_redirect` / `cross_drive` / `case_aliasing` defences.
- **`src/errors.ts`** — `OutOfScopeError` carries `attemptedPath`, a 19-value `OutOfScopeReason` enum, and an optional `resolvedItemId` (populated only by step 7 refusals). Joins on the verbatim agent-supplied path so `scope_denied` audit entries are stable.

body:
Closes #24

## What changed

- Extracted `cmd/gui/frontend/src/lib/LauncherMenu.svelte` — one component renders both the repo-row kebab and the account-header kebab, so visual and behavioural parity is a compile-time guarantee rather than a drift-prone copy.
- Restructured the full-view kebab into three sections: always-visible (browser, folder), per-category default using `terminals[0]` / `editors[0]` / `ai_harnesses[0]`, and per-category submenus that only appear when a category has two or more entries. Sweep branches stays as a repo-only entry below the submenus. Submenu positioning flips based on which side the parent menu is pinned to (left for repo-row kebab, right for account-header kebab).
- Fixed Svelte scoped-styles boundary: duplicated the base `.action-dropdown` / `.action-item` rules inside the new component so the menu renders as a vertical dropdown instead of flow-layout pill buttons.
- TUI: added direct-key shortcuts on both the repo and account detail screens (`t` = terminals[0], `e` = editors[0] on repo only, `a` = ai_harnesses[0]), plus an `o` / `O` launcher modal listing every configured launcher grouped by category. Lowercase `e` / `o` on the account screen stay bound to the existing edit-form / open-folder actions; the capital `O` launcher covers editor access there without breaking muscle memory.
- New shared launcher helpers in `cmd/cli/tui/launchers.go` (argv-level `{path}` / `{command}` resolver, minimal duplication of the GUI's logic since the TUI already owns a console and doesn't need the Windows `cmd.exe /C start` wrapper).
- Docs: README "What it does" gains a one-line hook for the clone/account launcher actions. `docs/gui-guide.md` Clone + Account actions sections rewritten to describe the default-then-submenu layout, submenu hide rules, and click-not-hover behaviour.

## Test plan

- [ ] GUI full view: repo-row ⋮ renders as a vertical dropdown with sections — browser/folder, default launchers, submenus (appear only when ≥2 entries in the category), Sweep branches at the bottom. Default-launcher entries hide cleanly when a category has zero entries.
- [ ] GUI full view: `Terminals ▸` / `Editors ▸` / `AI Harnesses ▸` open on click, flip side based on kebab position, close on outside-click or action fire.
- [ ] GUI full view: account-header ⋮ uses the same layout, with no Sweep entry.
- [ ] GUI compact view unchanged — folder / editor / terminal / harness icons still launch their defaults.
- [ ] TUI repo detail (cloned repo): `t` / `e` / `a` launch the first configured entry of each category, `o` opens the launcher modal (arrow-keys, Enter, Esc).
- [ ] TUI account detail: lowercase `e` still opens the edit form, lowercase `o` still opens the account folder, capital `O` opens the launcher. `t` / `a` launch the first terminal / harness against the account's parent folder.
- [ ] Empty-category keys are silent no-ops (no crash, no error) when pressed on a config with nothing in that category.
- [ ] `go vet ./...`, `go test -short ./...`, and a full wails build on Windows all pass.

author: grant-l
body:
## Summary

One-line fix to a pre-existing test failure: `src/tests/test_navier_stokes.py::TestFullProof::test_ns_smoothness_proven` was raising `KeyError: 'Step_4_Continuum_Limit'` on every run.

## Root cause

`full_navier_stokes_proof()` in `src/ave/axioms/navier_stokes.py` merges the continuum-limit result with the Sobolev H¹ theorem and returns the combined dict under key `Step_4_Continuum_and_Sobolev`. The test was still asserting the pre-rename key `Step_4_Continuum_Limit`, which has not existed in the returned dict since the Sobolev bound was added.

The `smoothness_preserved` field the test actually cares about is still present inside the merged dict (inherited from `continuum_limit_ns()`); only the outer key name needed updating.

## Regression posture

|---|---|---|
| pytest | 835 passed, 3 skipped, **1 failed** | **836 passed**, 3 skipped |

author: iorlas
body:
## Summary

- Closes the recurring CSS 404 in Docker/Linux builds tracked at [TanStack/router#4959](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/4959).
- One-line change: `@import "tailwindcss"` → `@import "tailwindcss" source("./")` in `apps/web/src/styles.css`.

## Why

Without an explicit `source(...)`, `@tailwindcss/vite`'s content scan runs independently in the client and SSR Vite passes. On Linux the two passes walk the filesystem in different orders, produce different CSS content and different content hashes. The SSR bundle bakes in one hash, the client pass emits the CSS with a different hash, and browsers 404 on the CSS.

macOS local builds happen to converge, which masks the bug during development.

`source("./")` pins the scan root to the CSS file's own directory (`apps/web/src/`) — narrow enough to be walk-order-deterministic across platforms.

`source("../")` was tried first and did **not** fix it — scan root was still too wide. Reference: issue comment [#3774241578](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/4959#issuecomment-3774241578) independently confirms `source("./")` works.

## Test plan

- [x] Local macOS `pnpm --filter @project/web build` — matching hashes (was already working pre-fix).
- [x] Downstream consumer, fresh Linux Docker build, no cache — matching SSR + emitted-file hashes, CSS served at `/assets/styles-<HASH>.css` with `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, app renders fully styled.

author: theopie
body:
## Why

The site went stale for days earlier this week without anyone noticing. Root cause was a single batched LLM call returning `[]`, which the pipeline accepted silently. That's not a failure mode I'd ship to a paying customer.

This PR makes the pipeline behave like a product: deterministic where possible, observable when it isn't, and able to degrade gracefully without operator intervention.

## What changed

**Structuring** (`structurer.py`)
- Anthropic → Ollama (MiniMax M2.7 cloud via local proxy)
- `temperature=0` for reproducible output
- One source per request — multi-source prompts reliably made MiniMax return `[]`
- Bounded retry with a small temperature nudge on empty responses from historically-productive sources

**State & fallback** (`state.py`, `__main__.py`)
- Per-source rolling history (last 14 runs) persisted to `state/source_state.json` (gitignored)
- Last-known-good events cached per source
- When a source returns empty or fails, the orchestrator substitutes the cache; the 7-day window filter drops expired events automatically
- `consecutive_empty` streak tracked per source for anomaly detection

**Validation** (`validation.py`)
- ISO `dateTime` must parse, URLs must be http(s), required fields enforced
- Whitespace normalization, length caps, empty-optional cleanup
- Events failing validation are dropped, not silently propagated

**Health reporting** (`health.py`)
- `state/last_run.json` machine-readable after every run
- Console summary with per-source status vs. historical baseline
- Exit codes now reflect true health: `0` healthy, `2` degraded, `1` critical
- New `python -m the_word health` CLI subcommand

**Tests**
- 50 passing unit tests covering: state roundtrip, rolling window, baseline median, cache updates, structurer retry-on-empty, HTTP error paths, malformed JSON, markdown-wrapped JSON, validation edge cases (bad dates, bad URLs, non-string tags, overlong fields)

## Validated locally

- `pytest` — 50/50 pass
- End-to-end run with `--no-push` produced 15 events, wrote events.json, reported DEGRADED correctly (5 sources returned empty — state will accumulate over subsequent runs to enable fallback)
- Health report CLI works

## Test plan

- [ ] Review the `state.py` schema — particularly the rolling-window and baseline semantics
- [ ] Spot-check the retry-on-empty temperature heuristic in `structurer.py`
- [ ] Confirm `state/` stays gitignored after a cron run
- [ ] Let one or two cron runs accumulate state, then force a source to fail (e.g. block the URL) to verify fallback fires

author: profvjreddi
body:
## Summary

The first of five logical PRs that make up the staged-rollout foundation
for the new mlsysbook.ai ecosystem properties. This PR is the safety
net layer — three tiers of link checking plus a publish-guard so that
no `*-publish-live` workflow can deploy without a recent green
`*-validate-dev` run.

Nothing in this PR ships content; everything is plumbing.

### What's in this PR

**Tier 1 — pre-commit (instant, local).** New
`shared/scripts/check-internal-links.py` runs against staged `.md`/`.qmd`
files only, validates internal links + anchors, skips fenced code
blocks and inline code (so TikZ snippets etc. don't false-positive),
and is wired into `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with an `exclude` list for
known legacy / auto-generated paths.

**Tier 2 — per-subsite CI (every PR + every dev push).** Generalized
`.github/workflows/infra-link-check.yml` to take site-specific args
(`include_pattern`, `lycheeignore_path`, `accept_status`,
`fail_on_broken`). Every `*-validate-dev.yml` now invokes it as a
`check-links` job. Created `site-validate-dev.yml` and
`staffml-validate-dev.yml` for the two subsites that lacked validate
workflows. Universal exclusions live in `shared/config/.lycheeignore`.

**Publish guard.** New `.github/workflows/infra-publish-guard.yml`
blocks every `*-publish-live.yml` from running unless the latest
`*-validate-dev.yml` run on `dev` is green and recent (configurable
`max_age_minutes`, default 60). Wired as the first job of each publish
workflow.

**Tier 3 — nightly link-rot tracker.** New
`.github/workflows/infra-link-rot-nightly.yml` sweeps every subsite at
04:30 UTC and aggregates findings into a single sticky GitHub issue
(label `link-rot`). Each run replaces the issue body and appends a
comment, so the issue is the always-current dashboard.

### Risk surface

Tier 1 + Tier 2 are non-blocking by default (`fail_on_broken: false`)
so existing baseline failures don't immediately gate merges; we can
flip the flag per-subsite as backlogs are cleared. **Publish guards
CAN block** on green dev — that's the whole point.

### Verification done locally

- YAML schema validation on every modified/created workflow.
- `python3 .github/scripts/check_workflow_fork_safety.py` on all five
  new/modified workflows — clean.
- `check-internal-links.py` exercised against a real `.qmd` file.
- Pre-commit hook smoke-tested on the script itself (correctly skips
  non-md files).

### Verification still pending in this PR's CI

- The reusable workflows running on a real PR (this one). Specifically
  watching whether:
  - Lychee accepts `shared/config/.lycheeignore` patterns.
  - The per-site `include_pattern` globs match what we think they
    match.
  - The publish-guard's GitHub-API query syntax actually works (it's
    only invoked on workflow_dispatch, so this PR exercises everything
    EXCEPT the guard — that gets exercised the first time someone
    clicks "Run" on a `*-publish-live` workflow).

### What this PR does NOT change

- Nothing under `book/`, `tinytorch/`, `labs/`, `kits/`, etc. The
  source content is untouched.
- No publish workflow's deploy logic — only added a `guard` job before
  existing logic runs.
- No release-version state.

### Test plan

- [ ] CI: `book-validate-dev` runs to completion, including the new
      `check-links` job.
- [ ] CI: `tinytorch-validate-dev`, `labs-validate-dev`,
      `kits-validate-dev`, `mlsysim-validate-dev` all pass with
      check-links.
- [ ] CI: `site-validate-dev` and `staffml-validate-dev` (newly
      created) at least start and report.
- [ ] Pre-commit hook installs and runs on a sample staged `.qmd`
      change without hanging.
- [ ] Read-through of the link-check job summary in Actions UI to
      confirm Lychee output is interpretable.

### Followup

Four more PRs on the existing release-prep work. Tracked in
`RELEASE-PREP.md` (not in this PR — comes with PR-3).
