body:
This PR introduces the initial configuration system for the Node.js Azure DevOps migration tool: config is now loaded from JSON, validated with Zod, and exposed as inferred TypeScript types. It also wires `pnpm cli migrate --config <path>` to load/validate config and log the parsed result.

- **Config schema + typed API (core)**
  - Replaced the old flat config shape with the requested structured schema:
    - `source` / `target` (`organizationUrl`, `project`, PAT auth via `tokenEnvVar`)
    - `execution` (`dryRun`, `logLevel`, `concurrency`)
  - Kept inferred types from Zod (`z.infer`) and existing parse/load entry points.

- **Defaults and validation behavior**
  - Added schema defaults under `execution`:
    - `dryRun: false`
    - `logLevel: "info"`
    - `concurrency: 1`
  - Enforced URL validation and log level enum validation.

- **CLI integration (`migrate --config`)**
  - `migrate` command now loads config from file via core loader, validates it, and logs the typed config.
  - Existing `--dry-run` flag is applied as an execution override (`execution.dryRun = true`) at command orchestration level.

- **Tests and fixtures/docs alignment**
  - Updated core config tests to cover:
    - valid config
    - missing required fields
    - invalid URL
    - invalid log level
    - default application
  - Added CLI command test coverage for successful config load/validation and invalid config failure.
  - Updated sample config fixture and README config example to the new schema.

```ts
// packages/core/src/config.ts
export const MigrationConfigSchema = z.object({
  source: z.object({
    organizationUrl: z.string().url(),
    project: z.string().min(1),
    auth: z.object({
      type: z.literal('pat'),
      tokenEnvVar: z.string().min(1),
    }),
  }),
  target: z.object({
    organizationUrl: z.string().url(),
    project: z.string().min(1),
    auth: z.object({
      type: z.literal('pat'),
      tokenEnvVar: z.string().min(1),
    }),
  }),
  execution: z
    .object({
      dryRun: z.boolean().default(false),
      logLevel: z.enum(['trace', 'debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error', 'fatal']).default('info'),
      concurrency: z.number().int().min(1).default(1),
    })
    .default({}),
});
```

author: torlando-tech
body:
## Summary

- Bumps `reticulumKt` v0.0.8 → v0.0.9 to pick up [reticulum-kt#45](https://github.com/torlando-tech/reticulum-kt/pull/45), which exposes `Interface.online` as a `StateFlow<Boolean>` instead of an `AtomicBoolean`.
- Wires `NativeInterfaceFactory` to collect the new flow and re-notify the existing listener chain on every distinct online transition, so the interface card refreshes when a subclass flips online after registration.
- Migrates the two `iface.online.get()` call sites (factory log line + `RNodeRecoveryHelper` health check) to `iface.online.value`.

## Motivation

`RNodeInterface` sets itself online ~4 seconds after registration, once the USB handshake completes and radio config is validated. Columba's `InterfaceMgmtVM` only saw the `online` value at the moment of registration (via `InterfaceAdapter.online` snapshotted into a domain model), so the card stayed grey forever even though the radio was fully functional. User confirmed this was purely cosmetic — traffic flowed, announces arrived, just the UI indicator was stuck.

Chose the library-side fix (expose a flow) rather than a Columba-side workaround (e.g., poll every second) because: the library already knew when the transition happened and simply lacked a notification hook. Adding one is a ~40-line Kotlin-idiomatic refactor in `reticulum-kt`.

## Stacked on

- [reticulum-kt#45](https://github.com/torlando-tech/reticulum-kt/pull/45) **must merge first**, and v0.0.9 must be tagged before this PR's JitPack-backed CI will be green. See the bottom of that PR's description for the rationale.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :app:assembleNoSentryDebug` — builds locally against the `refactor/interface-online-state-flow` branch via `includeBuild` (reverted before commit; settings.gradle.kts is clean).
- [x] `./gradlew :reticulum:testDebugUnitTest` — passes locally.
- [ ] **Manual (pending physical RNode):** start the app with an RNode interface configured. The card's online indicator should transition grey → green within ~5 seconds of the card first appearing, matching the handshake window.
- [ ] **Manual recovery:** yank USB while online. Card should flip back to offline within the recovery loop's detection window. (`RNodeRecoveryHelper` already handles this; now reads `iface.online.value` rather than `.get()`.)

## Implementation notes

- `observeOnlineState` uses `drop(1)` to skip `StateFlow`'s initial replay on subscribe — `registerAndTrack` already pushes a snapshot via its explicit `notifyListeners()` call, so without the drop every new interface would emit a duplicate no-op notify.
- `distinctUntilChanged()` coalesces any redundant writes from subclass implementations (e.g., `setOnline(false)` being called twice during teardown).
- Collectors are keyed by interface name in `onlineObservers` and cancelled in `stopInterface()` to prevent leaks. `restartInterface()` goes through `stopInterface → startInterface` which cancels-and-reinstalls cleanly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context)

body:
## Summary

\`/handoff\` Step 6 spawns a new \`unleashed-alpha\` window via \`wt.exe -w new nt\`. With no focus-preservation around that call, the new WT window yanks OS-level focus away from whatever app the user switched to while the handoff was persisting artifacts. Observed today: typing in a browser was redirected into the freshly spawned onboard session.

## Fix

Inline HWND save/restore bracket around the existing Python one-liner in \`.claude/commands/handoff.md\` line 307:

\`\`\`python
u32 = ctypes.windll.user32
h = u32.GetForegroundWindow()      # capture BEFORE spawn
subprocess.Popen(r'wt.exe ...')    # spawn new WT window
time.sleep(0.8)                    # let wt.exe finish activation
u32.SetForegroundWindow(h)         # restore user's app
\`\`\`

## Related

- Sibling fix unleashed#337 / #338 (companion tabs INSIDE the wrapper, already merged). 
- This PR covers the separate spawn-time steal that happens BEFORE the wrapper process exists.

## Test plan (manual, post-merge)

1. In a Claude session, run \`/handoff\`.
2. Immediately switch to Chrome and start typing in the address bar.
3. Wait for handoff to complete (~30s). New WT window pops open.
4. Expected: Chrome keeps focus; mid-sentence keystrokes stay in the address bar.

Closes #969

author: quillaid
body:
## Summary

Full implementation of Phase 2 from the spawn panic audit (design doc PR #1926, implementation plan PR #1930).

Adds panic handling to all 29 production `tokio::spawn` sites in `crates/runtimed/src/`. Currently, when a spawned task panics, tokio silently drops it and the daemon degrades: blob server gone, autosave stopped, warming loops dead, pool accounting drifted.

## Implementation stages

### Stage 1: `WarmingGuard` RAII (Q3) ✅
RAII guard for pool warming counters. On Drop, rolls back `warming_failed_for_path`. `commit()` suppresses on success, `fail_with()` records specific errors. Replaces ~16 manual cleanup blocks.

### Stage 2: `task_supervisor` module
- `spawn_supervised(label, fut, on_panic)` — catches panics, logs, calls callback
- `spawn_best_effort(label, fut)` — catches panics, logs only
- Extracts `panic_payload_to_string` from existing `catch_automerge_panic`

### Stage 3: Kernel tasks (`jupyter_kernel.rs`)
6 sites. `on_panic` sends `KernelDied`. Stderr pump is best-effort.

### Stage 4: Daemon long-lived workers
13 sites across `daemon.rs`, `blob_server.rs`, `main.rs`, `runtime_agent_handle.rs`. Warming loops get single-respawn with CAS counter. Blob server gets respawn-with-counter.

### Stage 5: Notebook-sync + best-effort batch
4 supervised + 10 best-effort sites.

### Stage 6: Autosave (Q4) + final gate
`spawn_autosave_debouncer` gets `trigger_shutdown()` on panic. Final grep confirms only test site remains.

## Test plan
- [ ] Each stage: `cargo xtask lint --fix` + `cargo test -p runtimed`
- [ ] After stage 4: `cargo xtask build --release` + nightly install + gremlin suite
- [ ] Stage 6 final gate: `grep -n "tokio::spawn" crates/runtimed/src/` — only test site #30 remains

This PR includes algebraic variables in the time-step error control of the Rosenbrock algorithm. The approach to estimating error from algebraic terms is from Copilot, so I would like @dwfncar to look to make sure he agrees. It seems like there are a number of ways to handle this, and I'm not familiar enough with the math to know which is best for our use case. It may be that https://github.com/NCAR/micm/issues/842 is the best way to handle stiff systems with constraints in the long term.

However, I did use this implementation successfully with a stiff cloud chemistry mechanism that included several constraints. Prior to the fix, it was taking 700K+ internal solver steps, and after the fix it was down to about 10 after the first cold-start call to `Solve()`.

The change to the existing Rosenbrock test is just to remove an explicit check that the algebraic error tolerances were _not_ being applied.

author: jfberry
body:
## Summary

Removes disk round-trips from the multistaticmap hot path. Images flow in-memory from viewport render → overlay → grid compose → HTTP response. Disk writes happen only for explicit `?pregenerate=true`; a `CompositeImageCache` LRU handles cross-request burst sharing within the short-TTL window that makes up poracle traffic.

Expected impact against the current 103 ms multistaticmap baseline on this branch (HEAD `edc2eff`): ~50-80 ms after warmup, depending on `COMPOSITE_IMAGE_CACHE_SIZE` (default 200).

## Changes

- Renderer returns `*image.NRGBA` directly (`RenderViewportImage`); skips internal PNG encode when the caller's next step is a draw
- Handler pipeline's primary currency is `image.Image`, not `[]byte` — ensures shared components across multi requests reuse pre-decoded pixels, no PNG round-trip per cache hit
- New `CompositeImageCache` LRU (`services.GlobalCompositeImageCache`, size via `COMPOSITE_IMAGE_CACHE_SIZE`) replaces the short-TTL disk cache for base renders and final staticmap outputs
- Multi handler collects `[]image.Image` and composes in-memory — one encode per request at the HTTP boundary
- HTTP responses via `http.ServeContent` from encoded bytes (not `http.ServeFile`)
- Disk writes centralised in `handlePregenerateResponseBytes`, which also calls `enqueueWithBase` — enforces one-to-one "disk file ↔ expiry registration" invariant
- External-style tile stitching unchanged (still writes basePath to disk with age-based CacheCleaner sweep — one acknowledged exception, documented in CLAUDE.md)

## Accepted trade-off

Requests without a TTL no longer benefit from a 7-day disk fallback on duplicate responses. Reuse is LRU-bounded (~minutes at 200 slots). Poracle's burst-share window fits comfortably; long-window regeneration cost is ~50 ms single / ~150 ms multi.

If this turns out to matter for a non-poracle use case, a follow-up can add an opt-in `LONG_TERM_DISK_CACHE=true` env flag to re-enable async disk writes on the OwnedThreshold path.

## Plan + architecture

Full plan and rationale committed at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-19-bytes-first-in-memory-pipeline.md`. CLAUDE.md's "Base vs final path" section documents the image-first contract, LRU role, enqueue invariant, and the accepted no-disk-fallback trade-off.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `go test ./...` — all packages pass except the pre-existing `TestWorkerHangIsKilledOnContextDeadline` flake in the renderer package (OS signal timing race in the test harness, unrelated)
- [x] Race tests `TestEnsureBaseSingleflightDedupesSiblings`, `TestGenerateStaticMapSingleflightSurvivesLeaderCancel`, `TestReloadStylesPreservesConcurrentlyCreatedPool` still pass
- [ ] **Deploy to staging** — build Docker image via CI, run against production-equivalent traffic shape for 30+ min
- [ ] **Compare `rampardos_request_duration_seconds{type="multistaticmap",cached="false"}` avg** to the 103 ms baseline. Target: ~50-80 ms
- [ ] **Check `image_cache_{hits,misses}_total{cache="composite"}` hit rate** — should climb to >50% after warmup; if stalls, consider `COMPOSITE_IMAGE_CACHE_SIZE=500`
- [ ] **Check `renderer_pool_acquire_wait_seconds` p95** — sustained >100 ms is the tripwire to flip viewport mode off
- [ ] **Capture a fresh pprof** and compare to the 16:47 baseline — expect `png.writeImage` still dominant (unavoidable final encode), `image.Decode` / `readImagePass` minimal

## Deferred follow-ups (not blocking)

- `TestEnsureBaseDeletedBetweenCallsDoesNotError` has weaker coverage after the refactor (reviewer noted). Worth refocusing on the LRU-eviction scenario.
- Dead `utils.GenerateStaticMap` / `utils.GenerateMultiStaticMap` file-based wrappers are no longer called. Safe cleanup for a follow-up.

author: turer73
body:
## Summary

Admin dashboard `/api/admin/stats` was using the user-scoped Supabase client for aggregate `COUNT` queries. RLS policies on `game_sessions`, `session_answers`, `questions` filtered out rows the admin did not own, causing severely under-reported totals.

### Observed vs actual (live data today)

| Metric | Dashboard (user-scoped) | Supabase (service role) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `game_sessions` | 16 | 60 | **-44** |
| `session_answers` | 128 | 465 | **-337** |
| `questions` | 3,716 | 3,735 | **-19** |
| `profiles` (non-deleted) | ok | ok | 0 |
| `error_reports` (pending) | ok | ok | 0 |

## Root Cause

`src/app/api/admin/stats/route.ts` called `createClient()` (server component client — cookie-scoped JWT, RLS **enforced**) for every count. RLS policies on those tables filter by `owner_id = auth.uid()`, so an admin browsing the dashboard saw only their own sessions/answers/questions.

## Fix

After the existing `checkPermission(...)` guard, switch the aggregate queries to `createServiceRoleClient()` (RLS bypass). The service role key stays server-side and is never returned to the client, so this is safe once the caller is confirmed to be an admin.

```ts
// Auth (user-scoped, RLS on)
const supabase = await createClient()
const admin = await checkPermission(supabase, 'admin.dashboard.view')
if (!admin) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Yetkisiz erisim' }, { status: 403 })

// Aggregate counts (service role, RLS bypass)
const admindb = createServiceRoleClient()
const [users, questions, sessions, answers, reports] = await Promise.all([...])
```

Inline comments in the route explain the decision for future readers.

## Tests

Updated `src/app/api/admin/stats/__tests__/route.test.ts` to mock `@/lib/supabase/service-role` alongside the existing server mock. Three tests covering: 403 without permission, 200 with aggregate payload, null-count fallback.

- Local: `npm test` -> **388/388 passed** (pre-push hook)
- Local: `npm run type-check` -> clean
- Local: `npm run lint` -> 33 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors

## Follow-up

Other admin endpoints may have the same RLS problem. Will audit separately:
- `/api/admin/users`
- `/api/admin/reports`
- `/api/admin/logs`

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] After merge + Vercel deploy, reload `/admin` while logged in as admin
- [ ] Verify dashboard matches Supabase: ~60 sessions, ~465 answers, ~3,735 questions

Adopt the official `flags` SDK for the /.well-known/vercel/flags endpoint
so the Vercel Toolbar's Feature Flags panel can discover, describe, and

  human-readable `label` + `description` + release status.

  (no JSX, no React, no icons) plus a thin view wrapper that reattaches
  lucide-react icons. The serverless function imports the data module
  directly, giving the Toolbar the full registry metadata without
  pulling React into the function bundle.
- Add `tests/unit/flagsExplorerEndpoint.test.js` to cover the auth gate
  and response shape, and guard the shared test setup so node-env tests
  can opt out of jsdom-only polyfills.

respond; the Toolbar panel handles provisioning the matching access
proof.

## Summary

- Prepend \`ALTER TABLE clinical_flags ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS rule_id text;\` to \`0024_flag_dedup_constraint.sql\` so \`pnpm db:migrate\` succeeds against a fresh Postgres (was erroring with \"column rule_id does not exist\" when the partial unique index tried to reference it).
- Add a static-analysis guard test that ensures the ALTER TABLE appears before the partial index that references it.
- Wire the missing \`test\` script in \`packages/db-schema/package.json\` so the new guard (and the pre-existing encryption / hmac / mfa tests) actually run in CI via \`turbo test\`.

The \`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS\` is idempotent — existing databases (where \`rule_id\` was added via a prior \`drizzle-kit push\`, schema sync, or manual DDL) are unaffected. Fresh databases now get the column before the partial index references it.

author: davidasnider
body:
This PR addresses several critical hardware compatibility issues discovered during local testing:

1. **Forbidden Value Capping (255):** Hardware testing confirmed that the controller rejects packets containing the value `255` (0xFF). All channel values are now automatically capped at `254` within the `DiodLEDController` class.
2. **White Channel Logic:** Testing confirmed that the dedicated white channel (`0x4B`) is non-functional on this specific hardware. The integration now uses `ColorMode.RGB` and relies on RGB mixing to achieve white light (specifically `RGB=(254, 254, 254)`).
3. **Sequential Command Delivery:** The controller failed to process multiple commands in a single TCP payload (causing "Teal" or "Purple" color shifts). `CMD_CHUNK_SIZE` has been set to `1` to ensure each command is sent in its own TCP connection.

The changes have been verified with both unit tests and physical hardware testing.

- Added `--font-serif-lede: "EB Garamond"` and `--font-mono: "JetBrains Mono"` font tokens.
- Google Fonts `<link>` extended to all four families (Playfair Display, EB Garamond, Inter, JetBrains Mono).
- Flattened `.btn-primary` / `.btn-secondary` / `.btn-navy`: no gradients, no rounded corners, solid gold fill / gold-hairline outline, uppercase small-caps, hover glow `0 6px 24px -10px` of gold.
- Flattened `.card`: hairline border, no shadow, subtle hover tint on parchment.
- Flattened `.form-input`: square corners, hairline border, EB Garamond body, italic placeholders.
- Replaced `.gradient-navy` with flat navy; kept `.gradient-overlay` but softened to a subtle radial vignette only (the one gradient the handover permits).
- Added new editorial primitives: `.eyebrow` (11px / 0.28em uppercase with leading 36px gold hairline, + `.eyebrow-both` variant), `.roman`, `.lede`, `.sec-num`, `.fleur` (with 80px hairlines on either side of `✦ ❦ ✦`), `.ornament` (corner brackets), `.dbl-rule`, `.plate` (diagonal gold-stripe placeholder with mono label), `.terms-body`, `.font-mono` / `.font-lede` utilities.
- Kept `fadeIn / fadeInUp / countPulse / shimmer` keyframes (subtle, compatible).
- `agents/my-agent.ts`: updated the outdated `#2A3E5C` / `#D4AF37` palette reference and expanded the style brief so agent-generated UI stays on-brand.

### Shared components (`Header`, `Footer`, `ChatWidget`, `CookieConsent`)

- **Header** — dropped the gold "V" tile logo; brand mark is now text-only (Playfair "Code Victorian" + mono small-caps "Est. MMXXVI"). Scrolled state swaps drop-shadow for a hairline bottom border. Desktop nav uses small-caps 11px / 0.22em links; dropdowns are square hairline panels; mobile menu uses Playfair for primary links and EB Garamond for dropdown children.
- **Footer** — `gradient-navy` replaced with flat navy. Newsletter strip becomes a 2-col hairline grid with EB Garamond input and flat gold submit. Social icons are square hairline boxes (no pills). "Legal" column renamed "Correspondence" to match the editorial register. Bottom bar gets a `.dbl-rule` above the mono uppercase copyright row.
- **ChatWidget** — the `rounded-full` gradient FAB is now a 48×48 gold-outlined navy square with a `✦` glyph. Modal is hairline-bordered on cream, no `shadow-2xl`. 21st-dev wiring untouched.
- **CookieConsent** — hairline-bordered navy banner, square checkboxes with mono small-caps category labels, eyebrow header, `btn-primary` / `btn-secondary` for actions.

### Pages (13 files)

Every page got the same systematic pass while preserving every route, form field, and string of copy:

1. `app/page.tsx` — Hero: strip the SVG checker pattern and backdrop-blur form card; use an eyebrow + three-line Playfair headline with italic gold "Native"; form card is hairline-bordered with the corner-bracket ornament. StatsBar: hairline vertical dividers, Playfair numerals, mono small-caps labels. IssuesSection: I/II/III Roman glyphs instead of lucide icons; no card shadows. PetitionCTA: fleur above, flat gold progress bar, eyebrow. NewsSection: `sec-num` header, `.plate` diagonal-stripe placeholders in place of gradient image boxes, mono dates (MMXXVI), italic-gold kickers. DonationSection: square 5-tile amount grid with hairline dividers, flat freq toggle, corner-bracket card. FinalCTA: flat navy, fleur, italic-gold emphasis.
2. `app/petition/page.tsx` — Eyebrow hero; progress bar is a hairline + thin flat gold; petition body now inside a hairline/ivory card with Roman-numeral markers (I–V) on each clause; social share turned into a single hairline row of mono buttons; sticky signature form is corner-bracket-ornamented.
3. `app/issues/page.tsx` — Each of the 3 main issues gets a Roman numeral glyph in place of the lucide icon; alternating layout preserved; stats in a shared hairline column. "Additional Priorities" grid uses IV/V/VI Roman glyphs on navy with hairline dividers. CTA gets a fleur.
4. `app/news/page.tsx` — Featured article image area becomes a `.plate`; article grid cards are hairline-bounded (one continuous border grid); all dates in JetBrains Mono as MMXXVI roman; categories in italic gold.
5. `app/join/page.tsx` — Three tier cards in square hairline; the "Patriot" popular tier uses a gold-tinted background + corner-bracket ornament (replacing the `ring-2 + shadow` treatment); tier prices in Playfair italic gold; feature lists use `✦` bullets between hairline rows. Benefits grid is a 2×2 Roman-numeralled hairline matrix.
6. `app/about/page.tsx` — Eyebrow + italic-gold hero emphasis; mission section image becomes a `.plate`; values grid is a 2×3 Roman-numeralled hairline matrix; timeline's gold-pill year badges become Roman-numeral chips (`XXI`, `XXII`, …) with hairline borders.
7. `app/contact/page.tsx` — Form inputs square hairline; sidebar info box uses small-caps gold labels over EB Garamond values; quick-links turned into a hairline-separated list with italic-gold arrows.
8. `app/donate/page.tsx` — Amount selection is a 6-tile square grid (5 presets + custom) with flat gold active-state; frequency toggle is a flat 2-col hairline row; payment method radios sit inside a hairline box; corner-bracket ornament on the form card; impact sidebar uses hairline-divided Playfair-italic amounts with EB Garamond descriptions.
9. `app/events/page.tsx` — Date blocks become a single navy column with a Playfair-italic Roman numeral day + mono month. Event list is a continuous hairline-divided vertical list; types shown as italic-gold kickers; hover tints to parchment.

Routes, form fields, form action bindings, copy, Stripe references, env requirements, `components.json`, `vercel.json`, `next.config.mjs`, `postcss.config.mjs`, dependency list, `package-lock.json`, the `motion` / `react-markdown` / `react-syntax-highlighter` / `zod` packages, or `ChatWidget`'s 21st-dev wiring.

### Motivation
- A recent staging-fidelity change caused Event Mode image-conditioned requests to fail and surface the generic error "Unable to build your atmosphere right now.".
- The failure traced to sending image conditioning through the wrong OpenAI path/format which crashed the Event Mode image-generation flow.
- The intent is to preserve the same-room/same-architecture conditioning (venue as structural truth, optional reference for style) while making the server robust and diagnosable.

### Description
- Send conditioned image requests via `POST /v1/images/edits` using `FormData` and `image[]` with `venueImage` first and optional `referenceImage` second, instead of trying to pass images in a JSON `image` array to the generations endpoint.
- Add `input_fidelity` and other fields to the conditioned form, and keep the strengthened same-room staging prompt logic intact.
- Add robust server-side diagnostics including `extractErrorText`, `logImageError`, improved parse logic for Base64 payloads, and clear logging for conditioned/fallback/parse/runtime failures.
- Keep a hardened fallback that attempts unconditioned `POST /v1/images/generations` when edits fail, and return a usable result when possible (file changed: `app/api/atmosphere/route.js`).

### Testing

author: eins78
body:
## Summary

`meteoswiss-mcp` v2.3.1 (released 2026-04-18) is incompatible with the canonical **ChatGPT Deep Research / Connectors** MCP contract on the `fetch` tool. This PR restores compatibility and locks it in with a regression test suite + tool-manifest snapshot so the rename can't slip through CI again.

## Investigation

| Field | ChatGPT spec | v2.3.1 | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fetch` input arg | `id: string` | `url: string` ❌ | `id: string` ✅ |
| `fetch` body field | `text` | `content` ❌ | `text` (+ `content` alias for back-compat) ✅ |
| `fetch` output keys | `{id, title, text, url, metadata}` | `{id, title, content, format, metadata}` ❌ | `{id, title, text, content, format, url, metadata}` ✅ |
| `search` input | `query` | `query` ✅ | unchanged ✅ |
| MCP envelope | `content[0].type='text'` w/ JSON-stringified body | same ✅ | unchanged ✅ |

Origin: commit de9c937 (2026-04-18) renamed the param `id → url` claiming the rc.3 `id` name was an "unintentional rename". Git history disagrees — `id` has been the canonical name since the schema's first commit (d6b1c62). The reversion was itself the regression.

Authoritative sources used (verbatim, all cited in the plan):
- OpenAI Cookbook canonical Python reference: `fetch(id: str)` returning `{id, title, text, url, metadata}` — <https://github.com/openai/openai-cookbook/blob/main/examples/deep_research_api/how_to_build_a_deep_research_mcp_server/main.py>
- Vercel Labs canonical TS reference (`mcp-handler` + zod): same shape — <https://github.com/vercel-labs/deep-research-server/blob/main/app/mcp/route.ts>
- OpenAI Deep Research API guide — <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/deep-research>
- OpenAI MCP integration overview — <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/mcp>
- MCP TypeScript SDK release scan (1.21–2.0-alpha) — no SDK-driven rename to motivate the de9c937 commit.

Full investigation, contract diff, and references in the plan doc:
- [`docs/plans/2026-04-19-chatgpt-fetch-compat.md`](https://github.com/eins78/meteoswiss-llm-tools/blob/feature/chatgpt-fetch-compat/docs/plans/2026-04-19-chatgpt-fetch-compat.md)

## What's in this PR

5 atomic commits:

1. `docs/plans: chatgpt fetch compat plan` — initial plan stub.
2. `docs/plans: expand chatgpt fetch compat plan with full research` — comprehensive plan covering all three ChatGPT integration modes (Connectors, Apps SDK Developer Mode, Responses API direct), transport/auth/protocol revision, SDK changelog scan, reference servers, contract diff, and rollout sequence.
3. `meteoswiss-mcp: add chatgpt fetch/search compat regression tests` — new `test/integration/chatgpt-compat.test.ts` (9 tests) + a normalised tool-manifest Jest snapshot. Test-only commit; intentionally fails on its own to prove the regression exists.
4. `meteoswiss-mcp: restore id/text fields for chatgpt deep research` — the source fix (4 files) + updated `test/integration/meteoswiss-fetch.test.ts`. New tests now pass.
5. `changeset: chatgpt fetch compat` — patch-level changeset.

## Back-compat

The `text` field is a new addition; `content` stays as a deprecated alias for one minor version (will be removed in 3.0). Top-level `url` is also new.

The `url` argument shape from v2.3.1 is **not** preserved as an alias — v2.3.1 was published 24 hours before this PR was opened, the operator (eins78) is the only deployment, and adding a `z.preprocess` shim would either pollute `tools/list` or hide the alias from the manifest. Pure rename is the minimal patch. See plan §6.2.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter meteoswiss-mcp run lint` — passes (TypeScript + ESLint).
- [x] `pnpm --filter meteoswiss-mcp run build` — passes.
- [x] New `chatgpt-compat.test.ts` (9 tests) — passes including snapshot.
- [x] Existing `meteoswiss-fetch.test.ts` updated for `id` shape — passes.
- [x] Existing `meteoswiss-search.test.ts` — passes (unchanged).
- [x] All other integration suites — pass except the known macOS port-mapping flake (unrelated, pre-existing on `main`, documented as `port-mapping.test.ts` failing in parallel Jest on macOS).
- [ ] Manual verification: connect ChatGPT custom MCP connector to a live deployment and trigger a Deep Research run. Out of CI scope (requires API key + cost).

author: jpers1
body:
### Motivation
- Implement a compact, production-usable CLI pipeline to transcribe meeting audio into a single consolidated diarized JSON and render that JSON to readable Markdown, following the project's specification. 
- Provide reliable local chunking with overlap, conservative deduplication, and a best-effort speaker bootstrap to keep uploads under the 25 MB limit and improve speaker consistency across chunks.

### Description
- Add `meeting2json.py`, a single-file CLI that validates `.m4a/.mp3/.wav` input, inspects audio with `ffprobe`, optionally normalizes to mono 16 kHz with `ffmpeg`, chunks with configurable `--chunk-minutes` and `--overlap-seconds`, calls the OpenAI transcription API via `OpenAI().audio.transcriptions.create(...)` using `model="gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize"`, `response_format="diarized_json"`, `language="sl"`, and `chunking_strategy="auto"`, implements best-effort speaker bootstrap (2–10s reference clips encoded as data URLs), merges/deduplicates chunk segments into a global timeline, and writes a clean consolidated JSON document. 
- Add `json2markdown.py`, a small CLI that reads the JSON produced by `meeting2json.py` and writes a readable Markdown transcript with metadata, timestamps, speaker labels, and an optional `--compact` mode that merges nearby consecutive segments by the same speaker. 
- Add `requirements.txt` with the official `openai` package and update `README.md` with prerequisites, install steps, usage examples, explanation of JSON/Markdown outputs, chunking/overlap rationale, speaker bootstrap notes, and troubleshooting guidance. 

### Testing
- Successfully checked Python syntax using `python -m py_compile meeting2json.py json2markdown.py` which passed. 
- Validated Markdown rendering using a generated sample JSON and `python json2markdown.py sample.json --output sample.md`, which wrote `sample.md` successfully. 
- Attempted to install dependencies with `pip install -r requirements.txt` but the installation failed due to outbound package index/proxy restrictions in the environment, so the `openai` package could not be installed here. 
- Attempted to run `python meeting2json.py --help` but it failed in this environment with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai'`, and `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` were also not available in the container, so a real end-to-end transcription smoke test could not be completed here.

body:
### 💡 What: 
- Moved `import re` from the `_extract_location_mentions` method to the module level.
- Pre-compiled the location matching regular expressions (`location_patterns`) using `re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE)` in the `ATLASAgent.__init__` method and cached them as `self._location_regexes`.
- Updated `_extract_location_mentions` to use the pre-compiled `pattern.findall(text)` directly.
- Added a journal entry to `.jules/bolt.md` documenting the learning.

### 🎯 Why: 
The `_extract_location_mentions` method is a text processing loop called frequently to analyze social media posts. Calling `import` inline inside this function adds unnecessary function call and module lookup overhead. Additionally, repeatedly evaluating and compiling regex patterns via `re.findall(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE)` on every call degraded performance unnecessarily.

### 📊 Impact: 
Reduces per-call overhead for `_extract_location_mentions` significantly by eliminating dynamic module import lookups and regex recompilation. Expected to yield a noticeable improvement in high-volume text processing workloads.

### 🔬 Measurement: 
- The module syntax is verified: `python3 -m py_compile obsidian-council/agents/geolocation/atlas.py`.
- The core framework tests pass successfully: `pytest obsidian-council/`.
- To measure performance impact, compare execution times of a batch of text processing using the old vs new `_extract_location_mentions` method; the new one will show consistent execution times avoiding the initial compilation hit.

## Summary
Refactored the home feed from a hardcoded 3-day layout to a dynamic, bidirectional infinite scroll system that loads day-sections on demand while maintaining a fixed window of visible content.

## Key Changes

- **Dynamic day collection**: Changed from collecting only the first 3 days to collecting all unique days with published content, enabling unlimited scrolling capability
- **Bidirectional scroll logic**: Implemented a new infinite scroll system in `default.html` that:
  - Maintains a sliding window of 7 visible day-sections (configurable via `WINDOW_SIZE`)
  - Loads older days when scrolling down (bottom sentinel)
  - Restores previously hidden days when scrolling back up (top sentinel)
  - Automatically hides days outside the window to manage DOM size
- **Template refactoring**: Consolidated the three separate day-section blocks into a single loop that dynamically renders all days with appropriate styling (featured article on day 0, grid layout on subsequent days)
- **CSS additions**: Added `.day-hidden` class to hide off-window sections without removing them from DOM
- **Loader UI**: Added top and bottom loader indicators that activate during scroll-triggered content loads

## Implementation Details

- Uses Intersection Observer API with 200-400px root margins for smooth, predictive loading
- Maintains scroll position when hiding/showing sections to prevent jarring jumps
- Applies reveal animations to newly loaded sections for visual continuity
- Newsletter banner positioned between day 0 and day 1 (conditional on day index)
- Gracefully degrades if no day-sections exist or if all days fit in initial window
- Preserves existing autoload batch logic for topic/archive pages

author: yovanoc
body:
## Summary

When a Container is declared with `external: ["impit", "tough-cookie"]`, the bundler correctly excludes these packages from the bundle. However, the generated Dockerfile only copies `index.mjs` into the image — it does **NOT** run `bun add` to install the external packages.

At container runtime (Firecracker VM), Bun encounters bare `import` statements for the external packages and fails to resolve the module because it isn't in `node_modules`. The container process **crashes before any Effect code runs**, producing zero stdout and causing `port.fetch()` to hang indefinitely with `outcome: canceled`.

## Fix

`buildFinalDockerfile` now accepts an `external: string[]` parameter. When external packages exist and runtime is "bun", it injects a `RUN bun add <deps>` step between `WORKDIR` and `COPY`. Both call sites (`computeImageHash` and `buildAndPushImage`) now pass `props.external`.

### Example generated Dockerfile

```dockerfile
FROM oven/bun:1

WORKDIR /app
RUN bun add impit tough-cookie

COPY index.mjs /app/index.mjs
ENTRYPOINT ["bun", "/app/index.mjs"]
```

## Verification

Deployed to Cloudflare Workers with a DeviceContainer (Bun runtime). After the fix:
- Container image contains `node_modules/impit/` and `node_modules/tough-cookie/`
- `package.json` and `bun.lock` are generated in the image
- Container process no longer crashes on startup (no zero-stdout issue)
- `port.fetch()` connects successfully

## Summary

Completes the Lebowitz 4-point J=0 slice with an explicit closed form.

At J=0 with pairwise distinct sites, \`correlation_J_zero\` gives
\`⟨σ^A⟩ = t^|A|\` with t = tanh(β·h). For the Lebowitz 4-point
expression, cardinalities are 4, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, giving

  U₄ = t⁴ - t² · t² - t² · t² - t² · t² = -2·t⁴.

This is not a vanishing slice (unlike PR #214), but provides the
explicit Lebowitz bound at J=0. Adds both finite and ∞-vol forms.

- \`truncated4_J_zero_of_pairwise_distinct\` (finite, \`Inequalities/GHS.lean\`)
- \`truncated4Infinite_J_zero_of_pairwise_distinct\` (∞-vol, \`AmbientLattice.lean\`, ferromagnetic)

body:
## Summary
Completely rewrote the MAP Weekly Reports tab to eliminate the GitHub subscription setup flow and instead allow users to select from any existing document store with frontend-based file filtering. Configuration is now persisted in sessionStorage rather than creating dedicated stores.

## Key Changes

### Frontend (prd-admin)
- **Removed**: GitHub subscription creation flow, manual sync triggers, and store deletion
- **Added**: 
  - Store selection dropdown with live preview of available document stores
  - Prefix-based file name filtering (frontend-only, no backend query)
  - Auto-selection of newest report (sorted by git commit time, fallback to sync time)
  - "NEW" badge for files modified this week
  - Configuration persistence in sessionStorage (`weekly-reports-tab-config`)
  - Separate loading states for stores, entries, and content
  - Settings panel for reconfiguring store/prefix selection
  - Markdown content rendering with proper error handling

- **UI Improvements**:
  - Left sidebar with scrollable file list (300px fixed width)
  - Right panel for markdown content display
  - Top bar showing current store name, active filter, and file count
  - Responsive layout with independent scrolling for list and content

### Backend (prd-api)
- **Enhanced GitHub sync**: Added backfill of `github_last_commit_at` metadata for historical entries that lack this field
  - When syncing unchanged files (SHA match), now checks if entry is missing `github_last_commit_at`
  - Fetches latest commit date from GitHub API and updates metadata without re-pulling content
  - Updates `UpdatedAt` timestamp to reflect the backfill operation

### Documentation
- **Standardized all doc/ file H1 titles** to follow new naming convention: `# <App/Topic> [Subtitle] · <Type Suffix>`
- Type suffixes now consistently applied: ` · 规格` (spec), ` · 设计` (design), ` · 计划` (plan), ` · 规则` (rule), ` · 指南` (guide), ` · 周报` (weekly report), ` · 报告` (report)
- Updated `doc/rule.doc-naming.md` with detailed H1 title format specification and type suffix mapping table
- Added rule to CLAUDE.md requiring all doc/ files use one of the 6 mandatory prefixes

## Implementation Details

- **Time resolution**: Uses `metadata.github_last_commit_at` (from GitHub commits API) → `lastChangedAt` → `updatedAt` → `createdAt` for sorting
- **Week detection**: Calculates Monday 00:00:00 of current week in local timezone to identify "NEW" entries
- **Cleanup**: Removed unused imports (useCallback, DocBrowser, Github icon, etc.)
- **Error handling**: Graceful fallbacks for missing content, failed loads, and empty stores

body:
## Summary

Adds three new tools under `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/deepkeep_tool/` that let CrewAI agents interact with the [DeepKeep](https://deepkeep.ai) AI Firewall API.

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `DeepKeepCheckInputTool` | Check a user prompt against a firewall's safety guardrails |
| `DeepKeepCreateConversationTool` | Open a new tracked conversation in a firewall |
| `DeepKeepMakeApiCallTool` | Escape-hatch for any authenticated DeepKeep API request |

## Motivation

DeepKeep is an AI firewall platform that enforces guardrails (prompt injection, PII leakage, jailbreaks, policy violations, etc.) on LLM inputs and outputs in real time. These tools allow any CrewAI agent to screen user messages before passing them to an LLM, creating an auditable, policy-enforced layer around autonomous agent workflows.

## Usage

```python
from crewai_tools import DeepKeepCheckInputTool, DeepKeepCreateConversationTool

create_conversation = DeepKeepCreateConversationTool(subdomain="acme", api_key="dk_...")
check_input = DeepKeepCheckInputTool(subdomain="acme", api_key="dk_...")

agent = Agent(
    role="AI Security Guard",
    tools=[create_conversation, check_input],
    ...
)
```
## Checklist

- [x] Follows existing tool conventions (`BaseTool`, `args_schema`, `model_validator`)
- [x] Strict type annotations (mypy-compatible)
- [x] No new mandatory dependencies (uses `requests`, already in the project)
- [x] `example.py` included
- [x] `__init__.py` exports all three tools

author: madmax983
body:
Optimize apply_chromatic_aberration with Rayon parallel iterators and bitwise masking.

This significantly improves the performance of the `apply_chromatic_aberration` filter by replacing individual channel bitwise shifts and extracts with direct bitwise masks where possible, saving multiple operations per pixel. It also implements Rayon parallelization across image rows in both the scalar and AVX2 SIMD paths for faster execution on multi-core systems when the `parallel` feature is enabled. `par_chunks_exact_mut().for_each_init` is used to prevent the scratch row buffer from allocating per row, maintaining high-throughput.

Benchmark results show improvement from ~4.6ms down to ~330us on 1080p target.

author: yihuang-amd
body:
Two classes of submit failures were effectively silent until now:

1. JOB_NAME length overflow.  Slurm's --output path is %j-${JOB_NAME}.log; when it exceeds ext4's 255-byte per-path-segment limit, slurmd cannot open the log file and kills the job in prolog ("RaisedSignal:53"), leaving no writable log.  The caller sees "Submitted batch job X" and nothing else.  Root cause in our case: long passthrough arg lists encode into EXP_TAG, which encodes into JOB_NAME.

2. Partition-level prolog breakage.  A misconfigured or transiently broken Slurm prolog can kill every job scheduled onto it within seconds, also leaving no log.  Same symptom as #1.

Fixes:

- utils/parse_job_args.sh: reject at submit time when the worst-case --output basename (<7-digit id>-${JOB_NAME}.log) would exceed 255 bytes.  Zero latency, deterministic, shared automatically across submit.sh, k8s_submit.sh, and run_setup.sh (run_local.sh / in_container_run.sh) since all three source parse_job_args.sh.

- submit.sh: after sbatch returns, poll 'squeue -t all' at t+3s and treat FAILED / CANCELLED / NODE_FAIL / BOOT_FAIL / TIMEOUT / OUT_OF_MEMORY / DEADLINE as an immediate failure.  Mirrors the existing sbatch-failure path and cleans up the orphan artifact and job dir.  PENDING jobs pass through; delayed failures on queued jobs still require caller-side polling.

- skills/job-log-triage/SKILL.md: document the prolog-kill-no-log signature and the right entry point for triage (squeue -t all / sacct, not the log file), since the orphan outputs/ dir is cleaned up on detection.

Verified against job 13011 (auto-rejected by the length check) and jobs 13006-13010 (would now be caught and cleaned up by the t+3s poll instead of silently succeeding at the submitter level).

author: s243a
body:
## Summary

  This PR introduces `CachedResultRows` as an internal cached-row container seam in the C# query runtime.

  It keeps the public runtime surface unchanged while moving selected cache/materialization paths behind a container abstraction:

  - Adds `CachedResultRows` with an `AsObjectRows()` compatibility view for existing `IReadOnlyList<object[]>` consumers.
  - Migrates unseeded transitive-closure cache storage to `CachedResultRows`.
  - Routes counted path-aware depth replay through `CachedResultRows`, preserving final `object[]` row output while avoiding the previous intermediate target-value and boxed-depth arrays.
  - Migrates seeded transitive-closure source/target caches, including grouped variants, to store `CachedResultRows`.
  - Updates the row-container abstraction survey with the prototype status and next-step guidance.

  ## Rationale

  The existing runtime stores cached query results directly as `IReadOnlyList<object[]>`, which makes it hard to experiment with more compact or specialized internal result layouts.

  This PR creates a narrow compatibility boundary:

  - Existing execution APIs still return `IEnumerable<object[]>`.
  - Existing cache-hit behavior still exposes `IReadOnlyList<object[]>` where needed.
  - Row order and equality behavior are preserved.
  - Future cache-specific layouts can be introduced behind `CachedResultRows` without forcing a broad runtime rewrite.

  ## Validation

author: santiagomd11
body:
Extract desktop automation code (`computer_use/`) into its own repository: **[MONTBRAIN/vadgr-computer-use](https://github.com/MONTBRAIN/vadgr-computer-use)**. Full history preserved (`git filter-repo --path computer_use/`, 51 commits). Then converge this repo onto the published `vadgr-computer-use==0.1.0` PyPI package and drop every piece of daemon / cache / provider-key plumbing that the package now owns itself.

This repo now focuses on the core platform: **forge** + **api** + **cli** + **registry** + **gateway** + **frontend**. Desktop automation is consumed as an optional PyPI package.

## Commits in this PR

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `bedca1d` | Extract `computer_use/` into vadgr-computer-use repo |
| `21cebaa` | Drop nonexistent `[vision]` extra from CU package spec |
| `bca1afb` | Drop duplicate daemon plumbing now owned by vadgr-cua |
| `c747cc0` | Drop unused anthropic/openai api_key settings |
| `bcb8715` | Clarify CLI auth is the primary path (containerization doc) |

## Before / after shape

**Before:** `api/services/computer_use_setup.py` (~540 lines) re-implemented every piece of the daemon lifecycle locally: `_is_wsl2`, `_get_bridge_client`, `_probe_daemon`, `_get_windows_userprofile`, `_find_windows_python`, `_check_win_python_module`, `_DAEMON_DEPS`, `_ensure_daemon_deps`, `_deploy_and_launch_daemon`, `_start_daemon`, `_stop_daemon`, plus a `cache_enabled` parameter threaded through every function to drive the `AGENT_FORGE_CACHE_ENABLED` env var.

**After:** ~244 lines. The Windows-side bridge daemon is owned by the published `vadgr-computer-use` package (self-healing, file-locked, version-handshaked). This repo delegates lifecycle to the `vadgr-cua` console script:

- `_install_daemon()` → shells out to `vadgr-cua install-daemon`
- `_stop_daemon()` → shells out to `vadgr-cua stop-daemon`
- `_doctor_status()` → shells out to `vadgr-cua doctor`, parses JSON, surfaces `running` / `stopped` / `None`

The muscle-memory cache is gone in v0.1.0 of the package, so `AGENT_FORGE_CACHE_ENABLED` was a dead env var — removed from route body, frontend hook, Settings.tsx toggle, and tests.

## MCP config shape

All three provider configs (`.mcp.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`) now point at the venv console script directly:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "vadgr-computer-use": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "<cu_venv>/bin/vadgr-cua",
      "args": ["--transport", "stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

No `cwd`, no `PYTHONPATH`, no `AGENT_FORGE_DEBUG` env var. The shebang on the console script carries the venv Python so `import computer_use.mcp_server` resolves cleanly into site-packages.

## Auth model clarified

Vadgr invokes providers through their CLI binaries (`claude`, `codex`, `gemini`) configured in `providers.yaml`. The CLIs handle their own auth via `claude login` / `codex login` / `gemini auth`. Removed the declared-but-never-read `anthropic_api_key` / `openai_api_key` settings from `api/config.py` so they stop implying a raw-key requirement that does not exist. Containerization doc reworded to lead with the CLI-login path.

## Forge docs scrub

The package dropped `find_element` and the accessibility/vision fallback (0/5 success in real QA logs, 100s+ hangs). This PR updates the forge docs to match:

- `README.md`: desktop automation blurb no longer claims accessibility APIs + vision fallback

author: andrelake
body:
## Problem

The logout button was silently failing in production due to two independent bugs in `handleSignOut`.

## Root Causes

**1. Unreliable guest detection**
The check `!profile?.email` was used to identify guest users (no Supabase session). This incorrectly classifies authenticated users who signed in via an OAuth provider without email scope — they'd never call `supabase.auth.signOut()`, leaving an active session on Supabase.

**2. Logout depended exclusively on the `SIGNED_OUT` event listener**
After a successful `signOut()`, the code did nothing locally — it waited for the `SIGNED_OUT` event in `_layout.tsx` to trigger `clearUser()` + navigation. In production, this event can be missed due to race conditions (listener registered after the event fires, or subscription briefly unregistered during re-renders).

## Fix

- **Guest check**: replaced `!profile?.email` with `supabase.auth.getSession()` — detects an active Supabase session directly, independent of profile data
- **Deterministic logout**: wrapped `signOut()` in `try/finally` so `clearUser()` + `router.replace('/(auth)/login')` always runs regardless of network success or failure — no longer relies solely on the event listener

The `SIGNED_OUT` listener in `_layout.tsx` is preserved to handle external logouts (server-side session revocation, other devices).

## Files Changed

- `apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/user-area.tsx`

### Motivation
- The original `generator.ts` grew large and mixed search, shopping, compare, email, operator logic and response formatting in one file, making maintenance and testing difficult. 
- The goal is to split responsibilities into focused, well-typed modules while preserving behavior and the existing public API (`generateFinalAnswer` / `generateFinalAnswerStream`).

### Description
- Introduces `src/agent/vNext/generator-types.ts` to centralize shared types, normalization helpers, tool summarization, confidence estimation, LLM JSON extraction, fallback builders, and metadata construction. 
- Adds `src/agent/vNext/generator-response-mode.ts` to decide response type (`search | shopping | compare | email | operator | plain`) based on route intent, tool results, query signals, structured-data cues, and confidence. 
- Adds focused builders: `generator-search.ts`, `generator-shopping.ts`, `generator-compare.ts`, `generator-email.ts`, and `generator-operator.ts` that each produce domain-specific `Partial<StructuredPayloadSchema>` payloads (sources/cards/compare rows/emails/events/operator actions).

author: kninetimmy
body:
## Summary
Stage 2 of the X9 encrypted-config lifecycle plan (per locked plan in PR #142). Introduces the shared `IConfigStore`/`ConfigStore` pair that will serve as the single chokepoint for portable-config persistence in Stages 3-4. No Runner or Prep wiring yet — scope-limited by design.

- Adds `UnlockMaterial` record (cached PBKDF2 output) so unlocked sessions re-encrypt saves without re-deriving the key.
- Extends `SsdEncryption` with three symmetric-crypto members: `SaveEncryptedConfigAsync` (two-file atomic commit + `File.Replace` rollback), an in-memory `EnableConfigEncryptionAsync` overload, and `TryUnlockPortableConfigWithMaterial` (zeros key on every failure path).
- `ConfigStore` serializes saves with `SemaphoreSlim`, zeros the cached key on `LockSession`/replace, and carries forward the `NetworkMode + RequireApiKey` fail-closed guard.

## Why
The Stage 1 plan (#142) called for a single chokepoint to eliminate scattered `PortableConfig.SaveAsync` calls and hold the derived key in memory across a session. That lets Stage 3 (Runner) and Stage 4 (Prep) drop their per-save password prompts while guaranteeing the fail-closed guard and save serialization run on every write path. Landing Stage 2 on its own keeps the diff reviewable and leaves Runner/Prep untouched until they're explicitly re-wired.

## Security notes
- AES-256-GCM with fresh 12-byte nonce per save; PBKDF2-SHA256 @ 210k iters; 16-byte salt/tag (matches existing `SsdEncryption` parameters).
- Two-file atomic commit: stage `.tmp` pair, `File.Replace` blob (with `.bak`), `File.Replace` state (with `.bak`). On state failure the blob is restored via `File.Replace` — a crash mid-rollback cannot leave stale-state + no-blob.
- Derived keys are zeroed with `CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory` on `LockSession`, on `UnlockSession` when replacing prior material, and on every decrypt failure branch in `TryUnlockPortableConfigWithMaterial`.

## Test plan

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Enables users to embed TrueType (and TrueType-outline OpenType) fonts directly inside the generated PDF file, lifting the previous restriction of only being able to use the 14 built-in AFM fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier, etc.).

## Changes

### New: `TrueType.fs` — binary font metrics parser
A minimal, dependency-free parser for TrueType/OpenType font files. It reads the binary font tables needed to produce a valid PDF font embedding:

| Table | Data extracted |
|-------|----------------|
| `head` | `unitsPerEm`, bounding box |
| `hhea` | ascent, descent, `numberOfHMetrics` |
| `OS/2` | cap height, italic/bold flags → PDF `Flags` bitfield, weight → `StemV` estimate |
| `post` | italic angle (16.16 fixed-point → float) |
| `name` | PostScript name (nameID 6, Windows Unicode or Mac Roman) |
| `cmap` | format-4 Unicode→glyph mapping for char codes 0–255 |
| `hmtx` | per-glyph advance widths |

All widths are normalised to 1/1000 of a point (the unit used in PDF font dictionaries). The parser returns safe defaults when a table is missing or malformed so it never prevents PDF generation.

### Updated: `Layout.fs`

- New `EmbeddedFont` record carrying the raw font bytes and parsed `TrueType.FontMetrics`.
- Convenience constructors: `EmbeddedFont.fromFile`, `EmbeddedFont.fromBytes`, `EmbeddedFont.fromStream`.
- New `EmbeddedFontResource of EmbeddedFont` case on the existing `Resource` union — a page simply adds one entry to its `Resources` map, exactly like a standard `FontResource`.
- `Resource.resourceDictionary` updated to accept a resolved `Map<string, int>` of embedded-font object numbers and emit `PReference` entries for them.
- `PdfFile.build` updated to:
  - Collect unique embedded fonts across all pages.
  - Emit three indirect objects per unique embedded font: a **Font** dictionary (with `Widths` array for codes 32–255, `WinAnsiEncoding`, `FontDescriptor` reference), a **FontDescriptor** dictionary, and a **FontFile2** stream with the raw font bytes.
  - Adjust page object numbering to follow the font objects.

### Updated: `Pdf.fs`

- Added `PReal of float` to `PdfObject` for real-number values (required by the PDF spec for `ItalicAngle` and other fields). Written with invariant-culture formatting.
- **Bug fix**: `PStream` now writes the dictionary stored in its `d` parameter instead of a hardcoded `<< /Length N >>`. This is required to emit `Length1` for TrueType font streams and makes `PStream` correct in general.

### Updated: `FsPdf.fsproj`

`TrueType.fs` added to the compile order (before `Layout.fs`).

### Updated: `Tests.fs`

Two new tests:
- `TrueType metrics from file` — verifies the parser produces sensible values (non-empty PS name, 256-entry widths array, positive ascent, non-positive descent).
- `Embedded font PDF` — writes a single-page PDF with a font embedded from a `.ttf` file and asserts the file is produced and contains the PDF header. Both tests gracefully skip when the font file is not present.

## Usage

```fsharp
open FsPdf
open FsPdf.Layout

let embeddedFont = EmbeddedFont.fromFile "/path/to/MyFont.ttf"

let pdf =
    {
        Catalog =
            {
                PageLayout = SinglePage
                DefaultMedia = Letter
                Pages =
                    [
                        {
                            Resources =
                                Map.empty
                                |> Map.add "F1" (EmbeddedFontResource embeddedFont)
                            Contents =
                                [
                                    BeginText
                                    FontSize ("F1", 24.)
                                    NextLineTranslate (72, 700)
                                    ShowText "Hello from a custom font!"
                                    EndText
                                ]
                            MediaSize = Some Letter
                        }
                    ]
            }
        Info = None
    }

use stream = System.IO.File.OpenWrite "output.pdf"
PdfObject.writePdf stream (pdf |> PdfFile.build)
```

body:
## Summary

Adds **SemgrepProvider** to bring real multi-language SAST coverage to RepoSentinel. Before this PR the only true code analyzer was `PythonAnalyzer`, which made the project effectively Python-only. After this PR the orchestrator runs Semgrep with 6 community rule packs (security-audit, secrets, python, javascript, typescript, java) on every scan.

## Why

The project goal is to scan public GitHub repos for vulnerabilities across multiple languages, but the existing `ExternalScannerStub` always returned an empty list, so any non-Python repo produced almost no findings. Integrating Semgrep closes that gap with ~1000+ community rules and proper CWE/OWASP metadata, while keeping the pipeline backward compatible.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `app/providers/semgrep_provider.py` | **New** — ~220 lines. CLI wrapper + JSON-to-Finding mapper + fail-safe fallback. |
| `app/main.py` | Wire `SemgrepProvider` into the orchestrator behind a small factory; add `REPOSENTINEL_DISABLE_SEMGREP` opt-out env var. |
| `tests/test_semgrep_provider.py` | **New** — 23 unit tests (all mock the CLI, so they run anywhere). |
| `requirements.txt` | Add `semgrep>=1.50.0,<2.0.0` (with comment marking it optional). |
| `README.md` | New "Semgrep Integration" section with install/opt-out docs and measured impact table. |

## Backward compatibility

- `ExternalScannerStub` is **kept** as a fallback path; Semgrep does not replace it, it sits next to it.
- If `semgrep` is not installed, `SemgrepProvider` short-circuits and returns `[]` — the rest of the scan still runs end-to-end.
- Set `REPOSENTINEL_DISABLE_SEMGREP=1` to force the stub at runtime (useful for fast local iteration or CI workers without internet).

## How to test

```bash
# 1. Unit tests (no semgrep needed)
python -m unittest discover -s tests
# Expected: Ran 26 tests in ~0.02s, OK

# 2. End-to-end (requires `pip install semgrep`)
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
# Then submit any GitHub URL via the UI at http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

## Measured impact

| Repository | Language | Before | After | New high-impact issues caught |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| [we45/Vulnerable-Flask-App](https://github.com/we45/Vulnerable-Flask-App) | Python | 7 | **18** | SQL injection (line 261), `yaml.load` deserialization (line 329), MD5-as-password (line 141), 2 SSTI patterns, HTML-template XSS |
| [OWASP/NodeGoat](https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat) | JavaScript | **0 JS** | **17 JS** | 3× `eval(req.body.*)` in `contributions.js`, open redirect, 6× Express session misconfig, leaked RSA private key in `artifacts/cert/server.key`, bcrypt hash hardcodes |

<details>
<summary>Screenshots (drag-and-drop here)</summary>

- Vulnerable-Flask-App summary card (18 findings, 9 high / 9 medium)
- NodeGoat summary card (21 findings, 13 high / 8 medium)
- NodeGoat finding list showing `javascript`, `html-templates`, `secrets` language tags coexisting

</details>

## Languages now covered

- **Deep, language-specific rules**: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java
- **Cross-language security audit**: Go, Ruby, PHP, C#, Kotlin, Scala, Rust, C/C++, Bash, Dockerfile, etc. (via `p/security-audit`)
- **Cross-file secret detection**: any file type, including `.key`/`.pem`/`.env`
- **HTML template XSS**: Flask / Django / Mustache templates (via `p/security-audit`)

author: copilot
body:
Gameplay sessions could start without the graphics quality system initialized, causing rendering/audio behavior in the play area to degrade (missing visual fidelity controls, static-looking world behavior, and incorrect music state transitions). The issue was an initialization gap, not per-system rendering logic.

- **Root cause**
  - `QualityManager` existed in code paths but was not registered as a Godot autoload, so global quality state was never guaranteed at runtime.

- **Initialization fix**
  - Registered `QualityManager` in `project.godot` autoloads:
    - `QualityManager="*res://src/Systems/Graphics/QualityManager.cs"`

- **Boot-time guardrail**
  - Updated `BootLoader` autoload validation to include `/root/QualityManager` alongside core singletons (`GameManager`, `EventBus`) so startup fails fast if required global systems are misconfigured.

- **Code snippet**
  ```ini
  [autoload]
  GameManager="*res://src/Core/GameManager.cs"
  EventBus="*res://src/Core/EventBus.cs"
  AudioManager="*res://src/Systems/Audio/AudioManager.cs"
  LocalizationManager="*res://src/Systems/Localization/LocalizationManager.cs"
  ```

## Summary
- Browser-native (pure ES modules, no deps) Bayesian VoI sample-size calculator, deployable to GitHub Pages with zero backend.
- Adapted from IDinsight's `HKI_sampling_calculations.R` — histogram prior on coverage, single endline survey, Normal-Normal Bayes update on a normal-approximated binomial likelihood, asymmetric two-budget payoff (`V_up` vs `V_down`), optimal N picked by largest grid point still clearing a target marginal-ROI hurdle (default 8x).
- See [`docs/method.md`](docs/method.md) for the algebra and [`docs/idinsight_method_notes.md`](docs/idinsight_method_notes.md) for the per-step mapping to the source R script.
- Out of scope for v1 (deliberate): cluster sampling, continuous outcomes, baseline+endline diff, auxiliary-data fusion, explicit CEA pipeline (collapsed into V_up / V_down).

Closes #15.

## Diagnostic (premier test live xAI)

10/10 appels API retournent 200 OK, mais crash au parsing :

```
unexpected error: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'keys'
```

Trois écarts entre hypothèses initiales et réponse effective :

| # | Hypothèse | Réalité |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `output_text` = `{"items":[...],"warnings":[...]}` | **Array JSON nu** `[{...}, {...}]` |
| 2 | tool calls de type `tool_call` / `tool_use` / `function_call` | Type réel **`custom_tool_call`** |
| 3 | `usage.tool_calls` existe | N'existe pas → fallback obligatoire |

Le `response_format: json_schema strict` qu'on envoie **n'est pas honoré** de façon garantie.

## Fixes

### `scripts/xai_client.py`

- `_parse_response` : wrappe list → `{items: list, warnings: []}` ; `warnings` setdefault ; non-list/non-dict lève `ValueError` (→ retry → `XAIInvalidResponse`)
- `_count_tool_calls_in_output` : ajoute `custom_tool_call` en tête des 4 types

### `tests/test_xai_client.py` (+2 tests)

- `test_200_bare_array_output_wraps_as_items`
- `test_200_primitive_output_raises_invalid`
- Test existant `tool_call_entries` mis à jour (inclut `custom_tool_call`, compte 4 au lieu de 3)

### `docs/xai-integration.md`

- Shape réelle documentée (plus "Hypothèse" — "Confirmée au premier appel live")
- Points TODO(live) #1 et #2 marqués ✅ résolus
- Nouveau point #5 à surveiller : shape des **items** retournés (pas juste top-level) — le LLM peut ignorer notre schema et renvoyer ses propres fields (`post_id`, `author`, `content` observés dans l'issue). Si ça arrive, il faudra un adaptateur dans `sourcing._to_item()` — pour l'instant, le fix ne couvre que le top-level.

- [x] `pytest -q` → **106/106 verts** en 1.8s (+2 vs 104)

## Métriques live observées (pour référence)

- ~0.04 $ pour 10 appels (soit ~0.004 $/appel — nettement moins cher qu'estimé)
- 6-10s par appel
- ~16-20K tokens input par call (gros — prompt ~8K + résultats tools ~8-12K)
- ~0.4-1.3K tokens output

## Prochaine étape

Re-tester live avec ce fix. Si nouveau crash sur shape items (`post_id` vs `title`), on ouvre un issue #16 et on ajoute un adaptateur dans `sourcing.py`.

## Summary
Adds photo attachments to the Coach chat. Ephemeral by design — image bytes are sent to Anthropic for the current turn only, never stored.

- **Camera/photo button** next to the composer, opens the device picker (camera or library on iOS).

If no caption is typed, the prompt defaults to "What do you see in this photo?" so the coach can still respond.

author: nibsbin
body:
## Summary

This change consolidates all `Quill` creation paths into a single public entrypoint: `engine.quill(tree)`. The core constructors `Quill::from_tree` and `Quill::from_path` become crate-private, eliminating the dual-path confusion and removing the `Option<Backend>` as a meaningful runtime state outside the core library.

## Key Changes

- **Core library visibility**: `Quill::from_tree` and `Quill::from_path` changed from `pub` to `pub(crate)` in `crates/core/src/quill/load.rs`

- **Engine API rename**: `engine.load_quill(tree)` renamed to `engine.quill(tree)` in `crates/quillmark/src/orchestration/engine.rs` to follow Rust factory naming conventions and match the WASM surface

- **CLI binding migration**: All CLI commands (`render.rs`, `info.rs`, `schema.rs`, `validate.rs`) updated to construct `Quillmark::new()` and call `engine.quill_from_path(path)` instead of calling `Quill::from_path` directly

- **Typst backend tests**: Migrated `Quill::from_tree` calls in `crates/backends/typst/src/compile.rs` and `world.rs` to use the engine

- **Python binding**: `PyQuill::from_path` routed through the engine via `PyQuillmark`

- **WASM binding**: 
  - Deleted `Quill.fromTree` static factory (line 154)
  - Renamed `quillFromTree` → `quill` on the `Quillmark` class
  - Updated JS tests to use `engine.quill()` instead of `Quill.fromTree()`
  - Removed the `NoBackend` error test (behavior no longer reachable from JS)

- **Documentation**: Updated all references across docs, prose, and README files to reflect the new `engine.quill()` API and removed obsolete factory patterns

## Rationale

There is no legitimate external use case for a backend-less `Quill`. Every consumer either renders or inspects metadata—both work correctly with a backend attached. The dual-path API created confusion at every binding layer. Consolidating to one entrypoint simplifies the API surface and self-documents the intended usage pattern.

author: takeo7
body:
## Observación (20260419, máquina real)

Usuario ejecuta `./niwa update` para aplicar el FIX completion-truth-and-roundtrip (PR #97). El updater reporta success en todos los pasos:

```
✓ app:image
✓ app:restarted
✓ schema_version: 17 → 17
✓ /health OK
```

**Estado real tras el "update exitoso":**
- Container `niwa-app` sigue corriendo el image viejo (migraciones 001-017, timestamp del install inicial).
- Migración 018 existe en el repo del host pero nunca entró al container.
- `schema_version` sigue en 17 mientras el código nuevo espera 18.
- `docker logs niwa-app --since 1h | grep migration` devuelve vacío (el container no reinició).
- `systemctl restart niwa-executor.service` falló con exit 5 (scope mismatch: user vs system).

## Raíz

El update engine **afirma sin verificar**. `docker compose up -d` es idempotente y puede saltarse recreate; el updater trust-based asume que `compose up` = container nuevo. No hay ningún inspect de `docker inspect niwa-app` `.Image` pre/post, no hay polling de `schema_version` contra el max esperado, no hay lectura del scope systemd del install.

## Brief

`docs/plans/FIX-20260420-update-engine-reliability.md` (336 líneas, **L**).

Reemplaza "healthcheck triple" por **contrato verificable**: cada `✓` en la salida del updater se respalda con una inspección concreta. Si cualquier verificación falla → rollback completo (git reset + DB restore). Nuevo `.install-config.json` que el updater lee para saber scope de systemd y paths. Extiende `/health` con detalle para que el updater pueda verificar schema vía HTTP.

Cierra **Bug 37** (systemd scope hardcodeado), **Bug 38** (no verifica image del container), **Bug 39** (acepta schema unchanged como OK cuando hay migraciones pendientes).

Captura el incidente de 20260419 como test de regresión — fixture obligatoria.

## Restricciones duras del brief

- Cada `✓` del updater va respaldado por un step de inspección. Si no, no se imprime.
- Rollback hard (git + DB) en cualquier fallo de verificación. No warnings.
- `.install-config.json` como fuente única de verdad de paths y scope.
- Fuera de scope explícito: no migrar migraciones a volume, no auto-update on startup, no tocar UI del botón "Actualizar".
- Codex reviewer obligatorio.

## Estado de la instalación real actual

**Rota pero estable congelada**: no ejecutes tareas ni hagas otro update hasta que este FIX esté mergeado. Cuando entre, reinstalar limpio (instrucciones en la última sección del brief).

## Test plan

- [x] Brief sigue `docs/plans/_TEMPLATE.md`.
- [x] Cada bug (37, 38, 39) tiene verificación explícita post-fix.
- [x] Fuera de scope declarado.
- [x] Criterio de hecho verificable.

Solo merge del brief. Sin código productivo.

## Cómo se invoca

Sesión Claude Code nueva en el repo, mensaje literal:

> implementa el brief en `docs/plans/FIX-20260420-update-engine-reliability.md`

Orden de 14 pasos en la sección "Orden de implementación sugerido".

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent failures when manual timesheet evidence stored as images (PNG/JPEG) is later treated as PDFs by downstream flows (queue attach, single upload, invoice bundle merge). 
- Centralise byte-level detection + conversion so image→one-page-PDF materialisation is deterministic and re-usable across multiple handlers. 
- Lazily repair existing rows where `timesheets.manual_pdf_r2_key` points to non-PDF bytes while leaving QR/electronic flows and DB schema unchanged.

### Description

- Added a reusable helper stack to detect and materialise manual-timesheet artifacts: `detectPdfOrImageContentKind`, `buildSingleImagePdfBytes`, `ensureTimesheetEvidencePdfArtifact`, and `ensureManualTimesheetBytesArePdf`, plus a small import change to bring `degrees` from `pdf-lib` into `broker/src/index.js` (these perform byte-sniffing, rotation-normalisation, image→PDF conversion, deterministic R2 storage keys and return structured metadata). 
- Updated `handleManualTimesheetQueueAttach` to materialise `TIMESHEET` queue items via the helper before creating the canonical `timesheet_evidence` row and to patch `timesheets.manual_pdf_r2_key` to the materialised PDF key while preserving `manual_pdf_rotation_degrees`, and to include original vs materialised key info in audit payloads. 
- Updated `handleTimesheetEvidenceAdd` to materialise `TIMESHEET` uploads the same way, insert evidence using the materialised PDF key, patch `timesheets.manual_pdf_r2_key` to that PDF key, and keep the single-`TIMESHEET` evidence rule intact. 
- Hardened `ensureTimesheetPdf` to lazily repair existing `manual_pdf_r2_key` rows that point to images by converting and patching to the generated PDF key (while preserving signed-QR guards). 
- Hardened invoice bundle merge (`_renderInvoiceBundleAndStore`) by normalising manual timesheet evidence and manual-timesheet lists into PDF bytes before calling `PDFDocument.load(...)`, and returning a clear unsupported-document-type error for non-supported bytes instead of a generic `PDFDocument.load` failure. 
- Schema verification (objects/columns referenced and where verified): for `handleManualTimesheetQueueAttach` relied on `public.manual_timesheet_queue` (`id,status,timesheet_id,content_hash,r2_key,last_rotation_deg,meta_json,original_filename`), `public.timesheet_evidence` (`timesheet_id,kind,display_name,storage_key,created_at,created_by`), `public.timesheets` (`timesheet_id,manual_pdf_r2_key,manual_pdf_rotation_degrees,is_current`) and `public.timesheets_financials` (`locked_by_invoice_id,paid_at_utc,is_current`) as seen in the function's REST calls and nearby code in `broker/src/index.js` and in `supabase/repeatable/19012026_extras.sql` and `supabase/repeatable/28012026_invoice_queuing.sql`; for `handleTimesheetEvidenceAdd` relied on `public.timesheets` (including `manual_pdf_rotation_degrees`), `public.timesheet_evidence`, `public.timesheets_financials`, and view `public.v_timesheets_summary_base` as used in the existing select/insert calls in `broker/src/index.js` and verified against repeatable SQL; for `ensureTimesheetPdf` relied on `public.timesheets` columns `manual_pdf_r2_key,manual_pdf_rotation_degrees,qr_token,qr_status,qr_payload_json,qr_scanned_at,qr_signed_hash,qr_signed_at_utc,timesheet_id,is_current` as used in existing selects and repeatable SQL (`supabase/repeatable/28012026_invoice_queuing.sql`, `supabase/repeatable/19122025_add_ready_to_pay_to_timesheets_summary_views.sql`); no new tables, views, enums, or column names were introduced and only the existing timesheets select shapes were widened to include `manual_pdf_rotation_degrees` where needed (verified in the modified `broker/src/index.js`).

### Testing

- Performed a static syntax check with `node --check broker/src/index.js` which completed without errors. 
- No RPC/SQL/schema migrations were added or modified and existing runtime guards for signed QR/electronic flows were left intact (manual testing of flows should be performed in staging to validate end-to-end R2 interactions and invoice bundle render).

author: copilot
body:
## Résumé

Implémente le mode enfant pour Flash Guess :

1. **Flag `kidFriendly` sur les mots** — environ 100 mots des mots par défaut sont marqués comme adaptés aux -12 ans (personnages/lieux/films bien connus des enfants). Les mots importés/exportés conservent le flag.

2. **Joueur enfant** — un joueur peut être marqué "👦 Enfant" lors de l'ajout (case à cocher facultative dans la ligne de saisie). Le badge "👶 Enfant" apparaît dans la liste des joueurs.

3. **Mode enfant automatique** — dès qu'un enfant est dans la partie, le mode enfant s'active automatiquement (bouton grisé "ON (auto)"). Sans enfant, le mode peut être activé manuellement via le toggle dans les options de partie. Le réglage manuel est persisté en localStorage.

4. **Filtrage des mots** — en mode enfant, seuls les mots flaggés `kidFriendly` sont utilisés pour la partie.

5. **Pause lecture par mot** — quand l'orateur est un enfant :
   - Le timer ne démarre pas au début du tour
   - Un bouton **"👀 J'ai lu !"** apparaît sous la carte mot
   - Le timer démarre/reprend seulement après que l'enfant a appuyé dessus
   - Cette pause s'applique aussi aux mots suivants (le timer est mis en pause à chaque nouveau mot)

6. **Badge `👶 -12 ans`** sur la carte mot pendant le jeu (visible pour tous, indique que le mot est kid-friendly).

7. **Éditeur de mots** — bouton 👶 sur chaque mot pour toggler le flag `kidFriendly` manuellement.

## Fichiers modifiés

- `flash-guess/words.js` — flags `kidFriendly`, `loadWords` préserve le flag, `getShuffledWords(cats, kidsMode)`
- `flash-guess/index.html` — checkbox enfant, toggle kids mode, bouton "J'ai lu !", badge mot
- `flash-guess/main.js` — toute la logique décrite ci-dessus
- `flash-guess/style.css` — styles pour tous les nouveaux éléments

## Summary
- **Cache UA-Hub identity on `ua_user_mappings_pending`** (audit migration 5). Needs Match used to walk `unifi.Client.ListUsers` live on every render — 17 pages × 10s HTTP timeout at LEF's directory size, which caused the "Loading unmatched users…" hang. - **Nightly UA-Hub directory mirror** (audit migration 6, new `internal/unifimirror` package). A 24h ticker walks `ListAllUsersWithStatus` once and upserts every observed user into `ua_users`. Downstream code paths (Needs Match enrichment, recheck pre-filter, audit diagnostics) now read from the local mirror instead of paging upstream. `first_seen` is preserved across refreshes so the table doubles as a rough audit trail.
